 Procurement Coordinator I 
 The Procurement Coordinator I supports the success of all Toho stakeholders and is responsible for ensuring the efficient execution of procurement strategies while facilitating cost-effective, timely, and high-quality work to procure a variety of goods and services. Procurements may include analyzing quotes, sole source, piggybacks, and invitations for bids from inception to award. This role requires exceptional organizational and communication skills, collaborative teamwork skills, and a working knowledge and understanding of public procurement processes and industry best practices. Under direct supervision of a Senior Coordinator or Procurement Supervisor, the Procurement Coordinator I functions at entry-mid level to perform detailed work in the preparation, research, writing, evaluating and administration of bids and contracts. Work involves communication with vendors and departmental officials on purchasing problems and shipping, receiving, and invoicing problems and processes; and may include supporting p-card administration and oversight. Procurement Coordinators may manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.
 Procurement Coordinator II 
 The Procurement Coordinator II supports the success of all Toho Water Authority stakeholders and is responsible for ensuring the efficient execution of procurement strategies while facilitating cost-effective, timely, and high-quality work to procure a variety of goods and services. This role requires exceptional organizational and communication skills, collaborative teamwork skills, and a working knowledge and understanding of public procurement processes and industry best practices. Under direct supervision of a Senior Coordinator or Procurement Supervisor, the Procurement Coordinator II functions at journey professional level to perform complex procurement services, analysis, and implement process improvement solutions. The role supports Toho Water Authority staff with procuring a wide variety of commodities and services using various solicitation methods including ITB/RFP/RFQu and alternate delivery methods of construction such as Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) or other strategies. The work involves leading all phases of the procurement process, from bid preparation through granting of the award for procurement and contract management including extensions, amendments and facilitating vendor performance issues. The Procurement Coordinator II will also contribute to the team by sharing knowledge and implementing continuous improvement strategies and processes with peers. Work is performed according to Toho Water Authority procurement guidelines, State of Florida laws, and any applicable federal laws and regulations to include requirements of grant agreements.
 Senior Procurement Coordinator 
 The Senior Procurement Coordinator is a seasoned and highly skilled procurement professional relied upon as subject matter expert. The Senior Coordinator may function as an individual contributor or as a lead for a team of procurement coordinators, making assignments, providing guidance and ensuring the efficient execution of procurement strategies, and driving optimal cost savings while maintaining high-quality standards. This role requires analytical abilities, collaborative skills, and a deep understanding of procurement processes and industry best practices. The Senior Procurement Coordinator performs complex procurements, advice and guidance, delivery, and process improvement solutions to support Toho Water Authority. This is accomplished by developing and overseeing solicitation packages, contracts planning, analyzing proposals and determining contract strategies, evaluating bid and proposals for technical compliance, developing and monitoring project management timelines, and coordinating contract specifications. This position is responsible for handling the more complex procurements, problem solving and mediating of challenging or unexpected problems involving multiple stakeholders and departments. Senior Coordinators may be assigned to lead and/or represent Procurement as subject matter experts in cross functional continuous improvement project teams. The Senior Procurement Coordinator may be assigned day-to-day oversight of entry and mid-level coordinators to gain leadership and supervisory experience.
 Essential Functions
 Procurement Coordinator I 
 Performs routine procurement work according to generally accepted public procurement principles, best practices, established procedures, departmental guidelines, and regulatory requirements applicable to the work.
 Prepares, reviews, and processes standard documents, including solicitations, sole source, piggyback, including addenda, contract award and purchase orders, to include all contractual requirements and specifications.
 Schedules and facilitates pre-bid conferences, public formal bid and proposal openings; receives and analyzes bids and proposals received for conformance with specifications and other requirements.
 Uses e-procurement platform and financial management software to create or review and investigate any vendor records, department requisitions for purchase orders; includes contract set-up and spend summary maintenance; verifies items and prices and approves requisitions for purchase order issue.
 Monitors the status of assigned contracts with staff to prepare for timely renewals, contract extensions or new solicitations.
 Serves as primary contact with departments and outside agencies for the purpose of obtaining procurement information, purchase order authorization; as primary contact between departments and vendors/bidders for various commodities and services.
 Performs various administrative support duties, e.g. filing materials, copying documentation, entering data into computer system tasks and may include oversight for the procurement card (P-Card) program including issuing new cards, reports, training and monitoring for compliance.
 Maintains and updates procurement templates, SOP’s, Project tracker, cost savings reports, and other department tools as needed.
 Collaborates with staff advising on procurement procedures and managing solicitations and contracts.
 All other duties as assigned.
 Procurement Coordinator II 
 Fully master and perform all responsibilities and tasks outlined in the Procurement Coordinator I job description, demonstrating proficiency and independence in each area.
 Performs routine procurement work according to generally accepted public procurement principles, best practices, established procedures, departmental guidelines, and regulatory requirements applicable to the work.
 Prepares complex bid and proposal documents to include all contractual requirements and specifications received from the end user; utilizes the automated procurement system with good judgment and understanding of the commodity codes, to determine vendors from whom to solicit bids and proposals; assignments require critical thinking and independent judgment carried out within the guidelines of established policies and procedures.
 Monitors the status of assigned contracts with staff to prepare for timely renewals or new solicitations; analyzes requests for price increases and contract extensions; confers with departments regarding specifications and updates when preparing solicitations.
 Facilitates pre-bid and pre-proposal conferences; conducts public formal bid openings and proposal closings; receives and analyzes bid proposals received for conformance with specifications and other requirements; initiates the approval process and procurement award to the Board and Executive Staff from the department or evaluation committee’s recommendation.
 Conducts review and approval of purchase orders in a timely manner.
 Serves as primary contact to Toho’s departments and outside agencies for the purpose of obtaining purchase order authorization for commodities and services; as primary contact between Toho’s departments and vendors/bidders for various commodities and services.
 Reviews sole source procurement requests to determine if all legal requirements have been met; analyzes quotations received for small procurements.
 Uses e-procurement platform and financial management software for solicitations, purchase orders and contract management.
 For Professional Services solicitations under Florida 287.055, ensures that all projects and documents fall within the Consultant’s Competitive Negotiation Act (CCNA) guidelines.
 Collaborates with Toho Water Authority staff advising on procurement procedures and managing solicitations and contracts.
 Facilitates meetings with staff and vendors to address contract performance issues and creates documentation of results.
 Ensure Toho’s procurement practices fall within compliance guidelines for use of Federal and State Grants, Loans, etc.
 All other duties as assigned.
 Senior Procurement Coordinator 
 The role of the Senior Procurement Coordinator includes and may perform all the essential functions of the Procurement Coordinator positions.
 Implements effective procurement strategies and processes, optimizing cost savings, supplier management, and contract negotiation. Recommends, develops, and implements improved process methods and procedures.
 Monitors and analyzes procurement data, trends, and metrics to identify opportunities for process improvement and cost reduction.
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including finance, operations, and legal, to align procurement strategies with overall organizational goals.
 Provides a high level of service to internal and external customers while effectively resolving inquiries and challenges.
 Evaluate and select suppliers based on predefined criteria, negotiate contracts, and manage supplier relationships to ensure the highest quality and value for the organization.
 Conduct market research and stay updated on industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices to drive innovation and continuous improvement in procurement processes.
 Establish and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, both internal and external, to understand their needs, provide strategic advice, and influence decision-making processes.
 Ensure compliance with procurement regulations, standards, and requirements.
 Prepares and presents reports, performance metrics, and analysis to stakeholders, highlighting achievements, challenges, and recommendations.
 Manage multiple projects, facilitates award of contracts, ensures vendor insurance compliance and verification of contractor licenses.
 Collaborate with departments to establish goals and timelines for projects, pre-qualification and proposal evaluations.
 Solicit procurements by preparing documents, determining procurement strategies for projects including proposals and professional services, managing solicitation process, conducing pre-proposal and other public meetings; bid openings, contributing to contract negotiations, preparing correspondence, and processes materials/supplies as needed.
 Reviews and advice on scope of work for RFP's, participates in the evaluation and selection of vendors and contractors, and proactively monitors contract expirations. Supports departments in monitoring contract budgets.
 May function as a lead for entry and mid-level procurement staff providing training, delegation of assignments, and direct and review the work of others for compliance and development opportunities.
 Perform duties as assigned/necessary which are related, or logical in assignment to the position.
 All other duties as assigned.
 Minimum Qualifications
 Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain that required qualification would be: 
 Procurement Coordinator I A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
 Minimum of three years of relevant experience. Such as working in public sector procurement or contract administration; experience in Florida public sector procurement highly preferred. 
 Experience using financial software applications for contracts/purchase orders and an e-procurement platform (OpenGov/Bonfire/BidNet etc.) or similar platforms. 
 Must possess and maintain a valid state of Florida Class E Driver's License.
 Procurement Coordinator II 
 A minimum of 2-year college degree with a focus on Business Administration, Public Administration, Supply Chain Management or related field.
 Five years of experience working in a public sector procurement or contract administration.
 Experience using financial software applications for contracts/purchase orders and an e-procurement platform (OpenGov/Bonfire/BidNet Etc.)
 Must possess a professional purchasing-related certification such asCertified Professional Public Buyer (CPPB) or Certified Procurement Professional (NICP-CPP) or Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM) or Certified Purchasing Manager (C.P.M.) or other relevant credential approved by Toho Procurement Leadership. 
 Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
 Senior Procurement Coordinator 
 Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, or related field.
 Minimum of five years’ experience working in public sector procurement or contract administration.
 Proven experience in procurement analysis, contract negotiation, and supplier management. 
 Three years of supervisory experience or experience in leading project teams. 
 Experience using financial software applications for contracts/purchase orders and an e-procurement platform such as OpenGov/Bonfire/Bidnet, SAP, and Oracle. 
 Must possess a professional purchasing related certification such as Certified Professional Public Buyer (CPPB) Certified Professional Public Officer (CPPO); Certified Procurement Professional (CPP) or Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM) or Certified Purchasing Manager (C.P.M) or other credential approved by Toho Procurement Leadership. 
 Must possess and maintain a valid state of Florida Class E Driver's License.
 DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS: 
 Experience in Florida Public Sector procurement.
 Experience managing multiple projects and deadlines.
 Experience with Requests for Proposals and other types of procurements – GSA/Cooperative Contracts, etc. especially in the areas of IT, Finance, HR, and Legal. 
 Extensive knowledge of procurement processes, strategic sourcing, and supplier relationship management.
 P-Card program administration, management and implementation, and Certified Procurement Card Professional (CPCP) highly desirable.
 Experience in developing and presenting training to procurement and organization staff.
 KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES 
 Basic knowledge of public purchasing and general accounting principles and techniques.
 Skill in performing routine to moderately complex mathematical computations and tabulations accurately and efficiently; intermediate level business mathematics, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, percentages and decimals.
 Ability to perform in accordance with pre-established local, State, and Federal policies, procedures and regulatory requirements applicable to the work.
 Ability to effectively communicate both orally and in writing.
 Ability to utilize personal computers, standard office equipment and standard software applications, e.g., word processors, database software, spreadsheet applications.
 Ability to read and interpret technical and legal documents, operation and maintenance instructions, and policy and procedure manuals.
 Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with unit employees, employees in other departments, public/private sector contacts, vendors, and the general public.
 Ability to maintain effective records maintenance and file management systems.
 Ability to organize work, establish priorities, meet established deadlines, and follow up on assignments with a minimum direction.
 Skill in preparing complex correspondence, summaries and reports in a clear and concise manner; skill in business English, e.g., correspondence formats, spelling, punctuation and grammar.
 Ability to access, operate and maintain various software applications.
 Skill in reading, updating and maintaining various records and files; skill in complex administrative support functions, e.g., records maintenance, data analysis, reports processing, documentation proofing.
 Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to handle or feel and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to reach with hands and arms. jobs.title: Heavy Equipment Operator – Vacuum/Jetter
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Heavy Equipment Operator I $22.34 - $27.91
Heavy Equipment Operator II $25.60 - $34.08
Senior Heavy Equipment Operator $27.36 - $36.45

The purpose of this position is to operate and maintain specialized heavy equipment, primarily a combination vacuum/jetter truck, to support the cleaning, maintenance, and operation of Toho Water Authority's wastewater lift stations and collection system infrastructure.

The Heavy Equipment Operator is responsible for performing vacuum cleaning, high-pressure water jetting, and removal of sludge, grease, sediment, debris, and other accumulated materials from lift station wet wells, piping, and associated equipment. This position requires the safe operation, inspection, and routine maintenance of specialized equipment to ensure reliable performance and minimize operational disruptions.

When the vacuum/jetter truck is unavailable or operational needs require, the employee may be assigned to assist System Mechanics with lift station inspections, preventive maintenance, general maintenance activities, and other related duties.

The position may also be required to operate other heavy equipment and commercial vehicles as assigned.

Essential Functions

  1. Operates combination vacuum/jetter trucks to perform routine and scheduled cleaning of wastewater lift station wet wells, piping, and associated infrastructure.
  2. Performs high-pressure water jetting and vacuum operations to remove grease, sludge, sediment, debris, and other accumulated materials to maintain proper lift station operation.
  3. Operates vacuum pumps, high-pressure water pumps, hydraulic booms, hoses, nozzles, and associated equipment safely and efficiently.
  4. Coordinates cleaning activities with Lift Station Maintenance personnel to minimize disruptions to lift station operations and prevent sanitary sewer overflows.
  5. Performs daily pre-trip and post-trip inspections of assigned vehicles and equipment, including inspections required by the Department of Transportation (DOT).
  6. Performs routine preventive maintenance on assigned equipment, including lubrication, fluid level inspections, cleaning, and minor mechanical repairs within the employee's training and authorization.
  7. Identifies and reports equipment deficiencies, mechanical issues, unsafe conditions, and necessary repairs to the appropriate supervisor.
  8. Properly transports and disposes of collected wastewater, sludge, sediment, and debris at approved disposal locations in accordance with established procedures and applicable regulations.
  9. Assists System Mechanics with lift station inspections, preventive maintenance, equipment cleaning, and general maintenance activities when the vacuum/jetter truck is unavailable or as assigned.
  10. Assists with emergency response activities, including sanitary sewer overflows, lift station failures, sewer blockages, and other wastewater collection system emergencies.
  11. Operates additional heavy equipment and commercial vehicles, including dump trucks, roll-off trucks, front-end loaders, skid steers, excavators, and other equipment, as qualified and assigned.
  12. Establishes and maintains safe work areas, including traffic control, proper equipment positioning, and implementation of applicable safety procedures.
  13. Maintains accurate daily work records, equipment inspection reports, cleaning logs, disposal documentation, and other required paperwork or electronic records.
  14. Follows established safety procedures related to high-pressure water systems, vacuum equipment, wastewater exposure, confined spaces, and hazardous working conditions.
  15. Attends required safety meetings, training sessions, and equipment operation certification programs.
  16. Performs other related duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued by an approved GED Administrator.
  2. A minimum of three years of relevant work experience operating commercial vehicles, heavy equipment, or specialized utility maintenance equipment.
  3. Experience operating combination vacuum/jetter trucks or similar wastewater cleaning equipment.
  4. Any combination of education and experience demonstrating the candidate's ability to successfully perform the essential functions of this position may be considered.
  5. Must possess and maintain a valid, unrestricted State of Florida Class A Commercial Driver's License (CDL).
  6. Must possess or obtain a Tank Vehicle (N) Endorsement within the first six months of employment, subject to applicable vehicle operating requirements.
  7. Must possess the ability to safely operate specialized equipment, follow written and verbal instructions, and complete required operational documentation.
  8. Must be able to work outdoors under varying weather conditions and respond to emergency situations as required.

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, sit, use hands to operate tools and equipment, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, climb, reach, and twist.
The position requires frequent and repetitive climbing in and out of commercial vehicles, accessing equipment compartments, and mounting and dismounting equipment multiple times throughout the workday. Employees are required to repeatedly assemble, connect, disconnect, lift, carry, and maneuver vacuum tubes, suction hoses, high-pressure water hoses, and associated equipment during daily lift station cleaning operations.
The employee must be capable of maintaining balance and stable footing while working around open lift station wet wells, access hatches, uneven terrain, and wet or slippery surfaces. Duties require physical coordination, manual dexterity, and the ability to safely position and maneuver equipment near open wet wells while maintaining awareness of surrounding hazards.
The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 75 pounds. The position requires repetitive physical movements and sustained physical activity throughout the workday.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Work is primarily performed outdoors at wastewater lift stations and other utility facilities under varying environmental conditions, including extreme heat, cold, rain, humidity, and adverse weather conditions.
Environmental factors include rugged or uneven terrain, wet and slippery surfaces, noise, vibrations, traffic, darkness, bright sunlight, confined or congested work areas, and exposure to wastewater, human waste,  sludge, biological agents, chemicals, sewer gases, fumes, and unpleasant odors.
The position requires frequent work in close proximity to open lift station wet wells and access hatches, presenting potential fall hazards and exposure to hazardous atmospheres. Employees routinely operate around high-pressure water systems, vacuum equipment, moving vehicles, hydraulic equipment, and other operating machinery.
Employees are required to follow established safety procedures, utilize appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), and comply with applicable fall protection, hazardous atmosphere monitoring, and confined-space safety procedures.
Work may also involve indoor environments, including maintenance facilities and office areas. The employee may be required to work extended hours, weekends, holidays, or respond to emergency situations as operational needs require.

jobs.title: Customer Experience Supervisor I
jobs.description_html:
General Description

The Customer Experience Supervisor provides leadership, coaching, and development for Contact Center and Front Desk staff while managing performance and fostering an engaged workplace.

Partnering with the Customer Experience Manager and Customer Experience Project Supervisor, this position ensures staff have the training, feedback, skills, knowledge, and resources to meet operational and customer service goals.

Essential Functions

Employee Leadership and Development

  • Supervises, coaches, mentors, and develops Contact Center and Front Desk staff.
  • Sets performance expectations, evaluates results, provides feedback, and monitors employee goals.
  • Maintains development plans, supports career and succession planning, and recognizes employee contributions.

Performance Management

  • Develops scorecards and monitors quality, productivity, attendance, workload, and customer service performance.
  • Conducts call reviews and one-on-one meetings, providing counseling and corrective action as needed.
  • Addresses employee concerns and promotes accountability, professionalism, and continuous improvement.

Training and Workforce Readiness

  • Oversees onboarding, training, and cross-training for Contact Center and Front Desk staff.
  • Develops training based on operational needs and ensures staff knowledge of policies, procedures, systems, and service standards.
  • Tracks training progress and employee competency development.

Team Engagement and Communication

  • Facilitates team meetings, staff communications, and cross-department collaboration.
  • Promotes employee engagement, a positive workplace culture, and consistent service standards.
  • Supports organizational initiatives, change management, and team effectiveness.

Administrative Oversight

  • Oversees scheduling, payroll, timekeeping, staffing plans, and workforce adjustments.
  • Supports recruitment, selection, onboarding, workforce planning, and organizational development.
  • Serves as back up to the Customer Experience Project Supervisor and other staff to ensure continuity of daily operations, timely completion of tasks, and adherence to established schedules and procedures.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED issued by an approved GED Administrator. 
  • Minimum of five (5) years of experience in contact center operations, customer service, utility operations, billing, collections, accounts receivable, or a related field plus two (2) years of supervisory, lead, coaching, or team leadership experience preferred. 
  • Demonstrated experience in employee development, performance management, coaching, and training. 
  • Strong leadership, communication, conflict resolution, and interpersonal skills. 
  • Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: 
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 75 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.  Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Billing/Collections Supervisor
jobs.description_html:
General Description

The purpose of this position is to provide direct leadership, coaching, and development for Billing and Collections staff. This position is responsible for managing employee performance, fostering a positive and engaged work environment, and ensuring employees receive the training, feedback, and support necessary to succeed.

Essential Functions

Employee Leadership and Development

  • Supervises, coaches, and develops Billing and Collections staff by establishing performance expectations, goals, and accountability standards.
  • Evaluates and monitors employee performance through regular coaching, feedback, development plans, and training opportunities.
  • Supports employee growth through career development, succession planning, and recognition of achievements.

 

Performance Management

  • Monitors employee performance through scorecards, productivity, quality, attendance, and customer service metrics. 
  • Conducts regular coaching, counseling, corrective action, and one-on-one meetings to support performance and development. 
  • Resolves employee concerns and fosters a culture of accountability, professionalism, and continuous improvement.

 

Training and Workforce Readiness

  • Oversees onboarding and ongoing training for new and existing employees. 
  • Coordinates cross-training and team training initiatives to enhance workforce flexibility and capability. 
  • Tracks training progress and competency development while ensuring compliance with policies, procedures, and customer service standards.

 

Team Engagement and Communication

  • Facilitates team communication and builds collaborative relationships across teams and departments. 
  • Promotes employee engagement, development, and a positive workplace culture. 
  • Supports organizational initiatives, change management efforts, and overall team effectiveness.

 

Administrative Oversight

  • Oversees scheduling, payroll, and timekeeping activities. 
  • Maintains staffing plans and recommends workforce adjustments to support operational needs. 
  • Assists with recruitment, hiring, workforce planning, and organizational development initiatives.
  • Provides backup support to Project Supervisors or other staff to ensure continuity of daily operations, timely completion of tasks, and adherence to established schedules and procedures. 
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED issued by an approved GED Administrator.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of experience in utility billing, collections, customer service, accounts receivable, or a related field plus two (2) years of supervisory, lead, coaching, or team leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in employee development, performance management, coaching, and training.
  • Strong leadership, communication, conflict resolution, and interpersonal skills.
  • Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: 
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 75 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.  Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Business Process Specialist - All Levels
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Business Process Specialist I: $27.36 - $36.45 Hourly
Business Process Specialist II: $29.26 - $39.02 Hourly
Senior Business Process Specialist: $32.77 - $46.82 Hourly

The Business Process Specialist is responsible for analyzing, documenting, modeling, and improving business processes across the organization to enhance operational efficiency, service quality, and organizational effectiveness. This role works closely with the Business Transformation Manager to facilitate process discovery workshops, develop process models using BPMN standards, identify improvement opportunities, and support the implementation of process changes.

The Business Process Specialist will work closely with the business stakeholders to document and improve processes across the entire enterprise. He/ she will serve as a bridge between business units and technology teams, ensuring that business requirements, process documentation, and improvement initiatives are effectively aligned with organizational objectives. While the primary focus of the role is process management and continuous improvement, the position also supports technology-related initiatives by collaborating with IT teams, reviewing system impacts, and helping translate business needs into functional requirements as and when necessary.

The ideal candidate is passionate about understanding how work gets done and helping teams improve it. They are comfortable leading process modeling workshops, documenting workflows using BPMN standards, applying Lean Six Sigma techniques, and partnering with both business and technology teams to deliver sustainable process improvements. They can effectively facilitate conversations, challenge assumptions, and translate ideas into actionable process improvements.

Essential Functions

Business Process Management

  • Facilitate process discovery, process mapping, and process improvement workshops with stakeholders across the organization.
  • Document current-state and future-state business processes using BPMN (Business Process Model and Notation) standards.
  • Maintain and govern process documentation repositories to ensure consistency, accuracy, and accessibility.
  • Analyze workflows, procedures, and business operations to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, risks, and improvement opportunities.
  • Develop process maps, swim lane diagrams, value stream maps, and supporting documentation.
  • Assist business units in defining process performance measures and key performance indicators (KPIs).
  • Support the development and maintenance of process governance standards, methodologies, and best practices.

Continuous Improvement

  • Apply Lean, Six Sigma, and other continuous improvement methodologies to improve business performance.
  • Conduct root cause analyses and facilitate problem-solving sessions.
  • Recommend process improvements that reduce waste, improve customer experience, enhance compliance, and increase operational effectiveness.
  • Support implementation and change management activities associated with process improvement initiatives.
  • Monitor and measure the effectiveness of implemented process changes.

Business and Technology Collaboration

  • Collaborate with business and IT stakeholders to understand process and system dependencies.
  • Analyze how applications and technology solutions support business processes and identify alignment opportunities.
  • Participate in software implementation, workflow automation, and digital transformation initiatives as needed.
  • Support user acceptance testing (UAT), process validation, and solution adoption activities.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Build collaborative relationships with leaders, subject matter experts, and frontline employees.
  • Facilitate workshops, interviews, and cross-functional working sessions to elicit process knowledge and improvement opportunities.
  • Present findings, recommendations, and process models to stakeholders at various organizational levels.
  • Provide guidance and coaching on process management methodologies and standards (if needed)

Minimum Qualifications

  1. Bachelor’s degree in relevant field
  2. 1-3 years process mapping/analysis
  3. Awareness of flowcharts and swimlane diagrams
  4. Awareness of basic Lean and Six Sigma concepts
  5. Facilitate SME interviews to document process models
  6. Able to harvest requirements in documented process
  7. Process maps, SOPs, workflows
  8. Analyze workflows and KPIs
  9. General business operations

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: 
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 75 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.
 
WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.  Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Business Support Manager
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Review of applications will begin on September 28, 2026.  The position will remain open until a candidate is selected.

Salary: $83,845- $119,787

The Business Support Manager provides leadership and coordination across departmental training, quality assurance, workforce management, and business support functions for the Customer Service Department. This role ensures alignment with departmental goals, service standards, data integrity requirements, and continuous improvement initiatives while promoting operational effectiveness and service excellence.

Essential Functions

  • Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching, and performance management for staff supporting departmental training, quality assurance, workforce management, and business support functions.

  • Maintain a working knowledge of core responsibilities across assigned functions, including curriculum development, onboarding, scorecard management, quality reviews, survey tracking, forecasting, scheduling, data audits, user acceptance testing (UAT), technology support, and process documentation.

  • Ensure departmental training materials, procedures, and standard operating documentation are accurate, current, and consistently applied across the Customer Service Department.

  • Lead quality assurance programs, including scorecard development, quality standards, coaching trends, compliance monitoring, and identification of opportunities to enhance the customer experience.

  • Support workforce management initiatives that optimize staff resources by evaluating call volumes, staffing needs, schedules, schedule adherence, and resource allocation to meet service-level goals.

  • Oversee business systems support by identifying system issues, validating data integrity, coordinating user acceptance testing, and facilitating communication between business operations and Information Technology.

  • Analyze operational trends, performance metrics, audit results, and other data to identify opportunities and recommend improvements to training, processes, systems, staffing, and service delivery.

  • Collaborate with other Customer Service leaders to address operational gaps, improve consistency, strengthen cross-functional coordination, and enable teams to focus on day-to-day service excellence.

  • Communicate priorities, risks, project status, performance trends, and opportunities for improvement to the Director of Customer Service.

Minimum Qualifications

Any combination of education and experience that demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.

· Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Management, Communications, Information Systems, or a related field.

· Seven years of progressively responsible experience in customer service operations, business support, training, quality assurance, workforce management, business analysis, or a related operational support area, including at least three years of experience in a supervisory, lead, project management, or team coordination role that included providing guidance, setting priorities, coaching employees, or leading cross-functional initiatives.

· Demonstrated ability to analyze and interpret operational reports, quality results, staffing data, customer feedback, audit findings, and performance metrics to identify trends, recommend corrective actions, and support continuous improvement.

· Experience developing, reviewing, or maintaining procedures, training materials, scorecards, dashboards, workflows, or process documentation.

· Working knowledge of customer service technology, case management systems, reporting tools, call center platforms, billing systems, or other business applications used to support service delivery.

· Experience coordinating cross-functional work with operations, IT, training, quality, workforce management, or leadership teams.

· Strong leadership, communication, organization, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

· Experience in a utility, municipal, government, call center, or high-volume customer service environment.

· Experience supporting system implementations, user acceptance testing, data audits, reporting improvements, or process automation initiatives.

· Experience leading or supporting employee development, onboarding, quality monitoring, performance coaching, or customer experience improvement programs.

· Familiarity with workforce forecasting, scheduling, adherence monitoring, service level tracking, or resource planning.

· Strong ability to translate operational needs into clear business requirements, training needs, process changes, and measurable improvement plans.

jobs.title: Lead Treatment Operator
jobs.description_html:
General Description

The purpose of this position is to ensure and maintain compliance and operations of the Toho Water Authority Wastewater Reclamation Facility assigned. This is accomplished by checking for normal operations, system pressure, and chlorine residuals; performing inspections on all pumps; performing maintenance on all equipment; and evaluating facility operations. Other duties include fulfilling monthly, quarterly, and annual work orders; approving all purchases; tracking all purchases on spread sheets; submitting new purchase orders; creating work orders for repairs; managing customer complaints; and assisting the Chief Operator.

Salary:

Treatment Operator III/C Lead:
$27.36 - $36.45 - Hourly
Treatment Operator IV/B Lead:
$29.26 - $39.02 - Hourly

Treatment Operator V/A Lead:
$32.77 - $46.82 - Hourly

Essential Functions

  1. Fulfills facilities operations by, conducting daily plant tour; collecting data; collecting samples; analyzing chlorine residuals in effluent; recording details in the log book.
  2. Assists the Treatment Operator Chief with biannual and annual employee evaluations.
  3. Manages work orders by generating and assigning work orders. Reviews work orders for timely completion; accurate equipment and work completed information; and ensures costs are captured correctly. Will also close all correctly completed work orders.
  4. Maintains correct inventory of facility chemicals by placing chemical orders as necessary, as well as fuel, and spare equipment.
  5. Remains updated on all company e-mail by daily opening e-mail account; filtering information; saving important data; and replying to emails in a timely manner.
  6. Ensures that the appropriate facility GST tanks levels, pressures, flow rates, and residuals are maintained.

jobs.title: Water Treatment Operator - All Levels
jobs.description_html:
General Description


Trainee: $20.87 - $26.08 Hourly
Operator I (C License): $23.88 - $31.85 Hourly
Operator II (B License): $25.60 - $34.08 Hourly
Operator III (A License): $27.36 - $36.45 Hourly
 
Progression to Operator IV & V will be evaluated based on qualifications and years of experience:
 
Operator IV: $29.26 - $39.02 Hourly 
Operator V: $32.77 - $46.82 Hourly 

The purpose of this position is to operate and maintain the water treatment plant and the drinking water for the public. This is accomplished by collecting daily meter readings; calibrating lab meters; checking plant equipment; adjusting the SCADA computer; checking charts for trends; performing oil changes and greasing; repairing equipment; collecting daily plant samples; recording dissolved oxygen readings; inspecting chlorine cylinders; communicating problems; creating and fulfilling work orders; completing plant and system checks; verifying equipment operation; evaluating trends; and verifying chemical residuals. Other duties include performing UV maintenance and repair; training employees; troubleshooting for plant malfunctions; creating monthly operation reports; managing monthly water charts and plumage reports; developing a majority of the forms the Water Plants use; replying to e-mails; performing janitorial work; overseeing fire flow tests; and supervising contractors.

Essential Functions

Trainee:

  1. Performs daily water plant checks by checking all equipment; monitoring hour meters and flow meters; checking chemical residuals; changing chemical analyzers; maintaining chemical inventory; transferring and inspecting chemicals; calibrating test kits; and adjusting feed rates.
  2. Performs all housekeeping duties by hosing down areas with debris; addressing safety concerns; checking for proper drainage; painting; disposing of trash; assisting with landscaping or beautification projects; and ensuring the facility is maintained.
  3. Collects samples for analysis by using gloves and caution in sampling areas; managing sampling containers carefully; avoiding contaminations; fulfilling chain of custody forms; and obtaining all information for chain of custody forms.
Operator I (C License):
  1. Performs daily water plant checks by checking all equipment; monitoring hour meters and flow meters; checking chemical residuals; changing chemical analyzers; maintaining chemical inventory; transferring and inspecting chemicals; calibrating test kits; and adjusting feed rates.
  2. Maintains the plant by completing maintenance work orders; greasing plant equipment; managing rust/corrosion control; and performing housekeeping practices and general cleaning.
  3. Manages plant repairs by scheduling work orders for internal repair; ensuring all plant equipment in repaired; and assisting mechanics and electricians when necessary.
Operator II (B License):
  1. Performs preventive maintenance by shutting off power; locking out equipment; greasing moving equipment; changing oils in gear boxes; guaranteeing all maintenance activities are safe; and painting equipment. 
  2. Controls processes by checking process basins; using odor sensory perception and results from laboratory tests; reviewing the performance of the process; and overseeing the SCADA system. 
  3. Performs housekeeping duties by cleaning for spider webs; removing all dirt and debris; maintaining materials and equipment; and ensuring the facility is aesthetically pleasing. 
  4. Gives plant tours by evaluating the process and equipment in the treatment process; obtaining daily readings from meters and gauges; maintaining records; and ensuring all equipment functions properly. 
  5. Maintains facility log books by recording duties and projects; maintaining a record of compliance issues; and maintaining entries of process issues and the integrity of the log book. 
  6. Obtains samples for analysis by using gloves and caution when approaching sampling areas; handling sampling containers carefully; closing sample containers promptly; filling out chain of custody forms; and collecting information for chain of custody form.
  7. All other duties as assigned.
Operator III (A License):
  1. Fulfills water plant daily operations by visiting individual facilities; collecting plant data; collecting samples to analyze residuals in water leaving the facility; making any necessary adjustments to chemical feed pumps; recording in log book all the details; and checking remote wells for normal operations. 
  2. Completes monthly work orders by pulling up assigned work orders; reviewing and prioritizing work orders; designating which are to being completed; and completing tasks on work order. 
  3. Remains updated with chemical purchases by approving all chemical purchases for the finance department; copying and filing chemical purchase invoices; submitting purchase orders; and tracking all chemical purchases. 
  4. Manages and replies all company e-mails by opening e-mail account; filtering through information; saving important data; and replying to emails.
  5. All other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Trainee:

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. This is an entry level position, previous relevant work experience is preferred but not required.
  3. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Operator I (C License):
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Minimum of one-year relevant experience.
  3. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
  4. State of Florida Drinking Water Treatment Plant Operator C License.

Operator II (B License):
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator. 
  2. Minimum of three years relevant experience. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. State of Florida Drinking Water Treatment Plant Operator B License. 
  5. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Operator III (A License):
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator. 
  2. Minimum of three years relevant experience. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. State of Florida Drinking Water Treatment Plant Operator A License.
  5. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Director of Treatment Facility Engineering
jobs.description_html:
General Description

The Director of Treatment Facility Engineering is a senior leadership position within Toho’s Engineering group, responsible for leading the planning, design, and delivery of critical treatment facility infrastructure that supports the organization’s operational, regulatory and strategic objectives. This position provides leadership and direction for a portfolio of complex capital improvement projects while fostering technical excellence, organizational capability, and continuous improvement across the program area. 

The Director is responsible for the engineering and design of water treatment facilities, wastewater treatment facilities, reclaimed water systems, supplemental water supply development, storage and pumping infrastructure, and other critical utility assets. The Director also serves as a key stakeholder and partner in long-range planning and capital project development and provides technical leadership throughout construction, commissioning, and operational startup. This role serves as a trusted advisor to the Chief Engineering and Construction Officer, helping translate strategic priorities into actionable programs, projects and engineering solutions.

Key Focus Areas

Deliver Complex Treatment Facility Projects 

Lead the engineering and design of large-scale and technically complex treatment facility projects while also serving as a key stakeholder and advisor in adjoining portions of the project lifecycle including planning, construction, commissioning, and startup.  Ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and in alignment with organizational objectives, regulatory requirements, operational needs, budget expectations, and long-term infrastructure strategies. 

Advance Strategic Planning and Risk Mitigation 

Support the development and execution of the organization’s infrastructure vision by identifying emerging needs and create sustainable strategies that position Toho for future growth and service demands.   Proactively evaluate project risks, resource requirements, schedule impacts and operational considerations to ensure successful project delivery. 

Develop Future Engineering Leaders 

Build and strengthen organizational capability by mentoring engineers, project managers, and emerging leaders.  Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration and continuous learning while supporting employee development, succession planning, and technical excellence across the Engineering Group. 

Success in this role requires technical leadership and development of trusted partnerships across the organization, collaborating with Operations, Engineering, consultants, contractors, regulatory agencies, and community stakeholders to advance strategic infrastructure investments, manage risk, and deliver sustainable, long-term value.

Essential Functions

  1. Provides technical leadership for the planning, design, and delivery of water treatment, wastewater treatment, reclaimed water, pumping, storage, supplemental water supply, and other treatment-related infrastructure projects.
  2. Collaborates with Operations, Planning, Engineering, Construction, the Program Management Office (PMO), consultants, contractors, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders to develop and deliver effective infrastructure solutions that support organizational objectives.
  3. Leads the planning, development, justification, and execution of the capital improvement program within the assigned program area, ensuring alignment with long-term infrastructure, operational, regulatory, and financial strategies.
  4. Provides technical leadership and support throughout the project lifecycle, including project development, preliminary engineering, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational startup.
  5. Directs engineering consultants, contractors, and technical service providers, including procurement, contract negotiations, technical oversight, performance management, and resolution of complex project challenges.
  6. Reviews and approves engineering reports, calculations, drawings, specifications, schedules, bid documents, construction deliverables, and other technical documentation to ensure quality, consistency, and operational reliability.
  7. Interprets and manages regulatory requirements associated with assigned facilities and projects and proactively identifies compliance risks and opportunities.
  8. Develops and maintains engineering standards, technical specifications, design criteria, and related procedures to promote consistency, quality, operational effectiveness, and long-term asset performance.
  9. Coaches, mentors, and develops engineers, project managers, and emerging leaders while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and technical excellence.
  10. Serves as a trusted technical advisor to executive leadership, operational teams, Board members, member governments, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
  11. Develops capital budgets, project forecasts, technical reports, presentations, Board agenda items, and other materials necessary to support project execution and decision-making.
  12. May serve as Engineer of Record and sign and seal engineering documents associated with internal projects.
  13. Maintains awareness of emerging technologies, industry trends, regulatory developments, and best practices to advance organizational performance and infrastructure outcomes.
  14. Supports and promotes workplace safety in accordance with Toho policies and procedures.
  15. May represent the Chief Engineering and Construction Officer in internal and external meetings as delegated.
  16. Performs all other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  1. Bachelor's degree from an ABET accredited university in Civil, Chemical, Mechanical, Environmental Engineering, or related discipline.
  2. Minimum of eight years relevant experience.
  3. Florida Professional Engineer License or the ability to obtain within 12 months.
  4. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  5. Must possess (or have the ability to obtain within 90 days) and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License 

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES:

  1. Extensive knowledge of the planning, design, construction, commissioning, operation, and optimization of water treatment, wastewater treatment, reclaimed water, pumping, storage, and alternative water supply facilities.
  2. Demonstrated ability to build trusted partnerships and effectively collaborate with Operations, Planning, Engineering, Construction, consultants, contractors, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
  3. Demonstrated ability to lead large, complex, and technically challenging capital programs and infrastructure projects.
  4. Strong understanding of applicable engineering principles, regulatory requirements, industry standards, and utility best practices.
  5. Exceptional leadership, coaching, mentoring, and team development skills.
  6. Strong strategic thinking, risk management, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.
  7. Excellent verbal, written, and presentation communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  8. Strong project and program management skills, including management of scope, schedule, budget, quality, and organizational resources.
  9. Ability to collect, analyze, interpret, and apply technical, operational, regulatory, and financial information to support decision-making.
  10. Ability to prioritize competing demands, manage resources effectively, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.
  11. Skilled in negotiation, conflict resolution, and consensus building.
  12. Demonstrated commitment to customer service, continuous improvement, accountability, and safety.

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: 
 The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to handle or feel and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk and bend, kneel, squat, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.
  
WORKING CONDITIONS:
 The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: SCADA Technician - I, II & Senior
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Salary
SCADA Technician I: $29.26 - $39.02 Hourly
SCADA Technician II: $32.77 - $46.82 Hourly 
Senior SCADA Technician: $36.72 - $52.45 Hourly 

The purpose of this position is to provide support on critical applications and department operations.  This is accomplished by performing technical work for the operation, performance, and maintenance of the Toho Water Authority Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. This system monitors and controls water, wastewater, lifts-stations, and reuse-distribution facilities. Under supervision and direction of the SCADA Manager, perform tasks related to the planning, asset management, programming, network configuration, testing, calibration, commissioning, and preventive maintenance of SCADA and related electrical control systems. Lead internal SCADA projects. Perform design and implementation of control and communication systems.

Essential Functions

  1. Manage SCADA system equipment, components, and assets.
  2. Take the lead in troubleshooting SCADA network communication problems.
  3. Maintain, analyze, and improve network system performance.
  4. Improve existing methodologies to ensure proper network system operation and security.
  5. Set-up Ethernet networks, computers and other HMI (Human Machine Interface) equipment for communication with field equipment using established industrial protocols.
  6. Program, install, and test switches, routers, modems and other network equipment.
  7. Test and run diagnostics to verify connectivity of equipment.
  8. Deploy system patches and firmware updates.
  9. Program PLCs for both control and process information gathering and reporting.
  10. Perform any other needed programming, updates, or diagnostics of the SCADA system.
  11. Develop, and update, equipment databases, software licenses, device applications and configurations.
  12. Develop and implement methods for backing up all systems including PLCs to maintain a current library of all custom applications, and ensure all data is retrievable.
  13. Maintain technical library, accurate records, documentation, work reports. Modify existing documents and drawings and incorporate red line markups as needed.
  14. Advise SCADA Manager of needed technology upgrades and assist in planning for upgrades. Collect historical information. Provide input and cost information for budgets.
  15. Develop specifications for vendors for repairs, upgrades, and new installation work.
  16. Manage equipment and software inventory, including spares, and order replacement equipment and software as needed. Maintain warranty information.
  17. Train technicians & operations staff in operation and maintenance of SCADA and PLCs.
  18. Confer with contractors, operators, mechanics, project engineers and supervisors about SCADA issues.
  19. Respond to and resolve internal customer complaints and issues.
  20. Provide documentation as required by others.
  21. Follow procurement rules to order parts.
  22. Understand and practice safe work procedures such as the NFPA 70E, and OSHA
  23. Gives plant data and backups by tagging databases to reports and iHistorian server; creating reports; updating Human Machine Interface screens; backing up Department of Environmental Protection documents; and backing up GE Intelligent Platform.
  24. Performs administrative duties by attending various meetings; training employees; completing work orders; maintaining vehicles; and answering e-mails. Condition facility assessments, meet with vendors.
  25. All other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  1. Associate's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or Electronics or 4 years related field experience.
  2. 6 years’ experience in SCADA control systems development and maintenance in lieu of the education requirement.
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver’s License.
DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS: 
  1. ISA – CCST Certification
  2. SANS GIAC Certification
  3. ISA – 62443 Certifications
  4. ISA – CAP Certification

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: 
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.  Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Electrician- All Levels
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Salary:
Electrician Apprentice: $23.88 - $31.85 Hourly
Electrician I: $25.60 - $34.08 Hourly 
Electrician II: $27.36 - $36.45 Hourly
Progression to Master Electrician will be evaluated based on qualifications and years of experience.
Master Electrician: $32.77 - $46.82 Hourly
The purpose of this position is to maintain all electrical equipment and pumps and requires constant field work and travel to various facilities. The electrician will be expected to repair electrical control panels; maintain inventory; applying for electrical service permits through the City or County Agencies, install electrical control panels, disconnect switches and meter cans, install ¾" to 2" aluminum and PVC piping, pull service wire to electrical devices, dig ditches and install equipment grounding, use concrete drill to penetrate concrete wet well to install 2" conduit, and maintain good verbal and written communication with internal and external customers.   Other duties include conducting on-call duty when necessary.

Essential Functions

Electrician Apprentice:

  1. Ability to follow electrical code manuals to install and repair electrical systems
  2. Digging trenches, building racks for control panels at lift stations, and installing conduit. 
  3. Understand schematic diagrams, CAD drawings, blueprints and other specifications required by our client
  4. Experience working with hand tools, power tool and electronic test equipment
  5. Installing service feeders for services, run pipe, pull branch circuits, install lighting, and minimum troubleshooting.
  6. Pipe running and bending ¾ to 2”, pulling circuits, terminating panel boards, installation of lighting, other electrical duties as required. 
  7. Utilizes vehicles by operating crane, hoist, and bucket trucks; maintaining inventory and truck; and conducting inspections on trucks.
  8. Maintains warehouse by operating forklifts; organizing material; and cleaning the warehouse.
  9. Demonstrate good verbal and written communication to customers and employees.
  10. Demonstrate good computer skills to respond to emails, communicate via phone, send and receive emails, utilize copier and fax machines, and use software application to complete work orders.
  11. All other duties as assigned.
Electrician I: 
  1. Repairs electrical failures by utilizing multi meters, meg meters, and amp meters; and corresponding with cooperators and mechanics. 
  2. Conducts preventative maintenance of electrical equipment by insulating tests on motors; checking amperage; checking for hot spots; calibrating meters; and maintaining electrical panels and rooms of debris. 
  3. Performs electrical installation by ordering material; corresponding with personnel; utilizing generators; and programming radios. 
  4. Utilizes vehicles by operating crane, hoist, and bucket trucks; maintaining inventory and truck; and conducting inspections on trucks. 
  5. Maintains warehouse by operating forklifts; organizing material; and cleaning the warehouse. 
  6. Conducts clerical work by answering and making phone calls; writing and sending emails; copying materials; and completing work orders.
  7. All other duties as assigned.
Electrician II:
  1. Repairs electrical failures by utilizing multi meters, meg meters, and amp meters; and corresponding with cooperators and mechanics. 
  2. Conducts preventative maintenance of electrical equipment by insulating tests on motors; checking amperage; checking for hot spots; calibrating meters; and maintaining electrical panels and rooms of debris. 
  3. Performs electrical installation by ordering material; corresponding with personnel; utilizing generators. 
  4. Utilizes vehicles by operating crane, hoist, and bucket trucks; maintaining inventory and truck; and conducting inspections on trucks. 
  5. Maintains warehouse by operating forklifts; organizing material; and cleaning the warehouse. 
  6. Conducts clerical work by answering and making phone calls; writing and sending emails; copying materials; and completing work orders.
  7. Calibrates and maintains controls and process instruments and other instruments using a 4-20ma control signal.
  8. Maintains arc flash compliance following safety protocols in a live environment.

jobs.title: Criminal Process Technician I
jobs.description_html:
JOB SUMMARY

Starting Pay:  $36,171.20 yearly or $37,273.60 yearly with 3+ years of experience

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS & ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

*** We are posting this position to create a Candidate Pool ***

Responsible for receiving, entering, verifying, processing, and validating various documents related to criminal process. The employee will regularly be required to work weekends, evenings, holidays, or extended shifts; shifts may vary. #oj

Minimum Requirements
  • At least 18 years of age.
  • Must be able to comprehend and communicate fluently in verbal and written English.
  • U.S. Citizen or possess a current permanent resident card.
  • Clean criminal history; any arrest history will be individually evaluated.
  • No illegal drug usage within the past year. Other drug usage will be evaluated on a case by case basis.
  • High school diploma or general education degree (GED) required.
  • Must be able to obtain FCIC/NCIC certification within six (6) months of employment.
  • Ability to receive paperwork and supporting documentation, to include the following items: active warrants, court minutes, and court orders.
  • Ability to confirm information/status of reports and research discrepancies and cases of mistaken identity. Perform monthly validations and/or statistical reports to ensure accuracy of records.
  • Ability to process paperwork, to include recalls for inactive warrants, notification to release forms, and bond paperwork. 
  • Ability to enter data into and retrieve information from the appropriate data base. Run queries, modify records, and flag files in databases such as FCIC/NCIC and agency Records Management System.
  • Ability to receive and screen telephone calls to determine how to direct the call; answer questions or route to appropriate individuals.  
  • Ability to provide information and documents to courts, citizens, outside agencies, and other law enforcement personnel. Answer routine questions and assist individuals with paperwork as needed. 
  • Ability to perform other clerical duties as needed to include the following: photocopying, faxing, filing, typing, etc.
  • Ability to maintain familiarity with procedures outside of primary assignment and within unit (i.e., judicial process, transportation/extraditions, child support) and assist these units when needed.
  • Ability to act as a liaison and conduct follow-up with judges, judicial assistants, clerk of courts, or other law enforcement agencies, as needed.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret general business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations. 
  • Ability to write reports and business correspondence. 
  • Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions.
  • Must have basic computer skills to include word processing, spreadsheet, and various database applications. 
  • Must have the ability to perform basic functions in Outlook and research information using the Internet. 
  • Must have basic mathematical skills, including the ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. 
  • Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions in written, oral, or diagram form. 
  • Ability to deal with problems involving several concrete variables in standardized situations. 
  • Must be detail-oriented with the ability to multi-task within established time-limits (e.g., simultaneously handle multiple phone lines and perform data entry with minimal errors). 
  • Must be able to present a positive image in person and over the phone. 
  • Must possess good interpersonal and customer service skills with the ability to work well with others. 
  • Must possess basic problem-solving abilities. 
  • Must have the ability to learn, understand, express, apply, and demonstrate knowledge of relevant Florida State Statutes as well as agency policies and procedures. 
  • Must be able to maintain confidentiality when dealing with sensitive information.

PROCESSING & TRAINING

ADDITIONAL PROCESSING:

  • Some positions, depending on the responsibilities, may require the candidate to successfully pass a physical or other selection processes when needed.
  • Please upload a copy of your resume that is no longer than two (2) pages in length to your application

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

PHYSICAL DEMANDS  

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit and use hands to handle or feel. The employee is regularly required to reach with hands and arms; talk; and hear. The employee is frequently required to sit, stand, and walk. The employee is occasionally required to climb or balance. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and ability to adjust focus.

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

Work is generally performed in a standard office setting. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. The employee will regularly be required to work weekends, evenings, holidays, or extended shifts; shifts may vary.
 
Work is generally performed in a standard office setting. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Depending on assignment the employee may be required to work evening, midnight and/or weekend shifts, as the unit must be manned by this position 24 hours a day, seven days a week.  Shift times may vary.
