jobs.title: Oasis Charter Schools- High School Interventionist
jobs.description_html:
GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

The Interventionist Teacher provides targeted small-group instruction, individualized academic interventions, and progress monitoring for students who demonstrate the greatest academic need. Working under the direction of the Principal or designee, the teacher uses assessment data to identify specific learning gaps, develop intervention plans, and adjust instruction to improve student growth and progress toward grade-level standards. The position expands the school’s capacity to provide timely academic support and helps classroom teachers meet the needs of all students.

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Since every duty associated with this position may not be described herein, employees may be required to perform duties not specifically spelled out but may be considered incidental in the performance of this job.

  • Identifies and prioritizes students for intervention using multiple sources of information, including diagnostic and screening assessments, state and local assessments, classroom performance, teacher referrals, and the school’s Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS) process.
  • Develops individualized intervention plans that document baseline performance, specific skill needs, measurable goals, instructional strategies, frequency and duration of services, progress-monitoring methods, and review dates.
  • Provides scheduled, evidence-based small-group and individualized instruction in assigned academic areas, which may include literacy, mathematics, foundational skills, course-specific prerequisite skills, and other areas identified through school data and student need, emphasizing the prerequisite and essential skills needed to access grade-level coursework and standards. Adapts instruction and materials to the developmental needs of the grade levels served.
  • Uses explicit instruction, modeling, guided practice, repeated opportunities for skill application, and timely, specific feedback to address identified learning gaps.
  • Organizes flexible instructional groups and coordinates intervention schedules with the Principal and classroom teachers to provide consistent services while supporting access to core instruction.
  • Prepares and implements intervention lesson plans and instructional activities aligned with identified skill deficits, applicable Florida academic standards, charter-approved curriculum, and approved intervention resources.
  • Administers approved diagnostic and progress-monitoring assessments at intervals established in intervention plans; analyzes results and adjusts instructional strategies, grouping, intensity, or duration based on student response.
  • Supports students in improving academic performance and, at the secondary level, course completion, credit attainment, and progress toward graduation requirements, as applicable to assigned grade levels, interventions, and student needs.
  • Maintains accurate, timely records of intervention plans, services delivered, attendance, assessment results, and student progress.
  • Collaborates regularly with classroom teachers to align intervention with classroom instruction, review specific learning gaps, share effective strategies, and support application of skills in classroom assignments.
  • Participates in MTSS, student support, and data review meetings; contributes documented evidence to decisions about continuing, modifying, intensifying, or exiting interventions.
  • Coordinates with exceptional student education staff, Section 504 coordinators, English language learner staff, counselors, and other appropriate personnel to support students’ identified needs and implement applicable accommodations within assigned responsibilities. This position does not assume ESE case-management, IEP development, Section 504 plan development, evaluation, or other compliance responsibilities unless separately assigned and appropriately qualified.
  • Communicates intervention goals and progress to students, families, classroom teachers, and administrators; helps students understand their learning goals and develop productive academic habits.
  • Establishes a safe, supportive, and structured learning environment that encourages participation, persistence, and student confidence.
  • Works with Administration to establish and review measures of position effectiveness, including growth from baseline, progress toward grade-level standards and individual goals, intervention participation, and relevant course performance and academic indicators; provides periodic summaries of student outcomes and intervention implementation, including students served, planned and delivered services, goal attainment, and recommendations for improvement, reviewed in the context of students’ starting points, needs, and participation.
  • Uses charter-approved instructional technology, assessment platforms, student information systems, learning management systems, and communication tools to support instruction, document services, and monitor student progress.
  • Provides appropriate supervision of students during assigned instructional periods and follows charter school policies and procedures related to student safety, emergency response, discipline, and mandatory reporting.
  • Attends and participates in required faculty meetings, professional learning communities related to instruction at assigned grade levels, academic intervention, assessment, and data analysis; uses feedback and results to improve practice.
  • Attends parent/guardian conferences, school events, and other assigned duties in accordance with the school calendar and charter school policies.
  • Maintains confidentiality, follows professional standards, and complies with applicable charter school policies and student support requirements.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Alternatives to the minimum qualifications can be made by the Board as they find appropriate and acceptable.
Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in education or related field.
Experience:
  • Required: Previous teaching experience.
  • Preferred: Teaching or intervention experience at the assigned grade levels, and experience providing targeted academic intervention, using assessment data to guide instruction, and monitoring student progress.
Licenses and Certifications:
  • Valid Florida teaching certificate appropriate to the assigned grade levels, subjects, and courses. Must maintain any additional certifications, endorsements, or training required for assigned intervention services, including applicable reading requirements.
  • Must meet applicable employment screening and fingerprinting requirements.

ADDITIONAL MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED: KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Knowledge of Florida academic standards, curriculum for assigned grade levels, and prerequisite and foundational skills in assigned instructional areas.
  • Knowledge of evidence-based intervention, explicit instruction, differentiated instruction, child and adolescent development and learning, and MTSS problem-solving processes.
  • Skill in identifying learning gaps, establishing measurable goals, and using diagnostic and progress-monitoring data to adjust instruction.
  • Ability to provide effective small-group and individualized instruction to students with varied academic, language, cultural, and learning needs.
  • Ability to align interventions with core instruction and collaborate effectively with classroom teachers and student support personnel.
  • Skill in organizing intervention schedules, maintaining accurate records, and using instructional technology and approved student data systems.
  • Ability to communicate clearly with students, families, and colleagues; provide constructive feedback; and maintain professional judgment and confidentiality.

jobs.title: Oasis Charter School- Food Service Substitute
jobs.description_html:
GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

Under the general supervision of the Lead Food Service Worker, the Substitute Food Service Worker is responsible for preparing and serving food to students and staff, maintaining a clean and sanitary work environment, and stocking of inventory and supplies. 

Individual(s) assigned to this classification must report to work per their assigned schedule.

Background Screening Requirement:
Florida law requires all school personnel to undergo a Level 2 background screening through the Florida Department of Education’s Background Screening Clearinghouse. In accordance with House Bill 531, employment is contingent upon an applicant’s eligibility for clearance and the successful completion of all required background screenings prior to hire.
 For additional information about the background screening process, please visit: https://info.flclearinghouse.com

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Since every duty associated with this position may not be described herein, employees may be required to perform duties not specifically spelled out but may be considered incidental in the performance of this job. 

  • Prepares, cooks, and serves food to students in accordance with menus and nutritional guidelines.
  • Handles and stores food safely, including checking and maintaining proper temperatures in accordance with food safety regulations.
  • Operates and maintains food warmers, serving stations, and other kitchen equipment, ensuring compliance with temperature and sanitation standards.
  • Upholds the highest standards of safety, cleanliness, and sanitation in all aspects of food preparation and service.
  • Monitors the condition of food service equipment and reports required maintenance or necessary repairs to supervisor. 
  • Sets up and cleans the cafeteria and serving areas before and after meal periods.
  • Cleans and sanitizes dishes, appliances, and all areas within the food service area.
  • Maintains inventory of food and supplies; assists in receiving, organizing, and storing deliveries and restocking inventory as needed.
  • Communicates effectively with students, staff, and supervisors to ensure smooth daily operations and a positive dining experience.
  • Attends vocational classes, seminars, and related in service training opportunities as assigned. 
  • Performs other duties as required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Alternatives to the minimum qualifications can be made by the Board as they find appropriate and acceptable.
Education:

  • High School Diploma or GED equivalent preferred.
Experience:
  • None; food service experience preferred.
Licenses and Certifications:
  • Food Safety Certification.

ADDITIONAL MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED: KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Ability to interact positively with students and perform duties with consistent courtesy and tact
  • Working knowledge of the English language.
  • Ability to communicate effectively.
  • Ability to understand and follow oral and written instructions.
  • Knowledge of the methods, supplies, equipment, and operating procedures related to food service.
  • Knowledge of safety precautions applicable to food handling and storage.
  • Ability to use independent judgement in relatively routine and stable situations.
  • Ability to work under stressful conditions as necessary.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with students, colleagues, and others.
  • General knowledge of reporting and record keeping principles and techniques.

jobs.title: Oasis Charter Schools- Media Coordinator
jobs.description_html:
GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

Under the general supervision of the Superintendent or designated supervisor, the Media Coordinator maintains website content and supports digital communications across all four Oasis Charter Schools, ensuring information is accurate, current, and accessible in accordance with established accessibility requirements and Cape Coral Charter School Authority (CCCSA) policies and procedures. The position also assists designated staff in maintaining book and media inventory records and reviewing materials for age and developmental appropriateness in accordance with Florida Department of Education guidelines and school policies and procedures. Performs related work as required.

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Since every duty associated with this position may not be described herein, employees may be required to perform duties not specifically spelled out but may be considered incidental in the performance of this job. 

  • Posts, reviews, and updates website content for the Cape Coral Charter School Authority (CCCSA) and all Oasis Charter Schools, including news, announcements, calendars, staff information, and required notices, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and timely publication.
  • Reviews and corrects website content for accessibility, including alternative text, heading structure, color contrast, descriptive links, and captions, in accordance with established accessibility requirements.
  • Creates, converts, or remediates PDFs and other electronic documents into accessible formats, correcting document structure, reading order, tags, and formatting as needed.
  • Conducts regular website reviews for outdated information, broken links, and accessibility issues; documents findings, completes routine corrections, and coordinates unresolved technical issues with designated staff or the website platform vendor.
  • Maintains shared electronic files of approved images, documents, forms, and permission slips, ensuring current versions are available for publication and staff use.
  • Collects, reconciles, and maintains electronic inventories of books and media across all four schools, including classroom collections, and coordinates updates with designated school staff to screen books and media for age and developmental appropriateness using established Florida Department of Education guidelines and Charter School Authority procedures.
  • Maintains records of materials reviewed, authorized decisions, additions, and removals; prepares and publishes required collection and reading lists as directed.
  • Monitors school social media accounts in accordance with established posting expectations, communication procedures, and accessibility requirements.
  • Trains and supports staff throughout administration and all schools on routine website content updates, accessibility practices, document preparation, and established media procedures, as directed.
  • Maintains spreadsheets, review logs, and a calendar of recurring updates and reviews; tracks deadlines, approvals, corrections, and unresolved items and follows up with responsible staff.
  • May be assigned to back up other media or clerical staff after appropriate training.
  • Provides support in library/media centers and other learning facilities when appropriate.
  • Maintains confidentiality and complies with laws and policies concerning student information and school records.
  • Participates in training programs when appropriate.
  • Performs other duties as required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Alternatives to the minimum qualifications can be made by the Board as they find appropriate and acceptable.
Education:

  • High school diploma or GED required. Sixty (60) hours of college credit from an accredited institution or Paraprofessional Certification required.
Experience:
  • Three (3) or more years of experience in an educational setting preferred.
Licenses and Certifications:
  • Willingness to complete job-related accessibility training (such as through IAAP, DHS, The A11Y Collective, or an equivalent provider) within twelve (12) months of hire required.

ADDITIONAL MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED: KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • General knowledge of report and recordkeeping principles and techniques.
  • General knowledge of ADA, WCAG, and accessible document practices, or the ability to learn them quickly.
  • Skilled in written and oral communication for effective expression and clarity.
  • Ability to utilize a variety of modern office equipment and software, including content management systems, Microsoft Office, PDF tools, and social media platforms.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with supervisors, teachers, administrators, and staff across multiple campuses.
  • Ability to organize and review work for efficient results, accuracy, and attention to detail.
  • Ability to meet deadlines, manage multiple priorities, and work independently.
  • Ability to perform duties with consistent courtesy and tact in the best interest of the Cape Coral Charter School Authority (CCCSA).
  • Ability to issue and follow oral and written instructions.

jobs.title: Oasis Charter Schools- High School Math Teacher
jobs.description_html:
GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

Under the general supervision of the Principal or designated supervisor, the Teacher is responsible for developing and implementing instructional lessons for secondary students in accordance with federal and state laws, as well as Charter School Authority guidelines. This position supports the effective operation of the school by coordinating and communicating with administrators, instructional and support staff, parents, and students. The role requires the ability to prioritize tasks and work independently, with periodic supervision or review. 

Background Screening Requirement:
Florida law requires all school personnel to undergo a Level 2 background screening through the Florida Department of Education’s Background Screening Clearinghouse. In accordance with House Bill 531, employment is contingent upon an applicant’s eligibility for clearance and the successful completion of all required background screenings prior to hire.
 For additional information about the background screening process, please visit: https://info.flclearinghouse.com

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Since every duty associated with this position may not be described herein, employees may be required to perform duties not specifically spelled out but may be considered incidental in the performance of this job. 

  • Guides secondary students toward achieving their intellectual, emotional, physical, and social potential in a safe, inclusive, and efficient learning environment aligned with the goals of the school.
  • Plans and delivers instruction, both individually or cooperatively, that meet the individual needs, interests, and abilities of all students.
  • Contributes to the development, implementation, and evaluation of department or grade-level curriculum goals and instructional objectives.
  • Establishes a classroom environment that is safe, inclusive, and conducive to learning and appropriate to the maturity and interests of the students, fostering a culture of curiosity, participation, and mutual respect. 
  • Aligns instruction with curriculum goals by setting and clearly communicating objectives for lessons, units, and projects.
  • Utilizes a variety of instructional methods, materials, and resources appropriate for meeting student needs and learning objectives consistent with the capabilities of all individuals or student groups involved.
  • Effectively integrates technology to enhance instruction, student engagement, and academic outcomes.
  • Grades tests, exams, assignments, and projects; evaluates student performance and identifies learning strengths and challenges, Provides additional support when needed, and seeks support from specialists as appropriate.
  • Regularly monitors and assesses student progress, providing timely and constructive feedback to students and communicating academic performance, challenges, and achievements to parents or guardians.
  • Maintains open, consistent, and professional communication with colleagues, students, and parents or guardians to support student growth and academic success. 
  • Supports the implementation of school policies governing student conduct and promotes positive behavior and a respectful, well-managed classroom by developing fair and consistent rules and procedures to minimize disruptions and de-escalate students with social, emotional, and behavioral needs.
  • Recognizes and appropriately responds to signs of student distress or abuse in accordance with school procedures and law.
  • Plans and supervises meaningful tasks for auxiliary personnel and participates in evaluating their effectiveness in collaboration with department or grade-level leaders.
  • Maintains accurate, complete, and timely records in accordance with laws, Charter School Authority policies, and administrative regulations.

jobs.title: Oasis Charter Schools- Substitute Teacher
jobs.description_html:
GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

**NOTE** 
This posting is intended to create a general candidate pool for substitute teacher opportunities across all schools. Applicants should not expect an immediate response after applying. When a substitute need arises, individual schools may review candidates from this applicant pool and contact those whose qualifications meet the needs of the position to schedule an interview.

Under general supervision of the Principal or designated supervisor, the Substitute Teacher is responsible for ensuring the continuation of learning in the absence of the regular classroom teacher.

Background Screening Requirement:
Florida law requires all school personnel to undergo a Level 2 background screening through the Florida Department of Education’s Background Screening Clearinghouse. In accordance with House Bill 531, employment is contingent upon an applicant’s eligibility for clearance and the successful completion of all required background screenings prior to hire.
For additional information about the background screening process, please visit: https://info.flclearinghouse.com

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Since every duty associated with this position may not be described herein, employees may be required to perform duties not specifically spelled out but may be considered incidental in the performance of this job. 

  • Reports to the principal or designee upon arrival to the school and reviews written expectations set by the school.
  • Maintains student behavior in class by supporting school policies governing student conduct and promoting positive behavior and a respectful, well-managed classroom.
  • Maintains the established routines and ensures a classroom environment that is safe, inclusive, and conducive to learning and appropriate to the maturity and interests of the students, fostering a culture of curiosity, participation, and mutual respect.
  • Delivers instruction based on the lesson plan provided utilizing a variety of instructional methods, materials, and resources appropriate for meeting student needs and learning objectives.
  • Consults with the principal or designee for approval prior to initiating any procedures not specified in the lesson plans provided and substitute teacher's handbook.
  • Reports to Principal or designee at the end of the day to verify whether or not   attendance is required on the following teaching day.
  • Adheres to the Code of Ethics of the Education Profession in Florida and complies with all school and Charter School Authority policy requirements to which regular teachers are subject and which good practice dictates.
  • Promotes a culture of high performance and continuous improvement by modeling a commitment to excellence and lifelong learning.
  • Assists with school-related activities outside the classroom, including field trips, fundraisers, before and after school duties, and lunch or hall monitoring as assigned.
  • Performs other duties as required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Alternatives to the minimum qualifications can be made by the Board as they find appropriate and acceptable.
Education:

  • Associate’s degree from an accredited college or university.
  • Bachelor’s Degree Preferred
Experience:
  • Educational background preferred.
Licenses and Certifications:
  • Valid Florida teaching certificate preferred.

ADDITIONAL MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED: KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Skilled in oral communications for effective expression and clarity.
  • Some knowledge of report and record keeping principles and techniques and experience with industry-standard computer applications.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective-working relationships with supervisors, support staff, and others.
  • Ability to organize and review work for efficient results and accuracy.
  • Ability to handle a multitude of diverse tasks simultaneously while maintaining an attention to detail for the purpose of ensuring accuracy in task performance.

jobs.title: Instructor, Respiratory Care
jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

Maintain continued competence in assigned areas and related disciplines; foster positive working relationships with students, faculty, staff, and community members; support the College’s recruitment and retention efforts; contribute to College governance through committee service; and comply with College policies and procedures and applicable state guidelines related to faculty responsibilities. 

Responsible for demonstrating LSSC’s core values of Caring, Communicating, Collaborating, and Celebrating when interacting with students, employees, visitors, and community members.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to the following: 

  • Plan and carry out instructional duties that maximize learning by students.
  • Supervise students in accordance with program procedures, academic, and course-related concerns.
  • Teach assigned courses in accordance with course descriptions. Perform on-site clinical practice teaching at assigned hospitals.
  • Work a minimum of 35 hours per week, which includes 15 classroom hours, 10 office or student contact hours, and 10 hours as needed by the program/college.
  • Assist with registration and/or recruitment when requested.
  • Furnish each student with a course syllabus per College expectations.
  • Regularly examine the content of assigned courses and recommend changes to the LSSC supervisor if needed. Any additions, revisions, or supplemental materials incorporated into the course must be compliant with ADA accessibility standards and institutional accessibility requirements.
  • Function as a member of the faculty committee in developing the instructional program and educational philosophy of the college.
  • Attend all scheduled or called meetings by the President or Vice President of Academic Affairs, AVP Health Professions, and Program Director, unless excused by the administrator in charge.
  • Teach all classes for the full period as scheduled.
  • Evaluate student progress and achievement with clear methods presented in the course syllabus.
  • Utilize evaluation results for planning, instruction, counseling, and program modification.
  • Keep accurate and up-to-date records.
  • Submit grade reports and other required data on or before the deadline dates.
  • Resolve discipline problems within the sphere of responsibility.
  • Assist and counsel students as needed, including during office and campus hours.
  • Utilizes materials and equipment necessary to accomplish designated tasks.
  • Demonstrate knowledge of current instructional developments.
  • Regularly examines the content of assigned courses and recommends changes to the curriculum committee as needed.
  • Comply with appropriate administrative rules/regulations and Board Policy.
  • Participate in an annual evaluation process as specified by the Vice President of Academic Affairs.
  • Participate in Commencement ceremonies and Respiratory Care pinning ceremonies.
  • Maintain continuity of communication with students, community, faculty, staff, and supervisors through timely replies to meetings, phone calls, mail, and email requests.
  • Teach on multiple campus sites as needed.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Demonstrate computer technology proficiency in Microsoft programs (Word, Excel, Teams, & PowerPoint)
  • Effectively communicate in both a virtual and physical environment
  • Ability to work well in a team environment
  • Ability to successfully demonstrate knowledge and expertise in the applied field

ABILITIES/GENERAL:

  • Promote a common purpose consistent with stated College goals and demonstrate a commitment to students and the learning environment.
  • Possess knowledge of general written standards and procedures utilized, and have the ability to read, interpret, and follow procedural and policy manuals related to the job tasks
  • Demonstrate the ability to respond to supervision, guidance, and direction in a positive, receptive manner and in accordance with stated policies.
  • Provide quality customer service by creating a welcoming and supportive environment.
  • Present a professional image in word, action, and attire.
  • Demonstrate professionalism in dealing with a diverse population while understanding and respecting each other’s views of the world, personalities, and working styles
  • Conduct oneself in a manner consistent with the College’s standards of ethical conduct.
  • Apply effective techniques to create working relationships with others to achieve common goals; successfully communicate and collaborate with others to achieve goals.
  • Demonstrate skills necessary to look at situations and processes critically to make recommendations for improvement.
  • Strong service orientation and ability to effectively work as a member or leader of a team by cooperating with others, offering to help others when needed, and considering larger organizational goals rather than individual concerns. Includes the ability to build &/or support a constructive team spirit where members are committed to the goals and objectives of the organization.
  • Plan, organize, and successfully multitask to meet multiple deadlines and frequently new work tasks within required timeframes. Proven flexibility to successfully work on diversified projects at a fast and accurate pace.
  • Effectively manage change and adaptability
  • Adhere to all workplace safety rules, safety laws, regulations, standards, and practices
  • Ability to work various hours, including nights, early mornings, and weekends 
  • Ability to travel amongst various campuses and attend College events, on or off campus, as required. 

Minimum Qualifications & Education

  • Required:
  • Master’s degree from a U.S. accredited institution; or relevant alternative credentials may be considered.
  • Four (4) years of experience as a Registered Respiratory Therapist (RRT), including at least two (2) years of clinical respiratory care experience.
  • BLS Certification 
  • Active, unencumbered Registered Respiratory Therapy (RRT) license and a current State of Florida licensure (or other active state RRT licensure with transferability to the State of Florida). 
  • Preferred:
    • ACLS, and PALS Certification 
    • Teaching experience in higher education

jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

Assists the Campus Safety Department staff with applying policies and procedures to ensure the safety, security, and welfare of all students, faculty, staff, and visitors. Position is an armed Campus Safety Guardian position; however, there shall be no law enforcement authority, except to the extent necessary to prevent or abate an active assailant incident (an individual actively engaged in killing or attempting to kill people in a confined and populated area) on the premises of any Lake-Sumter State College Campus or facility.  

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to the following:   

  • Use necessary force to prevent or abate an active assailant incident.
  • Immediately respond to and engage to stop the threat of an active assailant.
  • Conduct perimeter, exterior, and interior checks of their assigned campus to ensure premises are secure.
  • Analyze information and situations regarding activities that may be in violation of college policies and/or an indication of possible criminal activity for the purpose of determining immediate actions and/or making recommendations to ensure the safety of students, staff, faculty, and the public.
  • Collaborate with other college personnel, representatives of local agencies, etc., for the purpose of preliminary inquiries into violations of college policies and providing information and/or taking action, etc., for safety and security.
  • Communicate college policies and procedures with personnel and visitors for the purpose of ensuring their understanding of the potential consequences of violation.
  • Participate in major campus events, including but not limited to Welcome Back and Commencement.
  • Prepare a variety of documents (e.g., reports, security logs, memos, letters, procedures, etc.) for the purpose of documenting activities, providing written reference, and/or conveying information.
  • Serve as a vital front-line and strategic member of the College’s Campus Safety Department.
  • Refers observations and incidents (e.g., injuries, altercations, suspicious activities, inappropriate social behavior, violations of rules, etc.) for the purpose of communicating information to appropriate institutional personnel and/or law enforcement for follow-up action.
  • Utilize and monitor surveillance technology.
  • Provide support in campus emergency situations and participate in all campus emergency drills.  
  • Utilize current technology, as appropriate, to perform job functions and participate in training programs offered to increase technology skill level, job proficiency, current trends, and best practices relevant to the area of responsibility.
  • Work collaboratively with all areas of the college in addressing safety and security concerns, providing guidance and advice to ensure consistent enforcement of college policies and procedures relating to safety and security.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Ability to work well in a collaborative decision-making environment. 
  • Ability to execute routine, effective oral and written communication skills, especially with the ability to speak and write persuasively. 
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with a variety of constituencies. 
  • Project professional demeanor and maturity, exercise sound judgment, demonstrate commitment toward outstanding service and teamwork. 
  • Demonstrated strong oral and written communication skills. 
  • Ability to maintain good working relations with all college personnel, members of the local community, and representatives of state and federal agencies. 
  • Demonstrated knowledge of state and federal laws, regulations, policies, and legal resources relating to but not limited to the Clergy Act and Title IX. 

ABILITIES/GENERAL:

  • Promote a common purpose consistent with the College's stated goals and demonstrate a commitment to students and the learning environment.
  • Possess knowledge of general written standards and procedures utilized, and have the ability to read, interpret, and follow procedural and policy manuals related to the job tasks.
  • Demonstrate the ability to respond to a multitude of situations and provide direction in a positive, receptive manner, and follow stated policies.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service by fostering a welcoming and supportive environment.
  • Present a professional image in words, actions, and attire.
  • Conduct oneself in a manner consistent with the College’s standards of ethical conduct.
  • Apply effective techniques to establish and maintain working relationships, fostering collaboration to achieve common goals; effectively communicate and collaborate with others to achieve shared objectives.
  • Demonstrate the skills necessary to examine situations and processes, making recommendations for improvement critically.
  • Strong service orientation and ability to effectively work as a member or leader of a team by cooperating with others, offering to help others when needed, and considering larger organizational goals rather than individual concerns. Includes the ability to build &/or support a constructive team spirit where members are committed to the goals and objectives of the organization.
  • Plan, organize, and successfully multitask to meet multiple deadlines and frequently new work tasks within required timeframes. Proven flexibility to successfully work on a variety of projects quickly and accurately.
  • Effectively manage change and adaptability.
  • Adheres to all workplace safety rules, safety laws, regulations, standards, and practices
  • Ability to work various hours, including nights, early mornings, and weekends 
  • Ability to travel amongst various campuses and attend College events, on or off campus, as required.

Minimum Qualifications & Education

  • Required:
    • Current Guardian Certification from a Florida Sheriff’s Office, as outlined in Section 30.15(1)(k).
    • Must maintain guardian certification through annual firearms requalification and mandatory training throughout employment.    
    • Associate's degree or higher from an accredited institution.
    • A combination of education and experience may be substituted for the degree requirement.
    • A minimum of 4 years of experience in law enforcement, military police, campus safety, or public safety. 
    • Must be 21 years of ag or older. 
    • Must have a valid Florida Driver’s License.  
  • Preferred:
    • Experience working in campus safety.
    • Knowledge of Federal law, Florida state statutes, and Administrative Code relevant to campus safety.
    • Established relationships with local law enforcement agencies.

jobs.title: Adjunct (Faculty) – Student Life Skills (High School Site)
jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

TITLE: Adjunct Student Life Skills (High School Sites in Lake County School District or Sumter County School District)
 LENGTH: OF APPOINTMENT: One-Term
 LOCATION: Current High School Site
 CLASSIFICATION: Instructional
 SUPERVISORS: Dean, Associate Dean, Program Manager

Dynamic and Engaging Opportunity Awaits You!

Are you ready to bring your expertise to life in the vibrant world of academia? Join our team as an Adjunct Instructor at Lake-Sumter State College (LSSC), where innovation meets education in an environment pulsating with energy and excitement!  LSSC Adjunct Instructors ignite the minds of our student body through dynamic lectures, interactive discussions, and hands-on experiences. Join us in shaping the future of our students by fostering a supportive learning environment grounded in LSSC’s core values: Communication, Collaboration, Care, and Celebrate!

The passion for your expertise is the catalyst for a dynamic educational journey for our students and their future success.

Lake-Sumter State College assures its students, employees, visitors, and contractors of their civil rights. LSSC prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, ethnicity, sex, age, disability, marital status, pregnancy, veteran status, religion, sexual orientation, or genetic information in any of its programs, activities, employment, and contracts.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to, the following:   

  • Plan and carry out instructional duties that maximize learning by students.
  • Supervise students in accordance with program procedures, academic, and course-related concerns.
  • Teach assigned courses in accordance with department expectations.
  • Assist with registration and/or recruitment when requested.
  • Syllabus must be submitted by the designated date according to LSSC policy and Florida State Board Rule. 
  • Ensure that each student receives a course syllabus detailing performance objectives, course expectations, grading procedures, withdrawal and attendance policies, and faculty office phone and email contact information.
  • Attend all scheduled or called meetings by the President or Vice President of Academic Affairs, Associate Vice President of Academic Affairs, Deans, and/or LSSC supervisor, unless excused by the administrator in charge.
  • Teach all classes for the full period as scheduled.
  • Evaluate student progress and achievement with clear methods presented in the course syllabus.
  • Utilize evaluation results for planning, instruction, counseling, and program modification.
  • Keep accurate and up-to-date records.
  • Submit grade reports and other required data on or before deadline dates.
  • Resolve discipline problems within the sphere of responsibility.
  • Assist and counsel students as needed.
  • Utilize material and equipment necessary to accomplish designated tasks.
  • Demonstrate knowledge of current instructional developments.
  • Regularly examine the content of assigned courses and recommend changes to the LSSC supervisor if needed. Any additions, revisions, or supplemental materials incorporated into the course must be compliant with ADA accessibility standards and institutional accessibility requirements.
  • Comply with appropriate administrative rules/regulations and Board Policy.
  • Participate in an evaluation process as specified by the Vice President of Academic Affairs.
  • Maintain continuity of communication with students, community, faculty, staff, and supervisors through timely replies to meetings, phone calls, mail, and email requests.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Adhere to all workplace safety rules, safety laws, regulations, standards, and practices
  • Ability to work various hours, including nights, early mornings, and weekends 
  • Ability to travel amongst various campuses and attend College events, or off-campus, as required. 

Minimum Qualifications & Education

Required:

  • Master’s degree in the teaching discipline listed in this job description, with at least 18 graduate-level semester hours in the listed teaching discipline.
  • Must be a full-time employee with the Lake County School District or Sumter County School District.

jobs.title: Program Director, RN-BSN
jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

The Program Director is responsible for developing, implementing, continuously improving, and promoting the RN-BSN program. This role supports the Assistant Vice President of Health Professions in supervising and evaluating faculty, initiating and coordinating course offerings and instructor assignments, and assisting with the planning and delivery of adjunct faculty orientation. The Director ensures that all program components comply with applicable accreditation standards and federal and state regulations. This position reports to the Assistant Vice President of Health Professions and includes teaching responsibilities as assigned, based on instructional needs, which may extend to branch campuses and off-site locations.


In addition, the Director serves as a supervisor, leader, mentor, and role model for both students and program personnel. The position is accountable for the ongoing development, implementation, and evaluation of the RN-BSN curriculum, while fostering a collegial, respectful, and high-performing work environment that supports employee engagement and student success.


Responsible for demonstrating LSSC’s core values of Caring, Communicating, Collaborating, and Celebrating when interacting with students, employees, visitors, and community members.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to the following:   

  • Educational responsibilities include, but are not limited to, teaching, curriculum development, and evaluation. Plan, prepare, and teach course content and curriculum, utilizing effective methodologies of instruction and assessment tools for the enhancement of learning. Utilize technology in teaching, communicating with students, and in the delivery of instruction.  
  • Teach not more than nine (9) credit hours as needed each semester. Keep records of students' attendance and grades in all assigned classes. Grade books should be kept for at least 3 years. Attend commencement exercises, convocations, faculty meetings, and College functions.  
  • Regularly examine the content of assigned courses and recommend changes to the LSSC supervisor if needed. Any additions, revisions, or supplemental materials incorporated into the course must be compliant with ADA accessibility standards and institutional accessibility requirements.
  • Administrative responsibilities include fiscal planning, continuous review and analysis, planning and development, and the RN-BSN Program's overall effectiveness. Assists the AVP in the preparation of the budget for the RN-BSN program. Orders and maintains necessary instructional equipment and supplies. 
  • Participate in enrollment management activities and share professional expertise with colleagues and students beyond the classroom. Supports student activities, including course and career guidance, with a focus on fostering a love of learning. 
  • Participate in the College’s Institutional Effectiveness Plan primarily by identifying student learning outcomes, assessing the extent to which these outcomes are attained, and using the results to improve student learning. 
  • Maintain expertise in the field of study and teaching pedagogy. Maintains active participation in professional organizations as appropriate. 
  • Resolve discipline problems within the sphere of responsibility.
  • Establish course syllabus with competencies tied to a matrix for assessment, and curriculum and content area standards.  
  • Maintain continuity of communication with students, community, faculty, staff, and supervisors through timely replies to meetings, phone calls, mail, and email requests.
  • Community engagement: developing community and industry partnerships.
  • Serves on Departmental, Division, and College Committees as requested or required.  
  • Assists in recruiting, interviewing, and recommending the employment of RN-BSN personnel. Ensures that all RN-BSN training complies with the relevant regulatory agencies. 
  • Recruit and participate with the advisory committee for the ASN/RN-BSN Programs.  
  • Perform additional faculty job requirements as required by specialized and accredited programs (ACEN).
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Exceptional people skills with the ability to communicate effectively with people from a wide variety of educational and professional backgrounds. 
  • Demonstrated quantitative, organizational, and technical skills adequate to help design, monitor, and interpret assessment results. 
  • Familiarity with student learning outcomes assessment and how this process relates to program and institution accreditation. 
  • Ability to maintain good working relations with all College personnel, members of the local community, and representatives of state and federal agencies. 
  • Ability to work well in a collaborative decision-making environment. 
  • Effective oral and written communication skills. 
  • Knowledge of RN curriculum design, implementation, and evaluation. 
  • Advanced computer and technology skills for daily work and online teaching.

ABILITIES/GENERAL: 

  • Promote a common purpose consistent with the College's stated goals and demonstrate a commitment to students and the learning environment.
  • Possess knowledge of general written standards and procedures utilized, and have the ability to read, interpret, and follow procedural and policy manuals related to the job tasks.
  • Demonstrate the ability to respond to supervision, guidance, and direction in a positive, receptive manner and follow stated policies.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service by fostering a welcoming and supportive environment.
  • Present a professional image in words, actions, and attire.
  • Conduct oneself in a manner consistent with the College’s standards of ethical conduct.
  • Apply effective techniques to establish and maintain working relationships, fostering collaboration to achieve common goals; effectively communicate and collaborate with others to achieve shared objectives.
  • Demonstrate the skills necessary to examine situations and processes, making recommendations for improvement critically.
  • Strong service orientation and ability to effectively work as a member or leader of a team by cooperating with others, offering to help others when needed, and considering larger organizational goals rather than individual concerns. Includes the ability to build &/or support a constructive team spirit where members are committed to the goals and objectives of the organization.
  • Plan, organize, and successfully multitask to meet multiple deadlines and frequently new work tasks within required timeframes. Proven flexibility to successfully work on a variety of projects quickly and accurately.
  • Effectively manage change and adaptability.
  • Adheres to all workplace safety rules, safety laws, regulations, standards, and practices
  • Ability to work various hours, including nights, early mornings, and weekends 
  • Ability to travel amongst various campuses and attend College events, on or off campus, as required.

Minimum Qualifications & Education

  • Required:
    1. Master of Science degree in Nursing from an accredited institution
    2. Active, unencumbered Compact RN License
    3. Three (3) years of asynchronous, higher education teaching experience
  • Preferred:
    1. Doctorate degree (DNP/PhD) from an accredited institution
    2. Five years (5) years of full-time hybrid or asynchronous higher education teaching experience

jobs.title: Instructor & Program Manager, SAAT Engineering
jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

The Instructor & Program Manager of SAAT Engineering will maintain a dual-role position as: A) an instructional faculty member and B) Program Manager responsibilities overseeing the Specialized Associate in Arts (SAAT) degrees in Engineering and other related academic programs as assigned. 

Observes college rules/regulations and state guidelines appropriate to the position and demonstrates the college's core values of Caring, Communicating, Collaborating, and Celebrating.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Work at least 35 hours per week, fall and spring semesters, consisting of 9 instructional hours (as assigned by supervisor; six hours reassigned from regular 15 instructional hour faculty load) with the balance being devoted to student support, college and community service, and program manager duties.  Base compensation covers additional hours beyond 35 per week that may be needed to fulfill program manager duties (such as recruitment events, program advising, etc.). 
  • Summer work hours will be no less than 65 hours total to perform program manager duties. 
  • Plan and carry out instructional duties that maximize student learning.
  • Develop and revise program curriculum, as needed, to the greatest extent possible within their area of expertise. 
  • Engage in program student recruitment and retention efforts. 
  • Coordinate practicum/internship on- and off-site student experiences, as needed. 
  • Ensure fiscal responsibility in the development and management of the schedule of classes and resource management in assigned budgets; monitor spending and approve expenditures according to established policies and procedures.
  • Collaborate with College partners in support of initiatives, such as articulation agreements.
  • Collaborate and plan with others across the College to support student enrollment and retention.
  • Track and analyze student performance, enrollments, transfer rates, and learning outcomes to make informed decisions regarding the status of academic programs and resource management (e.g., personnel and classroom resources)
  • Work collaboratively with other faculty to ensure academic quality while focusing on student retention and completion.
  • Collaborate on faculty and staff development initiatives.
  • Assist in the marketing of each program and the program course offerings.
  • Collaborate with other college departments regarding the development of related programs. 
  • Supervise employees as assigned. 
  • Serve on College committees as assigned.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Work experience in the subject matter area is required.
  • Ability to demonstrate proficiency in working with various virtual meeting platforms.
  • Experience in online course development and delivery is preferred.

ABILITIES/GENERAL: 

  • Promote a common purpose consistent with the College's stated goals and demonstrate a commitment to students and the learning environment.
  • Possess knowledge of general written standards and procedures utilized, and have the ability to read, interpret, and follow procedural and policy manuals related to the job tasks.
  • Demonstrate the ability to respond to supervision, guidance, and direction in a positive, receptive manner and follow stated policies.

Includes the ability to build &/or support a constructive team spirit where members are committed to the goals and objectives of the organization.
  • Plan, organize, and successfully multitask to meet multiple deadlines and frequently new work tasks within required timeframes. Proven flexibility to successfully work on a variety of projects quickly and accurately.

  • Ability to work various hours, including nights, early mornings, and weekends

jobs.title: Student Assistant, Enrollment Service Center
jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

This entry-level position offers a unique opportunity for a current student to gain valuable work experience while contributing to Lake Sumter State College's success. The Student Assistant will provide essential support, working closely with faculty and staff to ensure the efficient operation of departmental activities.

This is a part-time position with an expected commitment of 20-25 hours per week. The schedule will be flexible to accommodate the student’s academic and other responsibilities.

Responsible for demonstrating LSSC’s Caring, Communicating, Collaborating, and Celebrating values.

Students cannot work during class.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to, the following:   

• Communicate with admitted and prospective students via email, phone, text, and Zoom to guide them through enrollment
• Address inquiries about admissions deadlines, academic programs, orientation, transcripts, and Florida Residency, etc
• Follow up with students as necessary
• Perform additional duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Strong Organizational and multitasking skills.
  • Excellent Verbal and written communication skills.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
  • Demonstrated commitment to professionalism and confidentiality.

Competency-Based Education (CBE) Goals Addressed in this position:

  • Career and Self-Development
  • Communication
  • Professionalism
  • Teamwork

Minimum Qualifications & Education

  • Currently enrolled at Lake Sumter State College (min. 6 credit hours)
  • Currently, hold and maintain a minimum 2.0 GPA
  • Minimum age of 18

jobs.title: Instructor, Nursing ASN
jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

Maintain continued competence in assigned and related areas. Maintain a good working relationship with students, faculty, staff, and members of the community. Assist in the college’s recruitment and retention efforts. Assist with college governance by serving periodically on college committees. Observe college rules/regulations and state guidelines appropriate to faculty responsibilities. 

Join us in shaping the future of our students by fostering a supportive learning environment based on LSSC’s core values of Communication, Collaboration, Care, and Celebrate!

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to the following:   

  • Plan and carry out instructional duties that maximize learning by students.
  • Supervise students in accordance with program procedures, academic, and course-related concerns.
  • Teach assigned courses in accordance with course descriptions. Perform on-site clinical practice teaching at assigned hospitals.
  • Work a minimum of 35 hours per week, which includes 15 classroom hours, 10 office or student contact hours, and 10 hours as needed by the program/college.
  • Assist with registration and/or recruitment when requested.
  • Furnish each student with a course syllabus listing performance objectives, course expectations, grading procedures, withdrawal procedures, class attendance policies, and office phone and e-mail access.
  • Regularly examine the content of assigned courses and recommend changes to the LSSC supervisor if needed. Any additions, revisions, or supplemental materials incorporated into the course must be compliant with ADA accessibility standards and institutional accessibility requirements.
  • Function as a member of the faculty committee in developing the instructional program and educational philosophy of the college.
  • Attend all scheduled or called meetings by the President or Vice President of Academic Affairs, AVP Health Professions, and Dean of ASN unless excused by the administrator in charge.
  • Teach all classes for the full period as scheduled.
  • Evaluate student progress and achievement with clear methods presented in the course syllabus.
  • Utilize evaluation results for planning, instruction, counseling, and program modification.
  • Keep accurate and up-to-date records.
  • Submit grade reports and other required data on or before the deadline dates.
  • Resolve discipline problems within the sphere of responsibility.
  • Assist and counsel students as needed, including during office and campus hours.
  • Utilizes materials and equipment necessary to accomplish designated tasks.
  • Demonstrate knowledge of current instructional developments.
  • Regularly examines the content of assigned courses and recommends changes to the curriculum committee as needed.
  • Comply with appropriate administrative rules/regulations and Board Policy.
  • Participate in an annual evaluation process as specified by the Vice President of Workforce.
  • Participate in Commencement ceremonies and Nursing pinning ceremonies.
  • Maintain continuity of communication with students, community, faculty, staff, and supervisors through timely replies to meetings, phone calls, mail, and email requests.
  • Teach on multiple campus sites as needed.
  • Competent in computer proficiency (Coursework, grading, as well as basic Microsoft Office knowledge)
  • Creates/follows current Faculty Learning Outcomes (FLOs) as instructed by AVP General Education & Transfer Programs
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Demonstrate computer technology proficiency in Microsoft programs (Word, Excel, Teams, & PowerPoint)
  • Effectively communicate in both a virtual and physical environment
  • Ability to work well in a team environment
  • Ability to successfully demonstrate knowledge and expertise in the applied field

ABILITIES/GENERAL:

  • Promote a common purpose consistent with stated College goals and demonstrate a commitment to students and the learning environment.
  • Possess knowledge of general written standards and procedures utilized, and have the ability to read, interpret, and follow procedural and policy manuals related to the job tasks
  • Demonstrate the ability to respond to supervision, guidance, and direction in a positive, receptive manner and in accordance with stated policies.
  • Provide quality customer service by creating a welcoming and supportive environment.
  • Present a professional image in word, action, and attire.
  • Demonstrate professionalism in dealing with a diverse population while understanding and respecting each other’s views of the world, personalities, and working styles
  • Conduct oneself in a manner consistent with the College’s standards of ethical conduct.
  • Apply effective techniques to create working relationships with others to achieve common goals; successfully communicate and collaborate with others to achieve goals.
  • Demonstrate skills necessary to look at situations and processes critically to make recommendations for improvement.
  • Strong service orientation and ability to effectively work as a member or leader of a team by cooperating with others, offering to help others when needed, and considering larger organizational goals rather than individual concerns. Includes the ability to build &/or support a constructive team spirit where members are committed to the goals and objectives of the organization.
  • Plan, organize, and successfully multitask to meet multiple deadlines and frequently new work tasks within required timeframes. Proven flexibility to successfully work on diversified projects at a fast and accurate pace.
  • Effectively manage change and adaptability
  • Adhere to all workplace safety rules, safety laws, regulations, standards, and practices
  • Ability to work various hours, including nights, early mornings, and weekends 
  • Ability to travel amongst various campuses and attend College events, on or off campus, as required. 

Minimum Qualifications & Education

  • Required:
    1. Master of Science degree in Nursing from an accredited institution
    2. Active, unencumbered Florida RN or APRN License
    3. Two (2) most recent years of clinical experience.
  • Preferred:
    1. Doctorate degree (DNP/PhD) from an accredited institution
    2. Teaching experience in higher education

jobs.title: Accountant
jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

The Accountant is responsible for performing the general accounting and financial duties for the Colleges and LSSC Foundation, including recording the pre-award and post-award grants. Prepare journal entries and process accounting and budget transactions throughout the year. Performs a broad range of accounting duties that require knowledge of generally accepted accounting principles and Governmental Accounting Standards Board statements. Responsible for promoting and sustaining a collegial, respectful, and high-performing work environment for all employees. 

Responsible for demonstrating LSSC’s core values of Caring, Communicating, Collaborating, and Celebrating when interacting with students, employees, visitors, and community members.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to the following:   

  • Assist in preparing month-end and fiscal year-end closing and reporting processes in preparation for the Annual Financial Report for both the College and Foundation.
  • Assist in maintaining the property management database.
  • Assist in budget preparations.
  • Reconciliation of all general ledger accounts
  • Serve as backup for Accounts Payable processing/disbursing vendor checks when needed.
  • Prepare invoices and billings.
  • Process employee travel reimbursement requests according to LSSC policies and procedures.
  • Assist with the preparation of audit schedules.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

  • Knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
  • Excellent skills in Microsoft Office 365 (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and the ability to become proficient in MS Teams.
  • Excellent planning, organization, attention to detail, and skills; ability to anticipate outcomes.
  • Ability to use appropriate technology to organize, synthesize, and communicate data.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Demonstrate critical thinking skills, ability to deal with ambiguity, resolve complex problems, and effectively manage projects.
  • Ability to successfully develop and manage relationships at all levels of the organization and influence various stakeholders.
  • Ability to consult with, challenge, and influence management to align processes and practices with college objectives.
  • Ability to maintain discretionary judgment in dealing with confidential matters.
  • Ability to meet deadlines and work independently in a fast-paced multi-priority environment.
  • Ability to exhibit a professional, courteous demeanor.

Minimum Qualifications & Education

  • Required:
    1. Bachelor’s Degree in a relevant field from an accredited institution.

jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

Dynamic and Engaging Opportunity Awaits You! 

Are you ready to bring your expertise to life in the vibrant world of academia? Join our team as an Adjunct Instructor at Lake-Sumter State College (LSSC) where innovation meets education in an environment pulsating with energy and excitement!  LSSC Adjunct Instructors ignite the minds of our student body through dynamic lectures, interactive discussions, and hands-on experiences. 

Join us in shaping the future of our students by fostering a supportive learning environment based on LSSC’s core values of Communication, Collaboration, Care and Celebrate!

The passion for your expertise is the catalyst to a dynamic educational journey for our students and their future success.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to the following:   

  • Plan and carry out instructional duties that maximize learning by students.
  • Supervise students in accordance with program procedures, academic, and course-related concerns.
  • Teach assigned courses in accordance with course descriptions.
  • Assist with registration and/or recruitment when requested.
  • Syllabus must be submitted to the dean's office prior to or during the first week classes begin.
  • Ensure that each student receives a course syllabus detailing performance objectives, course expectations, grading procedures, withdrawal and attendance policies, and faculty office phone and email contact information.

  • Teaches all classes for the full period as scheduled.
  • Evaluate student progress and achievement with clear methods presented on course syllabus.
  • Utilize evaluation results for planning, instruction, counseling, and program modification.
  • Keep accurate and up-to-date records.
  • Submit grade reports and other required data on or before deadline dates.
  • Resolve discipline problems within the sphere of responsibility.
  • Assist and counsel students as needed.
  • Utilize material and equipment necessary to accomplish designated tasks.
  • Demonstrate knowledge of current instructional developments.
  • Regularly examine the content of assigned courses and recommend changes to the LSSC supervisor if needed.
  • Complies with appropriate administrative rules/regulations and Board Policy.
  • Participate in an annual evaluation process as specified by the Vice President of Academic Affairs.
  • Maintain continuity of communication with students, community, faculty, staff, and supervisors through timely replies to meetings, phone calls, mail, and email requests.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Adhere to all workplace safety rules, safety laws, regulations, standards, and practices

Minimum Qualifications & Education

Required: 

Master’s degree in the teaching discipline listed in this job description, with at least 18 graduate-level semester hours in the listed teaching discipline.

jobs.title: Student Assistant, Instructional Support -Nursing
jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

This entry-level position provides a current Lake-Sumter State College nursing student with an opportunity to gain valuable work experience while supporting instructional activities within the Nursing program. The Student Assistant provides peer support to nursing students and assists faculty with instructional activities, learning resources, technology, and classroom operations.

This is a part-time position with an expected commitment of 20–25 hours per week. The schedule will be flexible to accommodate the student's academic and other responsibilities. Students cannot work during scheduled class times.

Responsible for demonstrating LSSC's values of Caring, Communicating, Collaborating, and Celebrating.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Provide support to nursing students in designated subject areas through online, face-to-face, and group settings.
  • Continually develop and maintain knowledge of nursing subject areas and tutoring/support skills.
  • Assist students with the course's online learning system and related instructional technology.
  • Assist instructors with instructional activities, including test proctoring.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and welcoming learning environment.
  • Follow College and departmental procedures and policies.
  • Attend required training sessions and complete a professional development plan.
  • Maintain confidentiality of student and institutional information.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Strong organizational and multitasking skills
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment
  • Demonstrated commitment to professionalism and confidentiality

COMPETENCY-BASEDEDUCATION(CBE)GOALSADDRESSEDINTHISPOSITION:

  • Career and Self-Development
  • Communication
  • Professionalism
  • Teamwork

  • Currently enrolled in the 2nd through 4th semester of the Nursing program.
  • Recommendation from the Nursing Program Director.
  • Currently enrolled at Lake-Sumter State College with a minimum of 6 credit hours.
  • Maintain a minimum 2.0 cumulative GPA.
  • Must be at least 18 years of age.

jobs.title: Athletics - Assistant Coach
jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

The Assistant Coach will work closely with the head coaching staff and student-athletes to provide support. 

IMPACT STATEMENT: 

This position provides experience in sports management, equipment preparation, maintenance, and care. Assist in promoting and sustaining a collegial, respectful, and high-performing work environment and demonstrating LSSC’s core values of caring, communicating, collaborating, and celebrating.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to the following:    

  • Assist with daily operations, including practice/game day equipment set-up/breakdown; equipment and practice area maintenance, laundry of game uniforms, and assisting the coach with preparation and stats.  
  • Coordinate and manage practices and games.
  • Assist in the recruiting process of student-athletes who exhibit regard for character and excellence in their lives.  
  • Assist with teaching sound athletic fundamentals, which are merged with sound strategy that results in efficient performance by athletes. 
  • Foster good conduct by players and coaches by setting a good personal example.
  • Assist with ensuring safety in all aspects of the athletic programs. 
  • Support the head coach in monitoring equipment and facility needs and assist with maintenance and care of the convocation center.
  • Adhere to the policies and procedures provided by LSSC, FCSAA, and NJCAA.
  • Perform other duties as required.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Basic computer skills  
  • Knowledge of Microsoft applications; especially Word and Excel 
  • Customer service skills and etiquette in dealing with customers in person and on the phone 
  • Basic English and math skills are required for clerical work and ticket sales 
  • Ability to alphabetize and file  
  • Attention to detail and proficiency in organization are required  
  • Previous office experience preferred 

ABILITIES/GENERAL:

  • Promote a common purpose consistent with the College's stated goals and demonstrate a commitment to students and the learning environment.
  • Possess knowledge of general written standards and procedures utilized, and have the ability to read, interpret, and follow procedural and policy manuals related to the job tasks.
  • Demonstrate the ability to respond to supervision, guidance, and direction in a positive, receptive manner and follow stated policies.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service by fostering a welcoming and supportive environment.
  • Present a professional image in words, actions, and attire.
  • Conduct oneself in a manner consistent with the College’s standards of ethical conduct.
  • Apply effective techniques to establish and maintain working relationships, fostering collaboration to achieve common goals; effectively communicate and collaborate with others to achieve shared objectives.
  • Demonstrate the skills necessary to examine situations and processes, making recommendations for improvement critically.
  • Strong service orientation and ability to effectively work as a member or leader of a team by cooperating with others, offering to help others when needed, and considering larger organizational goals rather than individual concerns. Includes the ability to build &/or support a constructive team spirit where members are committed to the goals and objectives of the organization.
  • Plan, organize, and successfully multitask to meet multiple deadlines and frequently new work tasks within required timeframes. Proven flexibility to successfully work on various projects quickly and accurately.
  • Effectively manage change and adaptability.
  • Adheres to all workplace safety rules, safety laws, regulations, standards, and practices
  • Ability to work various hours, including nights, early mornings, and weekends 
  • Ability to travel amongst various campuses and attend College events, on or off campus, as required.
. 

Minimum Qualifications & Education

  • Required: 
    1. Associate's Degree
    2. Two years of coaching experience, preferably post-secondary education, high school, or elite level. 
  • Preferred:
    1. Bachelor’s Degree 
    2. Prior coaching and playing experience

include, but are not limited to the following:

jobs.title: Laboratory Assistant, Medical Laboratory Technology
jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

The MLT Laboratory Assistant is a support staff member who plays a key role in ensuring the smooth operation of labs within the MLT Program. This position is responsible for preparing, setting up, and breaking down laboratory sessions, ensuring that all equipment, materials, and instructional resources are ready for use and properly stored afterward. The role includes maintaining an accurate inventory of supplies, monitoring stock levels, and coordinating the ordering and restocking of materials to support ongoing instructional needs.


Responsible for demonstrating LSSC’s core values of Caring, Communicating, Collaborating, and Celebrating when interacting with students, employees, visitors, and community members.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

include, but are not limited to the following:   

  • Maintain inventory records by keeping track of stock levels, locations, use, warranty, and maintenance of equipment and supply items.
  • Manage, track, process, report, and reconcile supply orders and receiving reports for MLT labs.
  • Manage student laboratory supplies.
  • Assist with budget preparations of laboratory supplies.
  • Assist clinical faculty in the set-up and tear-down of laboratory supplies. 
  • Maintain a list of hazardous materials, monitor material levels, and process requests for removal.
  • Notify vendors of any repair, maintenance, and replacement of equipment.
  • Perform other duties as assigned, including assistance with other Health Professions labs as appropriate.
  • Ensure lab environment is clean, safe, and orderly on a daily basis. 

CLERICAL:

  • Calendar management: Schedules appointments and maintains the calendar.
  • Preparation of correspondence.
  • Inventory document preparation and organization of files.
  • Organizes office operations and procedures, acquisitions, distribution, and store supplies.
  • Schedules/coordinates meetings and room set up as necessary.
  • Assist in establishing work procedures and standards to improve efficiency and effectiveness of operations while improving customer service.
  • Exemplify core values and provide excellent customer service to members of the general public and other LSSC employees.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office and database development/entry.
  • Organized and detail-oriented.
  • Problem-solving skills.
  • Initiative to follow and enforce standard lab safety guidelines.
  • Required to wear protective clothing such as goggles, gloves, closed-toed shoes, etc.
  • Advanced ability to communicate effectively both verbally and electronically.
  • Strong time management skills.
  • Demonstrate respect and confidentiality.
  • Works effectively with minimal supervision, applying strong interpersonal skills and maintaining flexibility to work irregular hours when required.

ABILITIES/GENERAL:

  • Promote a common purpose consistent with the College's stated goals and demonstrate a commitment to students and the learning environment.
  • Possess knowledge of general written standards and procedures utilized, and have the ability to read, interpret, and follow procedural and policy manuals related to the job tasks.
  • Demonstrate the ability to respond to supervision, guidance, and direction in a positive, receptive manner and follow stated policies.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service by fostering a welcoming and supportive environment.
  • Present a professional image in words, actions, and attire.
  • Conduct oneself in a manner consistent with the College’s standards of ethical conduct.
  • Apply effective techniques to establish and maintain working relationships, fostering collaboration to achieve common goals; effectively communicate and collaborate with others to achieve shared objectives.
  • Demonstrate the skills necessary to critically examine situations and processes, making recommendations for improvement.
  • Strong service orientation and ability to effectively work as a member or leader of a team by cooperating with others, offering to help others when needed, and considering larger organizational goals rather than individual concerns. Includes the ability to build &/or support a constructive team spirit where members are committed to the goals and objectives of the organization.
  • Plan, organize, and successfully multitask to meet multiple deadlines and frequently new work tasks within required timeframes. Proven flexibility to successfully work on a variety of projects quickly and accurately.
  • Effectively manage change and adaptability.
  • Adheres to all workplace safety rules, safety laws, regulations, standards, and practices
  • Ability to work various hours, including nights, early mornings, and weekends 
  • Ability to travel amongst various campuses and attend College events, on or off campus, as required.

Minimum Qualifications & Education

  • Required:
    1. Associate's degree from an accredited institution.
      • Upon evaluation, degree requirements and/or experience can be considered by the Hiring Manager or AVP of Health Professions.
    2. 1 year of similar laboratory or supply management experience.
  • Preferred:
    1. Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
