Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Manager Claims supports Insurance Company of the West’s mission to create the best insurance experience by driving operational excellence, ensuring regulatory compliance, and fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and service. This position leads a high‑performing team responsible for delivering exceptional claim outcomes and  customer experience. The manager ensures performance metrics are met while partnering closely with internal stakeholders to reduce claim costs, improve injured worker outcomes, and strengthen policyholder relationships. This role works cross functionally to drive the overall claims strategy. This position will oversee the Claims Support Services department, guiding strategic initiatives, supporting team development, and ensuring consistent, effective service delivery across all areas of responsibility. This role will lead a team of Claims Support Services Supervisors, fostering a collaborative, customer-focused environment while developing future leaders to deliver high-quality service and operational excellence across the claims department.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Operational Excellence

  • Monitors key performance indicators (KPIs) such as claim duration, reserve accuracy, litigation rates, and customer satisfaction.
  • Analyzes trends and provide actionable insights to improve outcomes and reduce loss costs.
  • Partners with Quality Assurance, Training, and other internal teams to strengthen processes and elevate claim quality.
  • Supports audits, compliance reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives.

 

Customer & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Builds strong relationships with policyholders, brokers, medical providers, and legal partners to support claim resolution and service excellence.
  • Collaborates with Underwriting, Risk Management, and Safety to address claim drivers and support policyholder retention.
  • Ensures clear, timely communication with injured workers to support recovery and return‑to‑work efforts.

 

Cross‑Functional Collaboration

  • Works closely with other Claims managers to ensure consistency, alignment, and shared best practices across the department.
  • Participates in strategic planning, department initiatives, and enterprise projects that enhance ICW Group’s claims operations.

Claims Oversight & Strategy

  • Oversee the full lifecycle of workers’ compensation claims, ensuring timely, accurate, and compliant handling.
  • Ensure adherence to jurisdictional requirements and ICW Group best practices.

Develops and leads a team of claims professionals to ensure daily operational success

  • Provides guidance to Team Members. Communicates Mission, Values, and other organization operating principles to direct reports.
  • Establishes and maintains the overall work cadence and, in partnership with department leadership, ensures performance and outcomes strive for excellence in delivery and customer experience.  Ensures that the entire team is engaged and that leadership practices encourage development, recognition, and retention.
  • Establishes and adheres to hiring criteria, on-boarding, and training requirements for incoming staff.
  • Manages performance and supports Team Member development through goal setting, coaching, and ongoing feedback for direct reports.
  • Acts as a resource for team members to answer questions and solve complex problems.
  • Manages budget, technology and other resources, workload, and customer requests for Department services. 
  • Maintains compliance with all Company policies, procedures, and assigned responsibilities.
  • Safeguards data quality, follows IT security guidelines, and monitors risk-related metrics.

 

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Directly supervises 2 or more employees within the Claims team and carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. These responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; conducting performance and salary reviews; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems; coaching, mentoring, and developing team members to further their skills and knowledge; creating and monitoring development plans; setting performance expectations/goals; forecasting staffing needs and planning for peak times and absences; enforcing department policies and procedures.

 

 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university (or equivalent combination of education and experience) along with a minimum of 5+  years’  related workers’ compensation claims experience required. At least one year supervisory or management experience of claims professionals required; may require claims adjuster experience (depending upon the team this position will lead).  Prior multi-state claims insurance with experience managing high volume caseloads.

 

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Insurance Education Association (IEA) Certificate, Workers Compensation Claims Professional (WCCP) Accreditation preferred. Chartered Property Casualty Underwriter (CPCU) designation a plus.

 

 

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Good computer skills with MS Office products, claims management systems,  databases with the ability to learn new software programs and tools
  • Advanced understanding of Workers’ Compensation claims principles and applications
  • Solid interpersonal skills with the ability to develop good working relationships
  • Excellent  communication skills (verbal/written), time management and organizational skills.
  • Must be able to effectively present information to direct reports, peers, management and public forums.  
  • Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.
  • Experience with process improvement methodologies, optimizing workflows and operational excellence programs
  • Demonstrated ability to distill complex information into clear, actionable guidance.
  • Must have data‑driven decision‑making and a high level of attention to detail.
  • Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment. Travel up to 15% is required.

Seeking Workers' Compensation Claims Examiners. Training will be provided for handling California jurisdiction.


The Claims Examiner position handles a variety of claims with a focus on providing the highest level of service for policyholders and ICW Group to bring claims to an equitable conclusion within Company standards and best practice guidelines. The Claims Examiner works with a sense of urgency, understands insurance coverage concepts, and navigates the legal system with the support of counsel to drive strategic outcomes.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Manages all aspects of a moderately complex claims inventory

  • Effectively communicates with policyholders, agents, attorneys, and witnesses to gather information and provide the highest possible level of customer service.
  • Promptly investigates claims to determine exposure, works with appropriate experts and makes strategic recommendations.
  • Utilizes appropriate resolution tactics (e.g., mediation, negotiation, denial, litigation or offer) to proactively drive outstanding results.
  • Operates within the requirements of related state and/or the governing entity rules and regulations as well as internal claims handling policies and procedures. 
  •  Partners with defense counsel throughout the litigation process in line with ICW litigation guidelines while monitoring legal fees and costs

 All Claims Examiners:

  • Consistently provides exceptional customer service
  • Effectively collaborates with cross-functional Team Members for project and process discussions
  • Makes recommendations for streamlining processes
  • Ensures accuracy of data in claims system for compliance with applicable regulatory reporting
  • Provides knowledge transfer across the organization
  • Continuously seeks to improve technical skills by attending job related training and tracking current case law 

Workers’ Compensation Claims (Specific Responsibilities):

  • Prepares and presents claims status reports for internal and external stakeholders
  • Administers timely and appropriate benefits to injured workers; manages and approves payment of benefits within designated authority level.  Works within applicable state rules, regulations as well as ICW Group’s internal claims handling policies and procedures.
  • Creates and adjusts reserves in a timely manner to ensure reserving activities are consistent with company policies
  • Resolves claims fairly and equitably, acting in the best interest of the insured while providing timely benefits to injured workers as required by law

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibility


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree (or equivalent combination of education and experience) required along with a minimum 1- 4+ years’ related claims or claims handling experience.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Workers’ Compensation: Certification that meets the minimum standards of training, experience, and skill required. WCCA and WCCP preferred. State Workers Compensation License is required in some branches.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Basic to good understanding of laws and jurisdictional restraints to manage claims
  • Excellent verbal communication skills, time management, attention to detail and organizational skills
  • Must be adept at learning new technology
  • Flexibility to adapt to changes in a fast-paced environment

Must have the ability to:

  • Read, analyze, and interpret technical and legal documents
  • Write reports and business correspondence
  • Respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers (insured), claimants and regulatory agencies
  • Present information at meetings, to management and clients
  • Solve practical problems and deal with a variety of variables in situations where limited standardization exists

Workers’ Compensation: Knowledge of workers’ compensation claims handling, reserving, litigation management, and resolution strategies

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

jobs.title: AVP, Actuarial & Pricing Analytics
jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!



ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Establishes and upholds department direction and vision.

  • Leads the establishment of vision and direction for the actuarial and pricing analytics department, in collaboration with senior leadership.
  • Represents the company in business settings and regularly with external parties, including regulators and industry groups.
  • Responsible for developing new business processes or comprehensive analytic efforts.
  • Ensures that the work product supports business growth and profitability.
  • Takes responsibility to extensively modify processes in order to improve accuracy and efficiency.
  • Invokes critical thought process to solve complex problems and identify dependencies in processes to enable direction of staff.
  • Ensures soundness of actuarial and pricing analytics analyses and consistency with Standards of Practice.
  • Advises senior and executive leadership on enterprise-wide actuarial and pricing analytics strategy, risk, and emerging issues.

 

Partners with business leaders to provide expertise on business efforts.

  • Partners with senior business leaders in administering multiple lines of business or other areas of responsibility similar in scope and complexity.
  • Organizes and coordinates actuarial efforts with business leaders to develop and implement new products and expand into new markets.
  • Fosters positive, collaborative working relationships with senior executive leaders across the organization.
  • Acts as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) for actuarial and pricing analytics matters at the enterprise level.
  • Prepares and communicates actuarial findings to business leaders.

 

Develops and manages a team of Credentialed Actuaries, Pricing Analytics Professionals, and Actuarial Analysts

  • Provides direction to team. Communicates Mission, Values and other organization operating principles to the team.
  • Establish high standards for the delivery of services and products rendered, resulting in excellent customer experience.  Ensures that the entire team is engaged and that leadership practices encourage development, recognition and retention.
  • Oversee team performance and development, including performance management, development planning, and coaching for direct reports. 
  • Acts as a resource for team members to answer questions and solve complex problems.
  • Manages budget, technology and other resources, workload and customer requests for services.  Ensures adherence to all Company policies and procedures and Compliance responsibilities
  • Instills awareness of regulatory industry compliance, Actuarial Standards of Practice, and ICW standards on AI systems and data used for modeling.

 

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position directly supervises employees, potentially including Managers and/or Directors, within the Actuarial and Pricing Analytics department and carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. These responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; conducting performance and salary reviews; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems; coaching, mentoring, and developing team members to further their skills and knowledge; creating and monitoring development plans; setting performance expectations/goals; forecasting staffing needs and planning for peak times and absences; enforcing department policies and procedures.

 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university required in Applied Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, Economics or related field.  Advanced degrees in related fields preferred.
  • Minimum 10 years of related experience, including demonstrated experience managing multiple lines of business or enterprise-wide initiatives; or, equivalent combination of education and experience.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Associate of the Casualty Actuary Society (ACAS) required. Fellow of the Casualty Actuary Society (FCAS), Certified Specialist in Predictive Analytics (CSPA) or Data Science certifications preferred.

 

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Strong communication, interpersonal skills and proven leadership ability. Thorough knowledge of actuarial and pricing analytics models and knowledge of commercial lines of business. Experience managing complex projects, resources and staff. Broad company and industry experience and expertise, with the ability to work collaboratively with other business leaders to solve complex business problems. Ability to mentor and train actuarial staff. Ability to take actuarial and pricing analytics ownership of multiple lines of business. Ability to shape and drive the strategic vision of the actuarial and pricing analytics department and broader enterprise. Demonstrated ability to build credibility and influence outcomes with senior executive leadership.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

#LI-Hybrid


The current range for this position is

$171,301.18 - $306,632.68

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses. If hired at ICW Group, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors unique to each candidate, including experience, education and the location of the role and considers employees performing substantially similar work.


WHY JOIN ICW GROUP?

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference
  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging
  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match
  • Bonus potential for all positions
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid holidays throughout the calendar year
  • Want to continue learning? We’ll support you 100% 


ICW Group is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. ICW Group will not discriminate against an applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex/gender, age, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Procurement Product & Operations Specialist plays a key role in driving the successful development and delivery of innovative products that meet the needs of the department and align with the company’s strategic goals. This role acts as the bridge between business stakeholders, development teams and end-users, ensuring clear communication and effective prioritization of features and enhancements throughout the product lifecycle.  


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Drives organizational goals and maximizes the value of the PVMS Technology.

  • Defines and communicates the continuous refinement of the PVMS technology vision and growth opportunities so that the highest possible value is leveraged; ensures users have effective and efficient access to relevant information.
  • Reviews current manual processes within PVMS and identifies ways to transition these processes to the PVMS technology platforms.
  • Participates in the review of all PVMS project, process and technology support requests and/or improvements to systems, ensuring both process and system requirements are fully identified, evaluated, tested, implemented and aligned with PVMS strategic priorities.
  • Works closely with leaders and IT to ensure the successful execution of the product roadmap.
  • Leads orchestration of key sourcing and third-party risk processes to ensure consistency in identification, prioritization and execution of delivery.
  • Oversees technical requirements specific to application configuration.
  • Recognizes the opportunities current technology provides and assesses its impact on business practices.  This includes leading the understanding of processes, documenting gaps and recommending ways to use the current technology while providing suggestions of new technology and workflows.
  • Accountable for each stage of the development process and the final product, evaluating progress and performance at each iteration and collaborates on the decision to move on to the next steps.
  • Oversees the data analytics and reporting functionalities and capabilities, ensuring information required to make decisions is available and easily accessible.
  • Anticipates product’s future needs by maintaining user personas and journey maps.
  • Owns and drives user-centric product outcomes collaboratively with business and IT leadership.

Fosters effective procurement operations, infrastructure and leads continuous improvement to ensure alignment with company initiatives.

  • Achieves baseline cycle times and performs retrospectives to ensure continuous improvement and iterative improvement of process and/or technology.
  • Assesses current practices and recommends continuous improvement processes/products based on data analysis and best practices to achieve targeted metrics for strategic sourcing and third-party risk success.
  • Supports the department in identifying and resolving operational challenges.
  • Drives business process design and improvement projects.
  • Introduces industry best practices through the development of center of excellence capabilities, including training and knowledge sharing.
  • Builds process excellence awareness across the department and with team members and leaders.
  • Supports and guides the organization through transformation, standardization and faster execution.
  • Assists in the development and maintenance of procurement policies, procedures, and guidelines for the company’s strategic goals.
  • Handles PVMS technology support & administration, including day to day issue resolution; ensures delivery of high-quality customer service to end users.
  • Drives data integrity within the PVMS Technology systems; oversees and maintains user security, and implements audit, research, and resolution processes.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree required in Business, Finance, Computer Science, Engineering, Supply Chain Management, or related field.
  • Minimum 7 years of related experience inclusive of leading product implementations, collecting business needs, and translating requirements to a technical audience.
  • Extensive experience implementing, maintaining and administering Source to Pay platforms such as Coupa, Ariba, Zycus, etc. 
  • Experience with procurement, contracts and third party risk in the financial services or insurance industry highly desired.
  • Experience as a Product Owner or similar role with the ability to successfully launch and manage products or platforms.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

  • Six Sigma certification or training preferred.
  • Certifications in procurement and supply management preferred, i.e. Senior Professional in Supply Management (SPSM), Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM), Certified Procurement Professional (CPP), Certified Supply Chain Professional (CSCP), Certified Professional Purchasing Manager (CPPM). Experience in SaaS technology or cloud preferred.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Demonstrated advanced skills in implementing and managing source to pay and third-party risk applications.
  • Knowledge of Agile processes and principles.
  • Understanding of the Insurance industry.
  • Ability to map value stream across business lines.
  • Possess technical expertise and understanding of product development practices.
  • Ability to balance technical constraints and a differentiated product that meets the needs of the marketplace.
  • Knowledge of mobile and web platform design conventions and technology limitations and opportunities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, experience working with cross-functional teams, and presenting to leadership.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications including Word, Visio, Excel, Project, and PowerPoint.
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills.
  • Advanced analytical, qualitative, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to apply critical thinking and analytical skills to recommend creative solutions to business and technical challenges.
  • Strong attention to detail. Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.


WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.


We are currently not offering employment sponsorship for this opportunity

#LI-Hybrid

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses. If hired at ICW Group, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors unique to each candidate, including experience, education and the location of the role and considers employees performing substantially similar work.


WHY JOIN ICW GROUP?

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference
  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging
  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match
  • Bonus potential for all positions
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid holidays throughout the calendar year
  • Want to continue learning? We’ll support you 100% 


ICW Group is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. ICW Group will not discriminate against an applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex/gender, age, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of the Managing Attorney is to oversee the operational aspects for the Litigation Management team working closely with the department Director.  This role will create, manage and improve operational processes, as well as assist with budget planning, financial measures and results. The Managing Attorney will identify and lead initiatives to improve the team’s efficiency and ensures effective communication between the legal and business teams.  This role acts as both a Litigation Attorney with a reduced case count and manages a staff of Litigation team members.  The position works autonomously and under the general supervision of the Litigation Management’s department Director.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Directs the operations of law office personnel providing litigation and legal services.

  • Oversees law office operations to ensure efficient operations of In-House Counsel.
  • Contributes to strategic business decisions to achieve company goals.
  • Ensures the firm is achieving its client satisfaction goals by evaluating productivity and quality of service. 
  • Identifies, makes recommendations for work process improvements and follows through to implement remediations. 
  • Works with management to ensure the department meets financial and ROI goals, identifies trends, prepares reports, and implements modifications as needed.
  • Mentors less experienced attorneys, law clerks, paralegals and assistants to help them advance in the field of law by continuing to expand their knowledge, skills and abilities.

Provides litigation services and is responsible for all aspects of assigned Workers’ Compensation matters.

  • Handles a reduced caseload of litigated files and ensures files are fully worked and moved to resolution.
  • Litigates workers’ compensation cases in California before all state and federal courts, administrative boards, and other court proceedings.
  • Represents ICW Group, its related entities and insureds before administrative boards, state and federal courts, Court of Appeal, and the California Supreme Court.
  • Analyzes complex legal and factual issues; conducts extensive, well-reasoned legal research, as necessary; independently develops and presents defense strategies on behalf of ICW Group.
  • Provides strategic legal advice, recommendation, and implementation of clear, cost-effective, and efficient plans of action.
  • Assists in analyzing, reviewing, and distributing information on new legislation, regulations, and court decisions.

Provides oversight of a team of Litigation Management professionals.

  • Supervises and evaluates, mentors, motivates, and develops associate attorneys, paralegals, law clerks, hearing representatives, and support staff to strengthen our legal team.
  • Communicates clear performance expectations for associate attorneys, paralegals, law clerks, hearing representatives, and support staff as well as providing support and guidance for achieving expectations.
  • Expands the substantive expertise of associate attorneys, paralegals, law clerks, hearing representatives.
  • Communicates and enforces team values including mission statement of In House Counsel (IHC) and ICW.
  • Establishes and maintains the overall work cadence and, in partnership with Department leadership, ensures performance and outcomes strive for excellence in delivery and customer experience.
  • Acts as a resource for team members to answer questions and solve complex problems.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Directly supervises employees within the Litigation Management team and carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of the Information Security Engineer IV is to design secure architectures and develop cybersecurity approaches and techniques for the security of all ICW related systems and infrastructure. This position will assist with strategic initiatives for short and long-term plans to identify and reduce the attack surface across applications and systems. The Information Security Engineer IV will drive the architecture to monitor and defend ICW Group’s technology against potential threats that jeopardize the financial growth and security goals of the Company.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Monitors, defends and drives improvements for ICW Group IT Information Security.

  • Monitors networks and systems for security breaches, using software that detects intrusions and anomalous system behavior and develops strategies to respond to and recover from a security breach. 
  • Identifies gaps in the technical tool/technology suite and makes recommendations
  • Leads security incident response, including preparation, detection, analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery.
  • Researches and implements methods to remediate network and application security vulnerabilities.
  • Leads and participates in security architecture controls reporting, compliance audits, monthly and ad-hoc statistics and trends, and risk-focused reports including internal and 3rd party Risk Assessments.
  • Utilizes automated tools to identify, assess, and report security concerns, with emphasis placed on effective communication to stakeholders. Takes an active lead to inform, advise, and partner with business units to help better secure operations.

Leads complex security endeavors.

  • Overseas complex security projects and issues.
  • Develops a set of security standards to respond to and recover from a security breach.
  • Provides support by proposing solutions, coordinating implementation, and enforcing information systems security policies, standards, and methodologies.
  • Uses advanced technologies including Intrusion Detection & Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS), Firewalls, SIEM, Antivirus, Network Packet Analyzers, Malware analysis and forensics tools to detect intrusions, breaches in compliance, etc.
  • Prepares and analyses system security reports by collecting, analyzing, and summarizing data and trends and makes recommendations to improve security.
  • Maintains operational security posture for an information system or program to ensure information system security policies, standards, and procedures are established and followed.
  • Creates and updates technical security standards for assets and software.

Serves as cyber security technical subject matter expert for the organization.

  • Provides information security expertise to system development teams throughout the life cycle process.
  • Partners with systems engineering teams to ensure system design and implementation are consistent with company policies, requirements, and directives.
  • Conducts risk assessments, penetration tests and diagnoses internet/extranet security, intrusion attempts, and cyber-crime response.
  • Leads and conducts information security risk assessments including documenting processes, service level agreements and best practices.
  • Develops the overall security design, development, testing and implementation of security solutions. Recommends compliance strategies that support customer requirements and alignment to company policy.
  • Ensures security quality, adherence to security guidelines, profitability, and information security related metrics for self and assigned projects.
  • Collaborates with key stakeholders on remediation strategies and follows remediation activities through closure.

Partners with project management and other internal teams in determining overall security solutions.

  • Prepares and presents comprehensive reports and recommendations to senior management and stakeholders on security-related matters.
  • Develops and implements comprehensive security architectures encompassing all areas of IT and business technology for ICW Group using standard and advanced security measures.
  • Works with peers, cross functional architecture leadership, and other internal groups to drive technical security risk down in targeted areas while ensuring adherence to ICW architecture standards.
  • Coaches and educates others to increase early detection rates and decrease IT risk and security.
  • Documents as is state of information security. Keeps current on industry trends, principles, and thought to define long range technology transitions. 
  • Performs end to end full stack reviews of current or incoming technologies for ITSEC compliance.
  • Ensures that proposed and existing technology architectures are aligned with organizational security goals and objectives.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibility but may mentor and train junior engineers.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's Degree from four-year college or university required with major or emphasis Engineering, Cybersecurity, Networking, or Computer Science related discipline.
  • Minimum 10 years of experience working in a security engineering related role designing secure networks, systems and application architectures or equivalent combination of education and experience required.
  • Minimum 3-5 years of experience in AWS Cloud Security services preferred.
  • Direct experience using advanced technologies such as Intrusion Detection & Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS), Firewalls, SIEM, Antivirus software, Network Packet Analyzers, content filtering, Malware analysis and forensics tools to detect intrusions.
  • Experience in cyber security role requiring knowledge of data analysis, risk assessment, risk mitigation, investigation methods, incident management concepts and practices, and policy and procedure development.
  • Experience with AWS Services such as AWS Identity & Access Management, AWS Organizations, AWS Security HuB, Guard Duty, CloudTrail, AWS CloudTrail.
  • Experience with LLM-based applications, document intelligence, automated data extraction, or AI systems processing structured or unstructured enterprise data preferred. 
  • Understanding of LLM applications, AI-enabled workflows, data pipelines, data handling, and human-review practices preferred.
  • Experience with AI/ML platforms, generative AI, LLM applications, data pipelines, AI-enabled automation, or analytics environments preferred. 

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Certification in GSEC, CISSP, and/or Security+ preferred. AWS Certified Security – Specialty, preferred.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Strong knowledge of risk assessment tools, technologies, and methodologies.
  • Knowledge of disaster recovery, computer forensic tools, technologies, and methods.
  • Knowledge of enterprise security platforms. 
  • Ability to communicate network security issues to peers and management.
  • Ability to read and use the results of mobile code, malicious code, and anti-virus software.
  • Strong understanding of endpoint security solutions to include File Integrity Monitoring and Data Loss Prevention.
  • Demonstrated experience as a lead engineer in the design, implementation and support in an enterprise IT environment.
  • Ability to apply principles of logical or scientific thinking to a wide range of intellectual and practical problems. 
  • Ability to hypothesize on root cause of inefficiencies and then test out probable solutions against those hypotheses.
  • Must be able to read, write and speak English effectively.
  • Ability to effectively communicate/present technical information to a non-technical audience.
  • Ability to cross train and share information with team members.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.  Employees are required to reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.  Employees must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds.  Employees are required to have visual acuity and be capable of operating and viewing computers and other electronic devices for extended periods of time.


WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of the Information Security Engineer III is to design secure architectures and develop cybersecurity approaches and techniques to protect ICW Group’s cloud, data, and/or AI-driven environments. This position will assist with strategic initiatives for short and long-term plans to identify and reduce the attack surface across applications and systems. This role partners closely with application, cloud, data, and analytics teams to ensure security is embedded into systems from design through production

This role supports ICW’s modern data initiatives by reducing risk, strengthening security controls, and enabling secure adoption of new technologies in a highly regulated insurance environment. The engineer contributes across vulnerability management, threat detection, and incident response while providing practical security guidance that balances risk, compliance, and business needs.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Monitoring, Detection, and Incident Support

  • Monitors cloud, on-prem, and SaaS environments for security threats using SIEM, EDR, cloud-native logging, and network telemetry.
  • Assists with security incident response activities, including investigation, containment, remediation, and post-incident analysis.
  • Researches and implements methods to remediate network and application security vulnerabilities.
  • Leads and participates in security architecture controls reporting, compliance audits, monthly and ad-hoc statistics and trends, and risk-focused reports including internal and 3rd party Risk Assessments.
  • Produce risk-focused security findings and communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Conducts threat hunting and root-cause analysis to identify anomalous behavior, exploitation attempts, and indicators of compromise.
  • Investigates potential data misuse, data exfiltration, and anomalous access patterns using logs, DLP, and monitoring tools.

Cloud & Generalist Security Responsibilities.

  • Prepares and analyses system security reports by collecting, analyzing, and summarizing data and trends and makes recommendations to improve security.
  • Serve as a senior technical contributor across cloud security, including IAM, logging, monitoring, detection, and secure deployment patterns.
  • Lead or contribute to vulnerability management across cloud infrastructure, applications, containers, and data platforms.
  • Participate in offensive and defensive security activities, including threat modeling, red team exercises, blue team detection improvements, and threat hunting.
  • Support incident response investigations involving cloud misconfigurations, data exposure, and/or AI-related security events.
  • Perform security architecture reviews and provide guidance to engineering teams to reduce risk while enabling business objectives.
  • Implement and improve security controls that strengthen ICW’s overall security posture while supporting modern cloud and data initiatives.

Security Architecture, Standards, and Risk

  • Partners with Engineering, Infrastructure, Cloud, Data, and Operations teams to embed security into system design and delivery.
  • Lead security reviews for new data, analytics, and/or AI initiatives, including architecture reviews and risk assessments prior to production deployment.  
  • Conduct threat modeling and security design reviews for systems involving data, analytics, AI, and/or cloud services.
  • Create and maintain technical security standards and guardrails related to data protection, cloud usage, and/or AI security.
  • Partner with internal teams to remediate security findings and track remediation activities through closure.

The purpose of this job is to serve as the first point of contact to process new injuries reported by customers. This position exists to ensure that initial requests from customers are handled thoughtfully and thoroughly, while following Company standards and procedures.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Provides excellent customer service as the first point of contact for customers.

  • Receives and intakes new initial claim documentation either via phone, e-mail, or fax and enters into claim systems.
  • Responds to insureds in a timely manner.
  • Directs questions to the appropriate contact in the department. 

Inputs new claims into enterprise resource planning (ERP) system as well as creates written documentation including physical file for manual storage.    

  • Reviews insurance policy information to determine coverage.
  • Completes data entry for all first reports of injury.
  • Determines severity of injuries and advises the appropriate levels of staff within standard operating procedures. 

Communicates with insureds, agents, internal and external stakeholders, as necessary. 

  • Assists examiners in contacting insureds or other involved persons to obtain missing or incomplete information to process claim.
  • Receives and/or returns telephone calls as directed by claim examiner.
  • Responds to insureds, agents or outside participants, as directed.
  • Processes incoming mail and other administrative duties relating to claims.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

High school diploma or general education degree (GED) required.  Minimum 1 year of related experience and/or training; or, equivalent combination of education and experience.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

None required.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Working knowledge or familiarity with customer service techniques, principles and practices.  Insurance industry understanding, a plus. Ability to read, write and comprehend simple instructions, short correspondence, and memos. Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to customers, clients, and other employees of the organization. Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals.  Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percent and to draw and interpret bar graphs.

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB 

The Manager, Organizational Change Management leads the people-side adoption capability within the Strategy & Transformation Office. This role establishes and operates a repeatable OCM methodology that helps the organization prepare for, adopt, and sustain changes to business processes, systems, roles, ways of working, and operating models. The role ensures major initiatives are supported by change impact assessments, stakeholder engagement, communication and training plans, readiness measures, and adoption metrics, so transformation outcomes are realized and sustained after delivery. 


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 


Builds and Leads the Enterprise OCM Capability 

  • Defines and maintains the enterprise change management methodology, standards, templates, and artifacts used across major initiatives. 
  • Establishes consistent expectations for change impact assessment, stakeholder analysis, sponsor alignment, readiness planning, communication, training, adoption measurement, and reinforcement. 
  • Builds OCM capability across project teams, business leaders, people managers, and change practitioners through coaching, tools, and repeatable practices. 

Leads Change Strategy and Adoption Planning 

  • Partners with portfolio, architecture, delivery, business, HR, and communications leaders to identify the operational and people impacts of each major initiative. 
  • Develops change strategies and plans that support adoption of new processes, systems, roles, policies, organizational structures, and ways of working. 
  • Ensures initiatives entering governance and delivery have clear change risks, stakeholder impacts, readiness needs, communication plans, training plans, and adoption success measures. 

Drives Stakeholder Engagement, Communication, Training, and Readiness 

  • Creates stakeholder maps, engagement plans, sponsor roadmaps, communication plans, training strategies, and readiness assessments for enterprise initiatives. 
  • Coaches executives, sponsors, people managers, and project leaders on their roles in leading change and supporting impacted teams through transition. 
  • Coordinates with HR, Internal Communications, Training, business leaders, and delivery teams to align messaging, learning, timing, and reinforcement activities. 

Measures Adoption and Reinforces Sustained Change 

  • Defines adoption, readiness, utilization, proficiency, sentiment, and reinforcement metrics for major initiatives. 
  • Monitors change progress and identifies adoption risks, resistance patterns, training gaps, and reinforcement needs. 
  • Reports change readiness and adoption health into STO governance forums so adoption outcomes are reviewed alongside delivery, portfolio, and architecture metrics. 

Leads OCM Team Operations and Continuous Improvement 

  • Plans and manages OCM capacity, work intake, prioritization, and resource assignment across the transformation portfolio. 
  • Maintains OCM artifacts, playbooks, lessons learned, and reusable assets to improve consistency and speed across initiatives. 
  • Identifies opportunities to improve change governance, stakeholder engagement, communications, training, and adoption measurement practices. 

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES 

May directly supervise change management practitioners, analysts, communications/training resources, or adoption specialists as the function matures. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws, including interviewing, hiring, training, planning and assigning work, coaching and developing staff, setting performance expectations, conducting performance reviews, addressing issues, and managing team capacity and priorities. 


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 

  • Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university required, preferably in Business Administration, Organizational Development, Communications, Human Resources, Psychology, Information Systems, or a related field; Master's degree preferred. 
  • Minimum 8 years of progressive experience in organizational change management, business transformation, organizational development, communications, training, or related transformation roles. 
  • Experience leading change management for enterprise technology, process, operating model, or business transformation initiatives. 
  • Experience coaching executives, sponsors, people managers, and project teams through complex organizational change. 

CERTIFICATES AND LICENSES 

Prosci Change Management Certification or equivalent OCM credential required. ACMP Certified Change Management Professional (CCMP), PMP, SAFe, Agile, or related transformation certification preferred. 


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS 

  • Strong knowledge of structured change management methodologies, tools, and practices, including stakeholder analysis, impact assessment, readiness planning, communication, training, adoption, and reinforcement. 
  • Ability to translate complex transformation objectives into practical change strategies that help employees understand, adopt, and sustain new ways of working. 
  • Excellent executive communication, facilitation, coaching, stakeholder engagement, and influence skills. 
  • Strong analytical skills and ability to define and use adoption, readiness, utilization, proficiency, and sentiment metrics to guide interventions. 
  • Comfort working across business, technology, HR, communications, training, portfolio, and delivery teams in a matrixed environment. 
  • Ability to manage change fatigue, resistance, competing priorities, and stakeholder concerns with sound judgment and practical mitigation plans. 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

This job operates in a professional office environment. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently will sit, stand, walk, and bend during working hours. Requires manual and finger dexterity and eye-hand coordination. May be required to lift light objects. Requires normal or corrected vision and hearing corrected to a normal range. 


WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

This role establishes and operates a repeatable OCM methodology that helps the organization prepare for, adopt, and sustain changes to business processes, systems, roles, ways of working, and operating models. The role ensures major initiatives are supported by change impact assessments, stakeholder engagement, communication and training plans, readiness measures, and adoption metrics, so transformation outcomes are realized and sustained after delivery. 
 ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Builds and Leads the Enterprise OCM Capability 
 Defines and maintains the enterprise change management methodology, standards, templates, and artifacts used across major initiatives. 
 Establishes consistent expectations for change impact assessment, stakeholder analysis, sponsor alignment, readiness planning, communication, training, adoption measurement, and reinforcement. 
 Builds OCM capability across project teams, business leaders, people managers, and change practitioners through coaching, tools, and repeatable practices. 
 Leads Change Strategy and Adoption Planning 
 Partners with portfolio, architecture, delivery, business, HR, and communications leaders to identify the operational and people impacts of each major initiative. 
 Develops change strategies and plans that support adoption of new processes, systems, roles, policies, organizational structures, and ways of working. 
 Ensures initiatives entering governance and delivery have clear change risks, stakeholder impacts, readiness needs, communication plans, training plans, and adoption success measures. 
 Drives Stakeholder Engagement, Communication, Training, and Readiness 
 Creates stakeholder maps, engagement plans, sponsor roadmaps, communication plans, training strategies, and readiness assessments for enterprise initiatives. 
 Coaches executives, sponsors, people managers, and project leaders on their roles in leading change and supporting impacted teams through transition. 
 Coordinates with HR, Internal Communications, Training, business leaders, and delivery teams to align messaging, learning, timing, and reinforcement activities. 
 Measures Adoption and Reinforces Sustained Change 
 Defines adoption, readiness, utilization, proficiency, sentiment, and reinforcement metrics for major initiatives. 
 Monitors change progress and identifies adoption risks, resistance patterns, training gaps, and reinforcement needs. 
 Reports change readiness and adoption health into STO governance forums so adoption outcomes are reviewed alongside delivery, portfolio, and architecture metrics. 
 Leads OCM Team Operations and Continuous Improvement 
 Plans and manages OCM capacity, work intake, prioritization, and resource assignment across the transformation portfolio. 
 Maintains OCM artifacts, playbooks, lessons learned, and reusable assets to improve consistency and speed across initiatives. 
 Identifies opportunities to improve change governance, stakeholder engagement, communications, training, and adoption measurement practices. 
 SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES 
 May directly supervise change management practitioners, analysts, communications/training resources, or adoption specialists as the function matures. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws, including interviewing, hiring, training, planning and assigning work, coaching and developing staff, setting performance expectations, conducting performance reviews, addressing issues, and managing team capacity and priorities. 
 EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 
 Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university required, preferably in Business Administration, Organizational Development, Communications, Human Resources, Psychology, Information Systems, or a related field; Master's degree preferred. 
 Minimum 8 years of progressive experience in organizational change management, business transformation, organizational development, communications, training, or related transformation roles. 
 Experience leading change management for enterprise technology, process, operating model, or business transformation initiatives. 
 Experience coaching executives, sponsors, people managers, and project teams through complex organizational change. 
 CERTIFICATES AND LICENSES 
 Prosci Change Management Certification or equivalent OCM credential required. ACMP Certified Change Management Professional (CCMP), PMP, SAFe, Agile, or related transformation certification preferred. 
 KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS 
 Strong knowledge of structured change management methodologies, tools, and practices, including stakeholder analysis, impact assessment, readiness planning, communication, training, adoption, and reinforcement. 
 Ability to translate complex transformation objectives into practical change strategies that help employees understand, adopt, and sustain new ways of working. 
 Excellent executive communication, facilitation, coaching, stakeholder engagement, and influence skills. 
 Strong analytical skills and ability to define and use adoption, readiness, utilization, proficiency, and sentiment metrics to guide interventions. 
 Comfort working across business, technology, HR, communications, training, portfolio, and delivery teams in a matrixed environment. 
 Ability to manage change fatigue, resistance, competing priorities, and stakeholder concerns with sound judgment and practical mitigation plans. 
 PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 
 This job operates in a professional office environment. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently will sit, stand, walk, and bend during working hours. Requires manual and finger dexterity and eye-hand coordination. May be required to lift light objects. Requires normal or corrected vision and hearing corrected to a normal range. 
 WORK ENVIRONMENT 
 This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB




ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Leads enterprise data governance support.

  • Leads the development and maintenance of metadata repositories and management systems (data catalog).
  • Performs advanced non-technical tool configuration within the Data Catalog, including complex Catalog UI, Templates, Terms/Glossaries, and Data Asset Curation.
  • Oversees documentation of data assets and their relationships in the data catalog.
  • Creates, enforces, and updates metadata standards and policies in the data catalog.
  • Leads collaboration efforts with teams to capture and maintain accurate metadata.
  • Implements and optimizes metadata governance processes.
  • Develops and delivers comprehensive training on metadata management best practices.
  • Oversees creation and maintenance of data quality documentation.
  • Establishes and maintains data governance metrics.
  • Collaborates with data owners and stewards to manage data definitions, quality, and usage.
  • Drives the use of insurance industry and ICW specific nomenclature/naming standards within all data assets including, but not limited to reports, meta data articles, and project documentation.

Provides data quality issue management and remediation.

  • Collaborates with team members throughout business and technical departments to document data quality issues.
  • Develops and implements data quality standards, data protection standards and adoption requirements across the enterprise.
  • Works with business partners to gather and understand functional requirements, develops queries and provides reports.
  • Ensures that a backlog of issues is consistently refined and updated for agile consumption.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibility.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's Degree from a four-year college or university required in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems, or related field. Master’s degree preferred.
  • Minimum 4-7 years of experience in data governance, metadata management, or related field required.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

CDMP (Certified Data Management Professional-Practitioner or Master), Certified Data Governance & Stewardship Professional (DGSP) from ICCP (Institute for Certification of Computing Professionals), or other Data Governance Certification (DGQP) preferred.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Advanced SQL experience, including performance tuning and complex queries.
  • Extensive experience with SaaS platforms.
  • Proven track record in implementing and managing data catalog and metadata management systems.
  • Familiarity with spreadsheet tools (e.g., Excel) for data manipulation.
  • Knowledge of insurance industry preferred.
  • Strong analytical and time management skills.
  • Must be organized, detail oriented, and able to multi-task.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Experience in leading small to medium-sized projects or teams.
  • Team-oriented focus; ability to conduct effective meetings with business and project teams.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.


WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of the Senior Managing Litigation Attorney is to oversee a team of attorneys ranging from entry level to seasoned senior litigation management attorneys.  This position is responsible for overseeing and reviewing work performed by attorneys to ensure compliance with defense counsel guidelines.  The role works to improve processes, as well as assists with budget planning, financial measures and results. The Senior Managing Attorney will identify and lead initiatives to improve the team’s efficiency and ensures effective communication between the legal and business teams.  This role acts as both a Litigation Attorney with a reduced case count and manages a staff of Litigation attorneys. The position works autonomously and under the general supervision of the Litigation Management’s department Director.

This is a hybrid position, offering the flexibility to work from both home and the office. Candidates must be able to work from one of our California branch offices in San Diego, Pasadena, or Rancho Cordova.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Directs the operations of law office personnel providing litigation and legal services.

  • Oversees the law office activities to ensure efficient operations of In-House Counsel.

  • Determines the intake and assignment of cases to ensure distribution based on each attorney’s level of expertise and associated location (region or county).  

  • Achieves the departments and company goals by making strategic business decisions.

  • Ensures the firm is achieving its client satisfaction goals by evaluating productivity and quality of service. 

  • Identifies, makes recommendations for work process improvements and follows through to implement remediations. 

  • Works with leadership to ensure the department meets financial and ROI goals, identifies trends, prepares reports, and implements modifications as needed.

  • Mentors less experienced attorneys and ensures the team continues to expand their job-related knowledge, skills and abilities.

  • Regularly reviews cases and provides feedback on legal strategies, compliance with deadlines, timeliness on response, and maximizing the department’s core goals.

Provides litigation services and is responsible for all aspects of assigned Workers’ Compensation matters.

  • Handles a reduced caseload of litigated files and ensures files are fully worked and moved to resolution.

  • Litigates workers’ compensation cases in California before all state and federal courts, administrative boards, and other court proceedings.

  • Represents ICW Group, its related entities and insureds before administrative boards, state and federal courts, Court of Appeal, and the California Supreme Court.

  • Analyzes complex legal and factual issues; conducts extensive, well-reasoned legal research, as necessary; independently develops and presents defense strategies on behalf of ICW Group.

  • Provides strategic legal advice, recommendation, and implementation of clear, cost-effective, and efficient plans of action.

  • Assists in analyzing, reviewing, and distributing information on new legislation, regulations, and court decisions.

Provides oversight of a team of Litigation Management professionals.

  • Oversees the entire employee lifecycle from identifying, training, coaching and retaining talent.

  • Supervises and evaluates, mentors, motivates, and develops attorneys to strengthen the legal team.

  • Communicates clear performance expectations for the assigned team as well as providing support and guidance for achieving the department’s metric, billable hours and expectations.

  • Communicates and enforces team values including mission statement of In-House Counsel (IHC) and ICW.

  • Establishes and maintains the overall work cadence and, in partnership with Department leadership, ensures performance and outcomes strive for excellence in delivery and customer experience.

  • Acts as a resource for team members to answer questions and assist in the solution to complex problems.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Directly supervises employees within the Litigation Management team and carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. These responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; conducting performance and salary reviews; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems; coaching, mentoring, and developing team members to further their skills and knowledge; creating and monitoring development plans; setting performance expectations/goals; forecasting staffing needs and planning for peak times and absences; enforcing department policies and procedures.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree from four-year college or university required.  Juris Doctorate from an accredited law school required. 

  • Minimum 10 years’ workers’ compensation legal experience handling complex cases along with a minimum of 2 years’ experience managing associate through senior litigation attorneys.  

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Licensed and in good standing with the State Bar of California with no history of public or private reprisals.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Good computer skills with MS Office (including MS Excel with the ability to create financial/performance reports). 

  • Proficient in the use of applications/programs to create automated reports, templates, systems and data retrieval of high quality and reliability. 

  • Expert knowledge litigating California workers’ compensation matters with trial experience and prior experience handling cases with varying degrees of complexity. 

  • Deep understanding of workers’ compensation administrative rules, laws, statutes, legal principles and practices. 

  • Excellent communication skills (verbal/written). 

  • Ability to communicate effectively with external and internal team members, clients, businesses, and members of the State Bar and Judiciary, including effectively responding to concerns and sensitive matters. 

  • Ability to effectively present information, verbally and in writing, to clients, claims personnel, top management, public groups, Board of Directors, mediators, arbitrators, judges, and juries.

  • Skilled at logical thinking to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. 

  • Consistently maintains professional and appropriate demeanor, works harmoniously with others and responds positively to feedback.

  • Demonstrated experience in working independently under minimal supervision, maintaining a strong work ethic, and exercising initiative.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office, home, and court environment and requires frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, scanner, and other standard office equipment.  The position requires traveling to various court locations and works at one of the offices of In-House Counsel on a weekly basis.

This description is a general statement of essential job functions and responsibilities. The position may include other duties as assigned.

We are currently not offering employment sponsorship for this opportunity

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses.   • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference
  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging
  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match

Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Triage Examiner serves as the initial point of contact and manages claims during the early phase of the claim lifecycle (typically the first 10 days) in alignment with Company standards, best practices, and applicable laws and regulations. With a strong sense of urgency, the Triage Examiner drives early intervention to positively influence claim outcomes, optimize efficiency, and ensure a smooth transition to the next specialized claim examiner for ongoing management, while establishing a professional and positive tone that supports effective claim handling.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONIBILITIES

  • Manages the early phase of the claims lifecycle by administering benefits to injured workers in accordance with statutory case law as well as pertinent regulations for the first 10 days of the claim.

  • Contacts and interviews injured workers, witnesses, medical providers, attorneys, agents, and policyholders to obtain information necessary for claim investigation and decision-making.

  • Communicates claim activity and processing with the injured worker and policyholder.

  • Makes initial compensability recommendations and evaluates benefit eligibility within assigned authority in accordance with applicable state laws and regulations, as well as ICW Group’s internal claims handling policies and procedures.

  • Creates  reserves in a timely manner consistent with company standards and best practices guidelines.

  • Establishes accurate claim setup, including coding, documentation, and file notes, in alignment with Company standards.

  • Identifies risks, complexities, or escalation needs and refers matters to leadership as appropriate.

  • Develops initial action plans and sets claim diaries to support effective claim handling and transition.

  • Ensures a seamless and timely transition of claims to the next specialized claim examiner, including clear documentation, defined next steps, and appropriate claim direction.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • High school diploma or general education degree (GED) required.  Bachelor’s degree from four-year college or university preferred.

  • Minimum 2-3 years’ insurance claims such as auto, property, liability, workers’ compensation or related experience required. 

  • At least 1+ year(s) of experience as a Triage Claims Associate or in a closely related workers’ compensation claim’s role.

  • Bilingual in Spanish preferred.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

  • California Only: All examiners must receive certification (Self Insurance (SIP) or Workers’ Compensation Claims Examiner designation) that meets the minimum standards of training, experience, skill, and further education as required. 

  • All other jurisdictions: State Workers’ Compensation License as required.

  • Must obtain certifications within 1 year of hire into this role.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Basic understanding of laws and jurisdictional restraints to manage injuries.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, time management and organizational skills. 

  • Requires a high level of attention to detail. 

  • Team oriented and a sense of urgency for execution.

  • Able to resolve conflicts fairly and equitably.

  • Problem solving and decision-making ability.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

We are currently not offering employment sponsorship for this opportunity

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses. If hired at ICW Group, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors unique to each candidate, including experience, education and the location of the role and considers employees performing substantially similar work.


WHY JOIN ICW GROUP?

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference
  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging
  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match
  • Bonus potential for all positions
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid holidays throughout the calendar year
  • Want to continue learning? We’ll support you 100% 


ICW Group is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. ICW Group will not discriminate against an applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex/gender, age, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.
