jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


ABOUT ICW GROUP 

ICW Group is a national, multi-line insurance carrier with an AM Best rating of 'A', approximately 1,300 employees, and headquarters in San Diego, California. ICW Group is executing an enterprise AI strategy that treats AI as core infrastructure: built on a single enterprise platform, governed by a single framework, and deployed under regulatory oversight from day one. As AI moves into underwriting, claims, and operational decisions, disciplined governance is what allows ICW to adopt AI quickly and defensibly. 

ABOUT THE AI GOVERNANCE OFFICE 

The AI Governance Management Office is ICW's standing execution and coordination function for artificial intelligence, sponsored by the SVP and Chief Digital and AI Officer. It serves the AI Governance Executive Committee (AIGEC) as its operational arm, turning AIGEC's policy, risk, and approval decisions into coordinated, well-governed delivery. The Office is the single operational home for AI intake, prioritization, coordination, enablement, and transparency.  

The Office is also ICW's single coordination point for NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool response preparation. California, ICW's domiciliary state, is participating in the 2026 NAIC pilot, which creates an active compliance window for the organization's higher-risk AI systems in underwriting and claims. 

PURPOSE OF THE JOB   

The AI Governance Manager is an advanced professional individual contributor within the AI Governance Management Office, reporting to the Director of Cloud, AI, ML, and Enablement Platforms. This dedicated position works independently with limited oversight to administer, facilitate, and execute AI governance day to day: coordinating the governance committees, operating the intake-to-decision workflow, owning the AI Hub, and maintaining the governance artifacts and evidence that keep ICW audit-ready and regulator-ready.  

Working closely with leadership and management at all levels, control functions, business owners, and external stakeholders, the AI Governance Manager makes governance practical and efficient so that teams move through it rather than around it. AIGEC and its subcommittees set policy, risk tolerance, and approvals; this role translates those decisions into consistent, well-documented execution, leads governance projects and processes, and provides guidance, coaching, and review of work products contributed by lower-level professionals and cross-functional partners. 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 

Governance Operations and Lifecycle Management 

  • Coordinate and administer AIGEC and its AI Risk & Compliance and Third-Party AI Governance subcommittees: run the cadence (intake triage, risk review, forums), prepare review packs, and document decisions and action items to closure. 

  • Operate the intake-to-decision workflow -- apply the risk taxonomy (Tier 0 through Tier 4), move each use case through the lifecycle gates with required signoffs and triggered control-function reviews, resolve intake or escalation issues, and maintain the decision log, exception register, and escalation paths. 
     

Policy, Standards, Controls, and Inventory 

  • Maintain the AI policy, standard, procedure, and control library with clear owners and review cadence, coordinate rollout of the policy suite (including the prohibited-use list), keep governance templates current, support control sufficiency testing for Tier 1 and Tier 2 systems, and recommend process and control enhancements that improve governance performance across the function. 

  • Administer the AI Systems Registry as the single audit-ready inventory of AI use cases, models, agents, and vendor AI, enforce the registry gate before build or deploy, guide business and technical owners through registry requirements, and coordinate model and system cards with lineage and classification for higher-risk systems. 

AI Hub Ownership 

  • Own and operate the AI Hub on SharePoint as the enterprise's single front door for AI serving approximately 1,300 employees -- intake, approved tools, responsible-use guidance, governance materials, learning, and metrics -- managing the content lifecycle and running it as the interface between AIGEC and the workforce. 

NAIC Regulatory Compliance Coordination 

  • Serve as the NAIC Response Coordinator, or lead significant portions of the response, for California DOI AI Systems Evaluation Tool inquiries, coordinate cross-functional evidence collection, maintain the artifacts serving Exhibits A through D (AI Systems Registry, model cards, AI Data Element Registry with Data Services, and the risk classification methodology), and track readiness and related policy updates as the pilot evolves. 

Monitoring, Audit Readiness, and Reporting 

  • Operate the governance KPI and KRI dashboard and produce reporting for AIGEC and executive leadership, assemble audit-ready evidence packs for Tier 1 systems, run regulatory scanning (NIST AI RMF, NAIC, ISO/IEC 42001, state AI laws), and route material changes into policy and control updates with operational recommendations. 

Training, Awareness, and Change Management 

  • Coordinate role-based AI governance training, attestation, and change-triggered learning, support the governance champion network and cultural-change activities, and provide guidance, coaching, and review of governance work products to reinforce clear ownership and consistent governance behavior. 
     

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES 

This role does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Information Technology, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.  

  • Minimum of ten years of experience in program or project management, governance, risk, or compliance operations within a technology, IT, or regulated environment. 

  • Demonstrated experience independently operating a governance, risk, or compliance program, including committee coordination, decision logging, evidence management, escalation management, and cross-functional process improvement. 

  • Experience with AI/ML programs, digital transformation, or technology transformation initiatives, or a strong record of ramping quickly on new governance domains. 

  • Advanced facilitation, stakeholder-management, and influencing skills, with the ability to navigate technical and business audiences at all levels of the organization, and influence practices, procedures, and policies at an operational level 

  • Proficiency with collaboration and tracking tools such as Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, or equivalent, and experience with SharePoint content management. 

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to produce executive-level packs, dashboards, regulatory response materials, and reporting. 

  • Extensive working understanding of governance frameworks and compliance requirements in regulated industries, including the impact of governance decisions on business, technology, risk, and control functions 

  • Experience in the insurance or financial services industry preferred. 

  • Familiarity with AI governance frameworks: NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, the NAIC AI Model Bulletin, and the NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool (Exhibits A through D) preferred. 

  • Experience with NAIC regulatory requirements or Department of Insurance examination processes preferred. 

  • Familiarity with the AI and ML platforms in use at ICW (AWS Bedrock, Snowflake Cortex) and enterprise AI tools (Claude Enterprise, Microsoft 365 Copilot) preferred. 

  • Experience with SharePoint site design and enterprise portal management. 

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS  

  • Risk, audit, or governance certification such as CRISC or CGEIT, or a project and program management certification such as PMP or PgMP, or SAFe / Lean Portfolio Management preferred. 

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS 

  • Governance Discipline: Advanced ability to operate and improve governance processes, cadence, controls, and evidence, so decisions are defensible, repeatable, and scalable across the enterprise. 

  • Facilitation: Ability to run committees, reviews, and cross-functional decisions across diverse technical and business teams, and to influence operational practices, procedures, and policies within and outside the immediate job function. 

  • Detail Orientation: Meticulous attention to governance artifacts, compliance documentation, and registry data integrity. 

  • Communication: Ability to synthesize technical, business, and regulatory information into clear, actionable materials for business owners, control functions, vendors, and executive leadership. 

  • Ownership and Project Leadership: Self-directed execution across multiple concurrent governance workstreams in a fast-paced environment. 

  • Adaptability: Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to establish structure and process where none exists. 

  • Regulatory Awareness: Genuine interest in AI regulation and responsible AI, and in keeping ICW's posture current as expectations evolve. 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS   

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk and hear.  

WORK ENVIRONMENT   

This position is based at ICW Group's Innovation Point campus in San Diego, CA. Occasional collaboration with remote team members and external partners via Microsoft Teams may be required. This position observes standard business hours with flexibility to support cross-time-zone engagements as needed. 
 

This description is a general statement of essential job functions and responsibilities. 

The position may include other duties as assigned. 

We are currently not offering employment sponsorship for this opportunity.

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses. WHY JOIN ICW GROUP?

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference
  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging
  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match
  • Bonus potential for all positions
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid holidays throughout the calendar year
  • Want to continue learning? We’ll support you 100%

The Claims Examiner works with a sense of urgency, understands insurance coverage concepts, and navigates the legal system with the support of counsel to drive strategic outcomes.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Manages all aspects of a moderately complex claims inventory

  • Effectively communicates with policyholders, agents, attorneys, and witnesses to gather information and provide the highest possible level of customer service.

  • Promptly investigates claims to determine exposure, works with appropriate experts and makes strategic recommendations.

  • Utilizes appropriate resolution tactics (e.g., mediation, negotiation, denial, litigation or offer) to proactively drive outstanding results.

  • Operates within the requirements of related state and/or the governing entity rules and regulations as well as internal claims handling policies and procedures. 

  •  Partners with defense counsel throughout the litigation process in line with ICW litigation guidelines while monitoring legal fees and costs

 All Claims Examiners:

  • Consistently provides exceptional customer service

  • Effectively collaborates with cross-functional Team Members for project and process discussions

  • Makes recommendations for streamlining processes

  • Ensures accuracy of data in claims system for compliance with applicable regulatory reporting

  • Provides knowledge transfer across the organization

  • Continuously seeks to improve technical skills by attending job related training and tracking current case law 

Workers’ Compensation Claims (Specific Responsibilities):

  • Prepares and presents claims status reports for internal and external stakeholders

  • Administers timely and appropriate benefits to injured workers; manages and approves payment of benefits within designated authority level.  Works within applicable state rules, regulations as well as ICW Group’s internal claims handling policies and procedures.

  • Creates and adjusts reserves in a timely manner to ensure reserving activities are consistent with company policies

  • Resolves claims fairly and equitably, acting in the best interest of the insured while providing timely benefits to injured workers as required by law

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibility

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree (or equivalent combination of education and experience) required along with a minimum 1- 4+ years’ related claims or claims handling experience.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Workers’ Compensation: Certification that meets the minimum standards of training, experience, and skill required. WCCA and WCCP preferred. State Workers Compensation License is required in some branches.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Basic to good understanding of laws and jurisdictional restraints to manage claims

  • Excellent verbal communication skills, time management, attention to detail and organizational skills

  • Must be adept at learning new technology

  • Flexibility to adapt to changes in a fast-paced environment

Must have the ability to:

  • Read, analyze, and interpret technical and legal documents

  • Write reports and business correspondence

  • Respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers (insured), claimants and regulatory agencies

  • Present information at meetings, to management and clients

  • Solve practical problems and deal with a variety of variables in situations where limited standardization exists

Workers’ Compensation: Knowledge of workers’ compensation claims handling, reserving, litigation management, and resolution strategies

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this role is to develop, manage, and grow a profitable book of business within assigned line(s) of business, while serving as a senior-level underwriting and distribution partner to agents and internal stakeholders.

Senior Business Development Underwriters are responsible for underwriting more complex risks within assigned line(s) of business (e.g., Workers’ Compensation or Commercial Package and its component coverages) and are expected to operate with a higher level of autonomy, authority, and judgment. In addition, this role plays a key leadership role in driving broader Commercial Lines growth by identifying cross-sell opportunities, promoting all Company products, and supporting agency and distribution strategy.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Underwriting & Portfolio Management

  • Underwrite, select, and price moderately complex to complex risks within assigned line(s) of business in accordance with Company guidelines

  • Maintain accountability for the profitability, growth, and retention of assigned portfolio

  • Evaluate detailed risk characteristics including operations, financials, management, and loss history

  • Exercise advanced underwriting judgment and authority to structure, price, and manage complex accounts

  • Utilize underwriting authority to apply appropriate pricing, credits/debits, deductibles, and alternative rating structures

  • Quote and explain complex pricing structures (e.g., retros, deductibles, large account programs) where applicable

  • Monitor portfolio performance and take proactive corrective action to achieve underwriting targets

  • Remain current on regulatory, rating, and coverage changes (e.g., WCIRB/NCCI, ISO/AAIS)

Business Development, Production & Distribution

  • Drive new business production and achieve growth objectives through proactive agency engagement, prospecting, and cross-sell execution

  • Develop, manage, and optimize a high-performing producer force aligned with Company strategy

  • Hold producers accountable for production, quality, and profitability expectations

  • Drive profitable sales across all Commercial Lines products, including increasing penetration of existing products and supporting new product introductions

  • Actively identify and lead cross-sell opportunities, partnering across underwriting teams to deliver total account solutions

  • Prospect, prequalify, and appoint new producers with strong alignment to target business segments

  • Set and manage production goals and performance expectations with key agency partners

  • Maintain deep knowledge of assigned territory, including competitor positioning and market dynamics

  • Influence and provide input on distribution strategy, product positioning, and market opportunities

Producer & Relationship Management

  • Serve as a lead Company representative with key and strategic agency partners

  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships through regular agency engagement, presentations, and strategic planning

  • Lead complex account and pricing discussions with agents and insureds

  • Provide underwriting and distribution guidance to agents, including structuring solutions for more complex risks

  • Deliver high levels of responsiveness, service, and professionalism in all interactions

  • Present agency performance insights, growth opportunities, and strategic recommendations to internal leadership and agency partners

Leadership & Mentorship

  • Mentor and support the development of Business Development Underwriters and junior staff

  • Provide guidance on underwriting approach, agency management, and deal structure

  • Participate in training, onboarding, and knowledge sharing across the team

  • Contribute to special projects, product initiatives, and process improvements as assigned

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but is expected to mentor, influence, and provide guidance to junior team members.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.
Minimum 5 years underwriting experience required; 7+ years preferred, with demonstrated experience handling more complex risks and agency relationships.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Current driver’s license required.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Demonstrated success in building and managing high-value agency relationships and driving profitable growth

  • Proven ability to underwrite complex risks and apply advanced underwriting judgment

  • Strong business development, negotiation, and relationship management skills

  • Ability to balance advanced underwriting discipline within assigned line(s) of business with production and cross-sell expectations across Commercial Lines

  • Ability to evaluate submissions, financials, and loss data to support complex decision-making

  • Advanced knowledge of Commercial Lines products, including Workers’ Compensation and/or Commercial Package and its component coverages

  • Ability to mentor, coach, and influence others

  • Strong analytical, communication, and presentation skills

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

  • Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

  • Role requires 50%-75% travel to meet with clients, attend industry events, and develop new business opportunities.

  • Travel is usually limited to automobile but occasional air travel is required.

  • Requires regular visits to outside locations such as producer's offices.

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

  • This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment. Requires the ability to work 20-30% of time from home.

This description is a general statement of essential job functions and responsibilities.

The position may include other duties as assigned.

We are currently not offering employment sponsorship for this opportunity.

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses.   • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference
  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging
  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match
  • Bonus potential for all positions
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid holidays throughout the calendar year
  • Want to continue learning? We’ll support you 100%

jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our  journey as we strive to transform the insurance  carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.

Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for ten consecutive years as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our  internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Quality Engineer II is an established, technical professional who serves as the Quality Engineering lead for their assigned delivery team. This role takes complete ownership of the test strategy, planning, and quality outcomes for the team, ensuring that quality is engineered into every stage of the software delivery lifecycle. Working independently with limited supervision, the QE II drives shift-left practices within the team, builds and maintains automated test solutions, and sets quality objectives that directly impact department results. The role requires practical depth in test engineering, the ability to solve difficult and moderately complex problems by drawing from prior experience, and the capacity to coordinate quality activities, delegate tasks, and coach junior team members.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the complete test strategy and test planning for the assigned Projects – defining scope, approach, risk assessment, entry/exit criteria, and test coverage targets for each release and sprint.

  • Act as the QE lead within the team and drive quality discussions during grooming, sprint planning, and design reviews; set quality objectives; and ensure the team delivers against them.

  • Develop, execute, and maintain comprehensive test plans, test cases, and test scripts for functional, regression, integration, API, and exploratory testing.

  • Build, maintain, and extend automated test suites using frameworks such as Playwright for UI, Postman/Newman for API, following clean code practice.

  • Execute API-level testing including payload validation, error handling, and contract verification for in-house and third-party service integrations.

  • Contribute automated tests to CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions), supporting continuous testing across regression, smoke, and feature validation stages.

  • Validate data integrity across integrated systems including ETL pipelines, data transformations, and end-to-end data reconciliation.

  • Identify, record, and thoroughly document defects; perform root cause analysis by reviewing logs, stack traces, and database states to diagnose systemic issues.

  • Participate in code reviews to provide quality-focused feedback on testability, error handling, and edge-case coverage.

  • Recommend enhancements to testing processes, tools, and standards to improve efficiency and effectiveness within the POD and broader team.

  • Own test data management, mock services, and QA environment configurations for reliable, repeatable test execution.

  • Leverage AI tools to assist in test case generation, coverage analysis, and failure triage.

  • Track and report quality metrics including defect density, escape rate, test coverage, and automation progress. Uses data to influence quality decisions.

  • Coordinate quality activities with distributed teams and offshore/nearshore vendor partners on test assignments, status calls, and triage.

  • Coach, guide, and review the work of junior team members; provide training on quality engineering practices and tools.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but may mentor and/or train less experienced members.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, or related field (or equivalent experience); 3+ years in quality engineering or software testing with 2+ years in test automation.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

N/A

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Practical, hands-on proficiency in at least one programming language (Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript) with the ability to read, understand, and debug production code.

  • Demonstrated experience designing test strategies and owning end-to-end test planning for a product, team, or release.

  • Hands-on experience building and maintaining automated tests using Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, REST Assured, or Postman/Newman.

  • Solid understanding of API testing concepts: request/response validation, status codes, error handling, and RESTful service patterns.

  • Working knowledge of SQL and database concepts – ability to write queries for data validation, verify data transformations, and support ETL testing.

  • Experience contributing automated tests to CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions) and understanding of continuous testing principles.

  • Familiarity with version control (Git), branching strategies, and pull request workflows.

  • Understanding of the test automation pyramid and strategic allocation of coverage across unit, API, UI, and data layers.

  • Exposure to performance testing concepts and tools (JMeter, k6, or equivalent).

  • Awareness of AI-assisted testing tools and willingness to adopt AI workflows for test generation and defect analysis.

  • Solid understanding of Agile/Scrum practices, shift-left testing, and the software development lifecycle.

  • Ability to work independently on moderately complex assignments with limited supervision; strong problem-solving skills drawing from prior experience and analysis.

  • Good communication skills; able to influence within the team and communicate with contacts within and occasionally outside the department.

  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate quality tasks, delegate work, and review the output of junior team members.

  • Preferred skills include strong Insurance domain background, specifically in Claims Management and/or Insurance Billing business workflows.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.  Employees are required to reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.  Employees must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds.  Employees are required to have visual acuity and be capable of operating and viewing computers and other electronic devices for extended periods of time.

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

 Own test data management, mock services, and QA environment configurations for reliable, repeatable test execution.
 Leverage AI tools to assist in test case generation, coverage analysis, and failure triage.

At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our  journey as we strive to transform the insurance  carrier space. Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for ten consecutive years as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our  internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this role is to develop, manage, and grow a profitable book of business within assigned line(s) of business, while serving as a senior-level underwriting and distribution partner to agents and internal stakeholders.

Senior Business Development Underwriters are responsible for underwriting more complex risks within assigned line(s) of business (e.g., Workers’ Compensation or Commercial Package and its component coverages) and are expected to operate with a higher level of autonomy, authority, and judgment. In addition, this role plays a key leadership role in driving broader Commercial Lines growth by identifying cross-sell opportunities, promoting all Company products, and supporting agency and distribution strategy.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Underwriting & Portfolio Management

  • Underwrite, select, and price moderately complex to complex risks within assigned line(s) of business in accordance with Company guidelines

  • Maintain accountability for the profitability, growth, and retention of assigned portfolio

  • Evaluate detailed risk characteristics including operations, financials, management, and loss history

  • Exercise advanced underwriting judgment and authority to structure, price, and manage complex accounts

  • Utilize underwriting authority to apply appropriate pricing, credits/debits, deductibles, and alternative rating structures

  • Quote and explain complex pricing structures (e.g., retros, deductibles, large account programs) where applicable

  • Monitor portfolio performance and take proactive corrective action to achieve underwriting targets

  • Remain current on regulatory, rating, and coverage changes (e.g., WCIRB/NCCI, ISO/AAIS)

Business Development, Production & Distribution

  • Drive new business production and achieve growth objectives through proactive agency engagement, prospecting, and cross-sell execution

  • Develop, manage, and optimize a high-performing producer force aligned with Company strategy

  • Hold producers accountable for production, quality, and profitability expectations

  • Drive profitable sales across all Commercial Lines products, including increasing penetration of existing products and supporting new product introductions

  • Actively identify and lead cross-sell opportunities, partnering across underwriting teams to deliver total account solutions

  • Prospect, prequalify, and appoint new producers with strong alignment to target business segments

  • Set and manage production goals and performance expectations with key agency partners

  • Maintain deep knowledge of assigned territory, including competitor positioning and market dynamics

  • Influence and provide input on distribution strategy, product positioning, and market opportunities

Producer & Relationship Management

  • Serve as a lead Company representative with key and strategic agency partners

  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships through regular agency engagement, presentations, and strategic planning

  • Lead complex account and pricing discussions with agents and insureds

  • Provide underwriting and distribution guidance to agents, including structuring solutions for more complex risks

  • Deliver high levels of responsiveness, service, and professionalism in all interactions

  • Present agency performance insights, growth opportunities, and strategic recommendations to internal leadership and agency partners

Leadership & Mentorship

  • Mentor and support the development of Business Development Underwriters and junior staff

  • Provide guidance on underwriting approach, agency management, and deal structure

  • Participate in training, onboarding, and knowledge sharing across the team

  • Contribute to special projects, product initiatives, and process improvements as assigned

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but is expected to mentor, influence, and provide guidance to junior team members.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.
Minimum 5 years underwriting experience required; 7+ years preferred, with demonstrated experience handling more complex risks and agency relationships.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Current driver’s license required.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Demonstrated success in building and managing high-value agency relationships and driving profitable growth

  • Proven ability to underwrite complex risks and apply advanced underwriting judgment

  • Strong business development, negotiation, and relationship management skills

  • Ability to balance advanced underwriting discipline within assigned line(s) of business with production and cross-sell expectations across Commercial Lines

  • Ability to evaluate submissions, financials, and loss data to support complex decision-making

  • Advanced knowledge of Commercial Lines products, including Workers’ Compensation and/or Commercial Package and its component coverages

  • Ability to mentor, coach, and influence others

  • Strong analytical, communication, and presentation skills

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

  • Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

  • Role requires 50%-75% travel to meet with clients, attend industry events, and develop new business opportunities.

  • Travel is usually limited to automobile but occasional air travel is required.

  • Requires regular visits to outside locations such as producer's offices.

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

  • This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment. Requires the ability to work 20-30% of time from home.

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses.  If hired at ICW Group, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors unique to each candidate, including experience, education and the location of the role and considers employees performing substantially similar work.

WHY JOIN ICW GROUP? 

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference 

  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging 

  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match 

  • Bonus potential for all positions 

  • Paid Time Off

  • Paid holidays throughout the calendar year 

  • Want to continue learning? We’ll support you 100%

jobs.title: Claim Specialist Subrogation
jobs.description_html:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

AXIS is seeking a Subrogation Claims Specialist to join our North America Claims team and support the continued expansion of AXIS’ recovery operations.  The successful Candidate will manage an inventory of moderate to high‑complexity subrogation claims, ensuring timely identification of recovery opportunities, thorough investigation, accurate liability assessment, and effective pursuit of recovery from responsible parties and insurers.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities


• Performs a combination of duties in accordance with departmental guidelines.    
• Reviews claim files to identify, evaluate, analyze, and interpret subrogation potential.
• Is responsible for subrogation activities including the identification and research of subrogation claims.
• Identifies legal liability and pursues, negotiates, and settles claims where subrogation is identified.
• Coordinates appropriate steps to secure evidence and ensure pursuit, development, and recovery of claims.  
• Interacts with policyholders, claimants, and witnesses to recommend and document the necessary information to move forward with subrogation or close a file.
• Assists claim handlers during the life of the claim file to request the necessary information needed to pursue subrogation.
• Works closely with our TPA and MGA’s to ensure that all avenues of subrogation are identified and pursued.
• May provide guidance and assistance to less experienced claims staff and TPA’s.

Skills, Knowledge and Abilities

• Advanced technical and product specific expertise, claims resolution skill and knowledge of insurance and claims principles, practices and procedures.
• Strong written and verbal communication, negotiation and presentation skills. Ability to effectively interact with all levels of internal and external business partners.
• Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects.

• Ability to deal with ambiguous situations and issues.

• Creativity in resolving unique and challenging business problems.

• Knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and other business-related software.

• Ability to adapt to change and value diverse opinions and ideas.

• Ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects.

• Ability to evaluate claims based on a cost benefit analysis.

• Ability to fully comprehend complex claim facts and issues; and to further articulate analyses of claims in presentations to business partners and management as well as in internal reports.

• Ability to implement strategies with a proactive long-term view of business goals and objectives.

• Ability to successfully work in hybrid and self-directed work environment

•  Axis Culture and Values – everyday demonstrate the Axis behaviors that support and align with AXIS values: People, Decisiveness, Excellence and Stronger Together


Education and Experience

• Bachelor’s degree or minimum 5-7 years of equivalent claims handling/underwriting experience in lieu of degree

• Valid licenses by state as required and add states to certifications as needed

•  Experience or exposure to handling commercial Property claims on behalf of a syndicate, insurance company, broker, loss adjuster or solicitor preferred

Role Factors

Preferred candidates will be able to commute to an AXIS office. We are a hybrid work environment, in office 3 days a week.

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of :

Alpharetta: $85- $110k

NJ: $95- $115k

Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.  

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.   

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes. 

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.description_html:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

Job Description: Head of Enterprise Portfolio & Delivery


Role purpose

The Head of Enterprise Portfolio & Delivery is accountable for ensuring AXIS deploys its technology and AI investments against the highest-value enterprise priorities and delivers those investments predictably with measurable business outcomes. The role leads enterprise portfolio planning, prioritization, investment governance and delivery-performance oversight, providing leadership with clear insight and recommendations on value, capacity, risk and execution. The role will also continue to mature AXIS’ Agile business-technology delivery model, strengthening accountabilities, decision rights, ways of working and delivery discipline.

The role leads the divisional Portfolio Leads across North America, Reinsurance & CUO, Global Markets, Claims and Corporate, and reports to the Head of Technology & AI Strategy.

The role goes well beyond portfolio reporting. Building on the foundations AXIS put in place over the past year, the focus now is pace and value: running the portfolio engine behind our enterprise planning and governance cadence, proactively finding and fixing root causes in troubled programs, and coaching Portfolio Leads and delivery teams to build that same capability across the organization.

Job Responsibilities

Strategic Portfolio Governance & Planning

  • Planning & Prioritization: Bring a strategic, enterprise lens to the planning cycle, working with Transformation Leads and Value Stream Leads to set the right level of ambition for each division, so that demand is prioritized by business value, capacity is committed to each division’s value stream, and every investment is tied to OKRs and business case benefits.
  • Executive Decision Framing: Shape the agenda and recommendations for enterprise portfolio and investment forums. Rather than collating submissions, pressure-test the evidence on value, financials, capacity and dependencies with teams, refine proposals until they are decision-ready, frame the trade-offs leadership needs to make, and follow decisions through to closure.
  • Stage Gating & Readiness: Own project readiness and stage gating, proportionate to size and risk, as a real challenge rather than a compliance check. Probe whether the problem, scope, plan, business case and delivery approach are credible, send back proposals that are not ready, and confirm key partners (e.g., vendor management, security, data compliance, finance, architecture, AI governance) have reviewed and signed off before work starts.
  • Governance Framework: Set lean, proportionate portfolio governance with clear mandates and decision rights, focused on outcomes over process, and evolve it as the delivery model matures.

Funding, Value & Performance


  • Capacity-Based Funding: With FP&A, shape annual capacity allocation across divisions and value streams, and drive quarterly start/scale/pause/stop decisions and in-year moves based on value and delivery evidence.
  • Investment Evaluation: Challenge business cases before funding, testing assumptions, alternatives and fully loaded costs and benefits, and hold divisions to one consistent benefit-tracking approach so committed benefits are tracked through to realization.
  • AI Investment Portfolio: Manage the portfolio of AI use cases from idea to scaled value, working with AI governance, so that AI investments are prioritized, scaled or stopped based on evidence; and use AI within portfolio management to predict delivery risk and automate portfolio insight.
  • OKRs & Reporting: Run the enterprise approach for cascading and tracking OKRs and KPIs, and provide leadership with one view of value and delivery predictability (e.g., features delivered in-quarter, idea-to-release cycle time), automated from ADO and supported by AI where possible.

Problem Projects & Root-Cause Resolution


  • Proactive Intervention: Use portfolio data and early-warning signals (e.g., slipping milestones, benefits at risk, rising cost, unresolved dependencies) to identify projects in trouble, and lead the deep-dive on the most critical ones.
  • Diagnosis & Resolution: Get beyond symptoms to root causes (e.g., unclear ownership, unrealistic plans, capacity or skills gaps, vendor performance, dependent-team delays). Bring business and technology teams together to agree recovery options (re-plan, re-scope, re-sequence, add capacity, pause or stop) and follow through to resolution.
  • Learning Loop: Turn recurring causes into fixes in standards, readiness criteria, planning practices and vendor management so problems do not repeat.

Portfolio Lead Leadership

  • Lead & Coach: Lead, coach and develop the divisional Portfolio Leads to one consistent standard. Coach them to act as operating partners to the Transformation Lead and Value Stream Lead rather than reporters: challenging and shaping portfolio direction, diagnosing root causes on troubled projects and influencing course corrections.
  • Delivery-Health View: Ensure each Portfolio Lead gives their division a consolidated view of budget, scope, resourcing, risk and schedule, built from the teams’ own tools (e.g., Azure DevOps (ADO)) rather than manual reporting.
  • Capability: Run a Portfolio Lead community of practice, deliver role-based training and build a bench of portfolio talent.

Business-Technology Delivery Model

  • Delivery Model Maturity: Continue to mature AXIS’ agile business-technology delivery model across structure, governance, ways of working, culture & talent, and tooling & technology, so that delivery becomes faster, more predictable and more clearly tied to business value.
  • Ways of Working & Coaching: Own the business-technology delivery playbook and standards, and coach delivery teams hands-on to adopt them, working alongside teams on live work rather than issuing guidance.
  • Maturity Measurement: Set leading and lagging metrics against a baseline to track the maturity of the delivery model, and refine the model based on evidence.

What Success Looks Like (18–24 Months)

  • Technology and AI spend tied to quantifiable OKRs, with evidence ready for every quarterly review
  • Measurable maturity gains in the Agile business-technology delivery model against baseline
  • Delivery predictability against annual aspirations; benefits delivered vs. plan
  • Troubled projects identified early and recovered, with fewer repeat issues
  • A strong, engaged Portfolio Lead team, and positive teammate sentiment on the changes

Qualifications


  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, computer science, finance, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Proven experience in portfolio and project management, strategic planning, or a related field, including leading an enterprise portfolio function and a team of portfolio leads.
  • Track record of leading an enterprise agile delivery or product operating model transformation, including value stream funding and OKRs, and of turning around troubled programs.
  • Experience presenting investment trade-offs and recommendations to an Executive Committee.
  • Preferred: Insurance or financial services experience.

Skills & Attributes

  • Problem Solving: Structures ambiguous problems, gets to root causes quickly and drives practical solutions through to resolution.
  • Influence Without Authority: Builds alignment and drives action across business, technology and vendor leaders outside direct authority, and coaches rather than commands.
  • Communication: Clear, concise and compelling, able to turn complex portfolio data into decision-ready insight for the Executive Committee and to have candid conversations when projects are off track.
  • Financial & Delivery Acumen: Builds and challenges business cases, understands capex/opex and capacity-based funding, and uses delivery metrics (e.g., predictability, cycle time, benefits realization) to drive decisions.

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $200,000 to $225,000 (NY). Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.

Job Description: Chief of Staff to the Group COO


Position Summary


The Chief of Staff to the Group COO serves as the strategic execution partner to the Group COO, ensuring alignment, execution discipline, and measurable value delivery across AXIS's Operations, Data & Analytics, Technology, AI, Transformation, Architecture, and Information Security portfolios. Based on the current AXIS role profile, the Chief of Staff acts as the strategic extension of the Group COO and the primary integration point across these functions.

This role converts strategy into action by driving portfolio governance, operating cadence, value realization, cross-functional execution, and executive decision support. The Chief of Staff enables the Group COO to focus on the highest-value strategic, operating, talent, and investment decisions while ensuring accountability for execution and outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & COO Agenda

  • Shape and manage the Group COO's enterprise agenda and strategic priorities.
  • Integrate Operations, Technology, Data & Analytics, AI, and Transformation into a unified operating model and execution roadmap.
  • Surface key trade-offs, dependencies, risks, and recommendations for decision-making

Portfolio Management & Value Realization

  • Maintain oversight of the COO portfolio, including investment priorities, benefits realization, execution health, and resource allocation.
  • Ensure major initiatives have clear business outcomes, ownership, success metrics, and accountability.
  • Challenge initiatives that are not delivering measurable business value.

Enterprise Execution & Transformation

  • Drive coordination across complex cross-functional initiatives.
  • Resolve interdependencies, delivery obstacles, and organizational barriers.
  • Ensure transformation efforts produce sustainable business outcomes rather than activity-based progress.

Data, Technology & AI Leadership

  • Act as the COO's integration point across Data & Analytics, Technology, AI, Architecture, and Operations.
  • Ensure investments are aligned to underwriting advantage, operational effectiveness, scalability, and business growth.
  • Support responsible AI adoption, governance, workforce readiness, and value realization.

Operations & Underwriting Support Effectiveness

  • Partner with Operations and Underwriting leadership to improve capacity, efficiency, resilience, service quality, and scalability.
  • Drive process modernization, workflow redesign, automation, and AI-enabled operating model improvements.
  • Support AXIS's objective of increasing underwriting capacity without proportionate increases in operational cost or headcount.

Governance, Risk & Resilience

  • Operate the management cadence for the COO organization, including strategic reviews, investment governance, risk reviews, and performance management.
  • Maintain visibility of operational, technology, cyber, AI, third-party, and execution risks.
  • Track and coordinate significant audit, regulatory, control, and remediation commitments.

Executive & Board Support

  • Prepare the Group COO for ExCo, Board, and executive leadership discussions.
  • Develop concise, decision-oriented materials, recommendations, and executive-level analyses.
  • Ensure consistent messaging across the COO portfolio.

Experience & Qualifications

  • Senior leadership experience in Operations, Strategy, Transformation, Technology, Data & Analytics, AI, or Enterprise Program Leadership.
  • Experience operating within a complex, regulated financial services or insurance environment.
  • Proven ability to lead large-scale cross-functional initiatives and influence senior executives without direct authority.
  • Strong commercial, financial, operational, and strategic acumen.
  • Working knowledge of technology, data, AI, governance, risk, and organizational design.

Leadership Capabilities

  • Enterprise thinker with strong business judgment.
  • Strategic, outcome-oriented, and execution-focused.
  • Excellent executive communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Strong financial and value-realization mindset.
  • Ability to challenge constructively and drive accountability.
  • Trusted advisor capable of operating effectively with senior leadership and the Board.

Success Measures

The Chief of Staff will be successful when:

  • The Group COO agenda is clear, focused, and effectively executed.
  • Strategic investments deliver measurable business value.
  • Cross-functional execution is coordinated and predictable.
  • Technology, AI, and data initiatives improve underwriting and operational performance.
  • Risks, dependencies, and remediation activities are proactively managed.
  • Executive and Board discussions are concise, fact-based, and decision-oriented.

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $225,000 to $275,000 (NY). Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 


In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  


Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is [Exempt/Non-Exempt] for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

As a direct report to the Head of E&S Property Claims, the successful candidate will be responsible for the quality, accuracy, and performance of serious and complex commercial property claims; provide direction and technical guidance through a continuous process of management involvement; and will lead, mentor, manage the performance and development of other Company employees.

    Using data-driven reporting and productivity metrics, this leader will develop the optimal target operating model to deliver best-in-class service for AXIS clients and that provides career paths for Axis claim professionals to grow and develop. This role will also be responsible for delivering the AXIS North America Claims value proposition engaging with stakeholders, brokers, and insureds to ensure constant communication and service engagement distinguishes Axis claims every day.

    This role will lead and develop a team of claims professionals to provide best-in-class service and are responsible for:
    • Direct supervision and management of claims including the investigation, analysis and evaluation of coverage liability and damages, within best practices
    • Close collaboration with the Head of Specialty Complex Claims for matters involving coverage disputes, including litigation and arbitration initiated by Axis issuing companies and when Axis issuing companies are parties to such litigation
    • Ensures that high quality Claim Summary Reports are being effectively completed and managed by Claim Leadership team to promote customer service excellence
    • Ensures understanding and administration of claim policies, procedures, and practices in accordance with company and policy standards
    • Directly responsible for implementing a people strategy that supports training and skills improvement initiatives that achieve increased bench strength and improved career pathing
    • Provides leadership that encourages and supports a professional environment and promotes a business culture that leverages attainment of desired business results
    • Focus on resolution and process improvement, fulfilling all obligations while maximizing cost effectiveness, helping the Company understand drivers, trends and helping our partners attract and retain business
    • Supporting underwriting inquiries and information requests regarding policy construction and drafting, reporting claim trends, data analysis, and risk assessments
    • Actively coaching and mentoring direct reports, providing regular feedback, and developing employees for broader roles and responsibilities that support professional growth and development and working collaboratively with HR Business partner support and guidance.
    • Recruit, hire and retain top talent and develop appropriate succession plans
    • Build and maintain key relationships with internal stakeholders (e.g., peers, Underwriting, Actuarial, various executive management leaders) and external stakeholders (e.g., brokers, insureds, attorneys, auditors, reinsurers, and vendors)
    • Axis Culture and Values – everyday demonstrate the Axis behaviors that support and align with Axis values: People, Decisiveness, Excellence and Stronger Together

    KEY SKILLS & ABILITIES:

    3-5 years of claims management experience in Claims Leadership of the specific lines of business as well as:
    • Demonstrated leadership, organizational, and management skills
    • A public profile and reputation for leadership and technical excellence
    • Demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate at all organizational levels, both internally and externally as well as the ability to identify and resolve complex, disputed claims
    • Analytical and data proficiency to drive results, make decisions and drive outcomes
    • Understanding of and ability to balance both the immediate claim issues as well as the broader portfolio impact and customer service impact of coverage disputes and issues
    • Excellent oral and written communication skills with the ability to deal effectively with people with conflicting expectations, differing opinions, and multiple viewpoints
    • Demonstrated ability and experience handling claims involving a wide variety of loss scenarios, including CAT losses, as well as reporting and presenting about same to senior management
    • In-depth knowledge of claims, litigation, arbitration, and trial processes as well as excellent analytical, investigative, and negotiating skills
    • Travel is associated with this role (e.g., team management, broker & client meetings, conferences & other marketing)

jobs.description_html:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

AXIS is hiring a Senior Claims Specialist – Environmental Claims for its North America Claim Team. This role will manage complex primary and excess environmental claims arising under specialty environmental insurance products and will work closely with internal and external partners to deliver timely, technically sound claim outcomes.


How does this role contribute to our collective success?

The individual will investigate, analyze, and evaluate coverage, liability, damages, and resolution strategy for complex environmental claims. The role contributes to disciplined claim execution, strong portfolio oversight, and effective collaboration with underwriting, legal, actuarial, reinsurance, and other business partners. The individual will also help develop environmental claims expertise across the broader Claims organization.


What Will You Do In This Role?

·    Assess complex environmental claims to determine coverage, liability, damages, reserve requirements, and settlement value.

·    Manage claims arising under environmental insurance products, which may include pollution legal liability, contractors pollution liability, site-specific pollution, storage tank, and related coverages.

·    Develop and execute claim strategies for matters involving remediation costs, bodily injury, property damage, natural resource damages, regulatory action, and other environmental exposures.

·    Analyze policy wording, historical operations, allocation issues, trigger and timing considerations, and the interaction of primary, excess, and other available insurance.

·    Direct defense counsel, coverage counsel, environmental consultants, experts, investigators, and other vendors to support efficient and effective claim outcomes.

·    Identify material developments and emerging exposures, maintain accurate reserves and financial information, and escalate significant claims in accordance with internal guidelines.

·    Manage legal, expert, and vendor costs in collaboration with the Litigation Management and Vendor Management teams.

·    Communicate clearly with senior executives, brokers, reinsurers, actuaries, underwriters, insureds, counsel, auditors, and other stakeholders.

·    Partner with Underwriting and Claims leadership to identify portfolio trends, emerging environmental risks, and opportunities to improve policy language and claim practices.

·    Lead or support initiatives that enhance claims processing efficiency, technical quality, data integrity, and regulatory compliance.

·    Participate in professional associations and continuing education to remain current on environmental law, regulation, science, and claims developments.

·    Serve as a mentor and technical resource to claims professionals, supporting skill development and career progression.


About You

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge may help you succeed in this role and contribute to our goals.


What We're Looking For

·    Significant experience handling complex environmental, toxic tort, long-tail casualty, or other technically challenging claims, preferably within the commercial insurance industry.

·    Demonstrated ability to analyze environmental policies, coverage issues, liability, damages, allocation, and complex factual records.

·    Working knowledge of environmental laws, regulations, remediation processes, and litigation trends relevant to environmental claims.

·    Ability to develop and execute resolution strategies for high-severity, multi-party, or contentious matters.

·    Strong judgment in establishing reserves, identifying material developments, and escalating significant exposures.

·    Ability to direct counsel, consultants, experts, and vendors while maintaining disciplined control of claim-related costs.

·    Clear and credible written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex issues to technical and non-technical audiences.

·    Ability to collaborate effectively across Claims, Underwriting, Actuarial, Reinsurance, Legal, Finance, and other business functions.

·    Demonstrated ability to lead process improvement initiatives, contribute to training materials, and critically review claims procedures.

·    Commitment to continuous professional development and to mentoring peers within the claims discipline.

·    Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience; professional insurance, legal, environmental, or claims designations are beneficial.


Role Factors

This role requires you to be in the office 3 days per week and adhere to AXIS licensing requirements. Some travel may be required based on business and claim needs.


What We Offer

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $140,000 to $155,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Senior Manager, Quality Assurance and Compliance | North America Claims, Claims Shared Services-

AXIS is seeking a Senior Manager, Quality Assurance and Audit, North America Claims to join the Claims Shared Services team. Reporting to the Head of Quality Assurance and Compliance, Claims Shared Services, this role will lead, oversee, enhance and optimize the North America claim direct handle, manager quality review and TPA oversight audit program. The role will also coordinate, oversee, and enhance the North America Claims SIU and Fraud program.

The successful candidate will plan, coordinate, monitor, and report on audits and quality file reviews across North America Claims, including specialty claim handler audits across multiple lines of business, TPA oversight audits, and leadership quality control file reviews. Incumbent may be responsible for technical file reviews. The role will manage audit execution through internal stakeholders and external audit partners, track findings through closure, report results to leadership, and use audit insights to strengthen claim handling quality, compliance, consistency, and operational performance.

This role is ideal for a claims, audit, quality assurance, or compliance professional with strong technical claims judgment, experience assessing specialty claim handler performance, working knowledge of TPA or outsourced claims partner oversight, and the ability to translate audit and file review results into practical actions that improve claim outcomes.

The successful Candidate will be responsible for:

Claims Audit Program Management
• Lead and report on the North America claim handler audit program, TPA oversight audit program, and leadership quality control file review program across multiple lines of business.
• Manage end-to-end audit execution, including planning, scope, scheduling, sample selection, file collection, stakeholder communications, and audit readiness.
• Coordinate with claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPAs, audit vendors, Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, and Operations to ensure consistent, timely audit delivery.
• Enhance audit standards, questionnaires, scorecards, and methodologies in line with claim best practices, regulatory expectations, and technical excellence standards.
• Review audit observations across coverage, liability, damages, reserving, litigation management, settlement strategy, documentation quality, compliance, and claim handling controls.
• Track findings, action plans, remediation activities, owner accountability, due dates, and closure evidence.

Audit Results, Analytics, and Reporting
• Gather, validate, and analyze audit results, quality assurance data, compliance findings, and technical claim handling trends.
• Develop dashboards, scorecards, and management reports covering quality review results, technical audit outcomes, recurring themes, risk areas, trends, and improvement opportunities.
• Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting for Claims leadership and governance forums, covering claim handler audit results, TPA oversight audit results, and leadership quality control file review outcomes.
• Measure audit effectiveness, remediation progress, transparency, accountability, and control discipline.

Compliance, Controls, and Remediation
• Partner with Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, Claims Operations, and Claims Leadership to align audit activity with regulatory, governance, and operational risk priorities.
• Monitor findings related to Medicare, regulatory obligations, documentation standards, claim handling controls, and other compliance requirements.
• Maintain action plans that address findings, strengthen controls, and promote consistent claim handling across North America specialty claim teams, TPA claim programs, and leadership quality control file reviews.
• Escalate material issues, recurring trends, control gaps, and remediation delays to appropriate leaders and governance forums.

SIU and Fraud Audit Program
• Enhance, measure, and report on the SIU and fraud deliverable program as part of the North America claims audit program.
• Assess whether SIU and fraud deliverables are timely, complete, consistent, and aligned with claim handling expectations, regulatory obligations, and technical audit standards.
• Identify themes, control gaps, escalation issues, documentation weaknesses, and opportunities to improve fraud identification, referral quality, and SIU oversight.
• Partner with SIU, Compliance, Claims leadership, TPAs, and audit vendors to strengthen execution, reporting, accountability, and remediation follow-through.

Technical Excellence and Continuous Improvement
• Use audit and quality control file review insights to improve technical claim quality, consistency, reserving discipline, litigation management, settlement practices, and compliance execution.
• Support updates to claims guidelines, audit protocols, procedures, workflows, controls, and training materials based on audit trends and root-cause analysis.
• Provide practical recommendations to claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPAs, and business partners to improve claim outcomes and audit performance.
• Participate in governance meetings, working groups, and initiatives related to claims quality, audit readiness, and technical excellence.

Stakeholder Management
• Build effective relationships across North America Claims, specialty claim teams, TPAs, Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, Actuarial, Finance, Operations, and Shared Services.
• Manage day-to-day coordination with external audit vendors, including schedules, deliverables, issue tracking, reporting inputs, and performance expectations.
• Provide audit and quality assurance subject matter support to claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPA managers, and governance stakeholders.
• Communicate findings, themes, risks, and recommendations clearly to management and senior leadership.

Skills
• 6–10 years of experience in commercial P&C insurance, reinsurance, specialty claims, claims audit, quality assurance, compliance, operational risk, or a related discipline.

Technical skills or claims management adjusting experience preferred.
• Minimum 3 years of experience supporting or managing claims audits, quality assurance reviews, compliance monitoring, operational controls, or remediation tracking.
• Experience working with TPAs, outsourced claims partners, audit vendors, or vendor oversight programs.
• Experience auditing specialty claim files across multiple lines of business and supporting technical claim quality reviews.
• Experience developing audit reports, dashboards, metrics, scorecards, or performance analytics for leadership review.
• Strong technical claims judgment and ability to assess claim handling quality across coverage, liability, damages, reserving, litigation, settlement, and documentation practices.
• Strong analytical, communication, project coordination, organizational, stakeholder management, and vendor management skills.
• Ability to identify themes, root causes, risks, control gaps, performance improvement opportunities, and remediation priorities.
• Ability to manage multiple audits, stakeholders, priorities, and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
• Strong proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and reporting tools.
• Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree, CPCU, AIC, ARM, CFE, CIA, CPA, JD, or other relevant professional designation preferred.

Additional Information

• Ability to work in a hybrid environment (3 days in office)
• Some travel may be required

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of 140-160K. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is [Exempt/Non-Exempt] for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.
