• Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting for Claims leadership and governance forums, covering claim handler audit results, TPA oversight audit results, and leadership quality control file review outcomes.
• Measure audit effectiveness, remediation progress, transparency, accountability, and control discipline.
Compliance, Controls, and Remediation
• Partner with Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, Claims Operations, and Claims Leadership to align audit activity with regulatory, governance, and operational risk priorities.
• Monitor findings related to Medicare, regulatory obligations, documentation standards, claim handling controls, and other compliance requirements.
• Maintain action plans that address findings, strengthen controls, and promote consistent claim handling across North America specialty claim teams, TPA claim programs, and leadership quality control file reviews.
• Escalate material issues, recurring trends, control gaps, and remediation delays to appropriate leaders and governance forums.
SIU and Fraud Audit Program
• Enhance, measure, and report on the SIU and fraud deliverable program as part of the North America claims audit program.
• Assess whether SIU and fraud deliverables are timely, complete, consistent, and aligned with claim handling expectations, regulatory obligations, and technical audit standards.
• Identify themes, control gaps, escalation issues, documentation weaknesses, and opportunities to improve fraud identification, referral quality, and SIU oversight.
• Partner with SIU, Compliance, Claims leadership, TPAs, and audit vendors to strengthen execution, reporting, accountability, and remediation follow-through.
Technical Excellence and Continuous Improvement
• Use audit and quality control file review insights to improve technical claim quality, consistency, reserving discipline, litigation management, settlement practices, and compliance execution.
• Support updates to claims guidelines, audit protocols, procedures, workflows, controls, and training materials based on audit trends and root-cause analysis.
• Provide practical recommendations to claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPAs, and business partners to improve claim outcomes and audit performance.
• Participate in governance meetings, working groups, and initiatives related to claims quality, audit readiness, and technical excellence.
Stakeholder Management
• Build effective relationships across North America Claims, specialty claim teams, TPAs, Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, Actuarial, Finance, Operations, and Shared Services.
• Manage day-to-day coordination with external audit vendors, including schedules, deliverables, issue tracking, reporting inputs, and performance expectations.
• Provide audit and quality assurance subject matter support to claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPA managers, and governance stakeholders.
• Communicate findings, themes, risks, and recommendations clearly to management and senior leadership.

• 6–10 years of experience in commercial P&C insurance, reinsurance, specialty claims, claims audit, quality assurance, compliance, operational risk, or a related discipline.
 Technical skills or claims management adjusting experience preferred.

• Experience working with TPAs, outsourced claims partners, audit vendors, or vendor oversight programs.
• Experience auditing specialty claim files across multiple lines of business and supporting technical claim quality reviews.
• Experience developing audit reports, dashboards, metrics, scorecards, or performance analytics for leadership review.
• Strong technical claims judgment and ability to assess claim handling quality across coverage, liability, damages, reserving, litigation, settlement, and documentation practices.
• Strong analytical, communication, project coordination, organizational, stakeholder management, and vendor management skills.
• Ability to identify themes, root causes, risks, control gaps, performance improvement opportunities, and remediation priorities.

Claims Specialist – Employment Practices Liability


Job Code



About the Team

AXIS is a leading provider of specialty insurance and global reinsurance. This role is on the Wholesale Financial Lines Claims team, which handles excess and primary claims for Employment Practices Liability (EPL), Directors and Officers (D&O), and related lines.

This role reports to the Head of Wholesale Claims – Financial Lines and is responsible for investigating, analyzing, and evaluating EPL claims, ensuring proper coverage determinations and navigating claims to successful conclusions. The selected individual will gain expertise in EPL claims and coverage while engaging with sophisticated insureds and resolving complex disputes. This role offers meaningful opportunities to handle claims in specialized insurance sectors and to learn to the broader range of Wholesale Financial Lines products.

What Will You Do In This Role?

  • Serving as a Claims Specialist focused on Employment Practices Liability claims within AXIS' North America Claim team.
  • Determining the appropriate valuation of complex claims, recommending settlement strategies, adhering to company policies, and collaborating with insureds, brokers, and partners effectively.
  • Traveling to participate in mediations, observe trials, and strengthen relationships with vital AXIS partners.
  • Escalating coverage concerns to internal teams and collaborating with external coverage attorneys when specific assignments necessitate their involvement.
  • Developing claim and litigation strategies, delegating tasks, and overseeing the work of external legal advisors effectively.
  • Assisting with underwriting inquiries while analyzing claim trends, conducting data analysis, and performing comprehensive risk assessments to support decision-making processes.
  • Keeping precise records of claim activities and promptly updating systems with all relevant details ensuring accuracy and efficiency.

About You

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table, so while there are some qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge might lend itself to fulfilling this role and help us achieve our goals.

What We're Looking For

  • Candidates who bring unique perspectives and diverse skills to the team.
  • Contribute actively to the success of a growing and dynamic team by bringing energy and a positive attitude.
  • Hold a Juris Doctorate.
  • Operate efficiently in settings with high visibility, shifting deadlines, and evolving expectations while staying focused and achieving outcomes.
  • Demonstrate organizational abilities and solve problems effectively.
  • Exhibit outstanding skill in verbal communication and written expression.
  • Showcase skill as a litigator or litigation manager, well-versed in dispute resolution.
  • Write coverage letters independently with precision and attention to detail, ensuring accuracy in all aspects of the work.

Role Factors

Travel is associated with this role. The role requires you to be in office 3 days per week and adhere to AXIS licensing requirements.

What We Offer

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $90,000 - $125,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more. Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

jobs.description_html:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

Senior Underwriter – Ocean Marine Cargo
New York or Chicago


The Senior Underwriter, Ocean Marine Cargo will act within established guidelines to analyze, evaluate, price, and manage new and renewal business in support of the growth of the U.S. Ocean Marine Cargo portfolio. The initial focus will include Small and Middle Market, Large Complex Transit, Stock Throughput, and Excess Stock Exposure risks


The role will also support AXIS’s broader Marine Logistics capabilities, which complement traditional Cargo coverage by addressing liability exposures throughout the movement, handling, and storage of goods. Relevant experience may include Cargo Legal Liability, Warehouse Legal Liability, Errors & Omissions, Shipper’s Interest, and packaged logistics solutions.


Candidate Profile

The Senior Underwriter, Ocean Marine Cargo will be a hands-on technical underwriting professional with a demonstrated history of success within a leading commercial insurance carrier, building and managing a complex Ocean Marine Cargo portfolio.


Candidates should have strong relationships across Ocean Marine Cargo wholesale and retail broker channels and full lifecycle underwriting experience, including solicitation and evaluation of submissions, risk analysis, structuring terms and conditions, pricing, preparing and issuing indications, quotations and binders, and portfolio management.


Candidates with Marine Logistics or related supply-chain liability underwriting experience are especially attractive, including exposure to freight forwarders, logistics providers, warehouse operators, and transportation intermediaries. Experience with Cargo Legal Liability, Warehouse Legal Liability, Errors & Omissions, Shipper’s Interest, or packaged Marine Logistics solutions is highly desirable.


The successful candidate should understand how traditional Cargo exposures interact with transportation, warehousing, contractual liability, and logistics-related risks across the broader supply chain, allowing them to evaluate opportunities from both a cargo/property and logistics liability perspective

Key Duties and Responsibilities

  • Underwrite and manage complex Ocean Marine Cargo business, including Small and Middle Market, Large Complex Transit, Stock Throughput, and Excess Stock Exposure risks.
  • Evaluate Marine Logistics opportunities that complement the Ocean Cargo portfolio, including Cargo Legal Liability, Warehouse Legal Liability, Errors & Omissions, Shipper’s Interest, and packaged logistics solutions.
  • Assess supply-chain exposures involving freight forwarders, logistics providers, warehouse operators, transportation intermediaries, and other businesses involved in the movement, handling, and storage of goods.
  • Review contractual and operational exposures to determine appropriate coverage structure, limits, retentions, pricing, terms, conditions, and endorsements.
  • Work with brokers to identify cross-sell opportunities across Ocean Cargo and Logistics, and develop broader solutions for clients with complex supply-chain exposures.
  • Prospect for new business and develop strategies targeting Small to Middle Market and Large Complex Corporate risks.
  • Develop and maintain strong wholesale and retail broker relationships, using those relationships to generate submissions and expand the portfolio.

Required Experience

  • 5+ years of direct Ocean Marine Cargo underwriting experience.
  • Demonstrated experience building and managing complex Ocean Cargo business.
  • Experience with Logistics, Cargo Legal Liability, Warehouse Legal Liability, Errors & Omissions, Shipper’s Interest, or related transportation/logistics liability products strongly preferred.
  • Understanding of supply-chain exposures and the contractual relationships among cargo owners, freight forwarders, logistics providers, warehouse operators, and transportation intermediaries.
  • Ability to build and expand retail and wholesale broker relationships.
  • Strong technical underwriting, portfolio management, negotiation, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a collaborative underwriting environment with strong attention to detail.

We currently expect to offer a base salary of $150,000 -210,000K for this position. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of various factors, including your specific years experience and work location. In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate performance and your performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package that includes medical plans.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

We are seeking an Enterprise Test & Quality Lead to provide end-to-end ownership of testing across development, QA, UAT, and release activities. This role is accountable for defining and governing the test strategy, coordinating testing across multiple concurrent delivery teams, improving environment and test data readiness, and ensuring that releases meet agreed quality and business acceptance criteria. The role is particularly important in a delivery context where shared environments, constrained non-production data, and cross-team dependencies require disciplined planning, strong stakeholder management, and clear operational control.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end test management lifecycle across Unit Testing, System Integration Testing, QA, UAT, regression testing, and release readiness.

  • Define and drive a Quality Engineering strategy embedding automated testing across the SDLC including “shift-left” and “shift-right” practices.

  • Define and maintain the overall test strategy, test plans, phase entry and exit criteria, acceptance thresholds, and defect management approach. Work and align with incumbent vendor to align QA to this overall strategy.

  • Define and enforce automated quality gates within CI/CD pipelines.

  • Coordinate testing across multiple concurrent scrum teams, ensuring alignment of delivery schedules, dependencies, and release milestones.

  • Define an environment strategy that enables parallel team execution, minimizes contention, and supports continuous testing.

  • Ownership of Test Data Governance Framework

  • o Ensure adherence and support from DPO / IRM / Privacy

  • Own the approach to Test Data Management, including data readiness, lineage, masking or obfuscation controls, and interim solutions required to support testing safely and effectively.

  • Partner with QA leads to define test scenarios, test cases, regression coverage, and the appropriate level of automation, including use of tools such as Tosca to deliver ROI driven automation, decisions on what to automate and coverage targets. 

  • KPI Management of QA vendor

  • SLA tracking

  • Capability and skill matrix optimization.

  • Trend analysis of defect origin (code, data, environment, design) leading to systemic issue elimination

  • Work with Product Owners and business stakeholders to secure UAT participation, define UAT scripts and acceptance criteria, and manage UAT execution to completion.

  • The Test Manager should be a critical input into the release management go / no go stage gate decisions.

  • Manage defect triage, retest cycles, and regression planning to ensure efficient resolution and minimal disruption to completed testing.

  • Provide decision grade insights on test progress, risks, defect trends, environment readiness, and overall release confidence to project and executive stakeholders.

  • Drive continuous improvement in test practices, with a focus on moving from reactive or waterfall-like testing toward a more agile, disciplined, and scalable operating model.

  • Define and oversee post release validation strategies, including observability, monitoring, and production quality feedback loops.

  • Skills and Experience

  • Proven experience in Test Management, QA leadership, or quality engineering leadership within complex technology delivery environments.

  • Strong understanding of end-to-end software testing practices across unit, integration, system, regression, data lineage and user acceptance testing.

  • Experience managing testing in agile delivery environments with multiple concurrent teams and shared environments.

  • Practical knowledge of test automation and engineering led strategy and tooling, ideally including Tosca or comparable platforms, especially AI driven technologies and processes.

  • Strong understanding of environment management and test data management, including handling of sensitive data in non-production environments.

  • Ability to define quality gates, release readiness criteria, and structured defect management processes.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work across engineering, QA, product, operations, and business teams.

  • Excellent planning, coordination, and communication skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and delivery risk.

  • Experience in regulated or control-conscious environments is highly desirable.

  • Experience of integrating testing into DevOps pipelines and familiarity with release orchestration and production validation techniques.

  • Experience of operating in SAFe (scaled agile) frameworks


Success Measures

  • Improved coordination and predictability across QA and UAT cycles including continuous validation and early user involvement.

  • Reduction in defects caused by environment or data issues rather than true functional failures.

  • Clear and consistently applied phase entry, exit, and acceptance criteria.

  • Increased confidence in release readiness and reduced rework or defect recycling.

  • Greater use of automation and regression coverage to support faster retest cycles.

  • Stronger governance, visibility, and accountability for end-to-end testing outcomes.


Key Interfaces
This role will work closely with Development Leads, QA Leads, Product Owners, Business UAT representatives, Environment and Release Management teams, Data and Privacy stakeholders, and senior programme or technology leadership.
Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • Relevant testing or quality certifications such as ISTQB Advanced Test Manager or equivalent are desirable.

  • Experience in insurance, financial services, or other highly regulated delivery environments would be advantageous.

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $180,00 - $230,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.  

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.   

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

 We are seeking an Enterprise Test & Quality Lead to provide end-to-end ownership of testing across development, QA, UAT, and release activities. This role is accountable for defining and governing the test strategy, coordinating testing across multiple concurrent delivery teams, improving environment and test data readiness, and ensuring that releases meet agreed quality and business acceptance criteria. The role is particularly important in a delivery context where shared environments, constrained non-production data, and cross-team dependencies require disciplined planning, strong stakeholder management, and clear operational control.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Own the end-to-end test management lifecycle across Unit Testing, System Integration Testing, QA, UAT, regression testing, and release readiness.
 Define and drive a Quality Engineering strategy embedding automated testing across the SDLC including “shift-left” and “shift-right” practices.
 Define and maintain the overall test strategy, test plans, phase entry and exit criteria, acceptance thresholds, and defect management approach. Work and align with incumbent vendor to align QA to this overall strategy.
 Define and enforce automated quality gates within CI/CD pipelines.
 Coordinate testing across multiple concurrent scrum teams, ensuring alignment of delivery schedules, dependencies, and release milestones.
 Define an environment strategy that enables parallel team execution, minimizes contention, and supports continuous testing.
 Ownership of Test Data Governance Framework 
 o Ensure adherence and support from DPO / IRM / Privacy
 Own the approach to Test Data Management, including data readiness, lineage, masking or obfuscation controls, and interim solutions required to support testing safely and effectively.
 Partner with QA leads to define test scenarios, test cases, regression coverage, and the appropriate level of automation, including use of tools such as Tosca to deliver ROI driven automation, decisions on what to automate and coverage targets. 
 KPI Management of QA vendor
 SLA tracking 
 Capability and skill matrix optimization.
 Trend analysis of defect origin (code, data, environment, design) leading to systemic issue elimination
 Work with Product Owners and business stakeholders to secure UAT participation, define UAT scripts and acceptance criteria, and manage UAT execution to completion.
 The Test Manager should be a critical input into the release management go / no go stage gate decisions.
 Manage defect triage, retest cycles, and regression planning to ensure efficient resolution and minimal disruption to completed testing.
 Provide decision grade insights on test progress, risks, defect trends, environment readiness, and overall release confidence to project and executive stakeholders.
 Drive continuous improvement in test practices, with a focus on moving from reactive or waterfall-like testing toward a more agile, disciplined, and scalable operating model.
 Define and oversee post release validation strategies, including observability, monitoring, and production quality feedback loops.
 Skills and Experience
 Proven experience in Test Management, QA leadership, or quality engineering leadership within complex technology delivery environments. 
 Strong understanding of end-to-end software testing practices across unit, integration, system, regression, data lineage and user acceptance testing.
 Experience managing testing in agile delivery environments with multiple concurrent teams and shared environments.
 Practical knowledge of test automation and engineering led strategy and tooling, ideally including Tosca or comparable platforms, especially AI driven technologies and processes.
 Strong understanding of environment management and test data management, including handling of sensitive data in non-production environments.
 Ability to define quality gates, release readiness criteria, and structured defect management processes.
 Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work across engineering, QA, product, operations, and business teams.
 Excellent planning, coordination, and communication skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and delivery risk.
 Experience in regulated or control-conscious environments is highly desirable.
 Experience of integrating testing into DevOps pipelines and familiarity with release orchestration and production validation techniques.
 Experience of operating in SAFe (scaled agile) frameworks
 Success Measures 
 Improved coordination and predictability across QA and UAT cycles including continuous validation and early user involvement.
 Reduction in defects caused by environment or data issues rather than true functional failures.
 Clear and consistently applied phase entry, exit, and acceptance criteria.
 Increased confidence in release readiness and reduced rework or defect recycling.
 Greater use of automation and regression coverage to support faster retest cycles.
 Stronger governance, visibility, and accountability for end-to-end testing outcomes.
 Key Interfaces 
This role will work closely with Development Leads, QA Leads, Product Owners, Business UAT representatives, Environment and Release Management teams, Data and Privacy stakeholders, and senior programme or technology leadership.
Preferred Qualifications
 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline.
 Relevant testing or quality certifications such as ISTQB Advanced Test Manager or equivalent are desirable.
 Experience in insurance, financial services, or other highly regulated delivery environments would be advantageous.
 For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $180,00 - $230,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.  
 I n addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.   
 Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

Senior Analyst, Third Party Services, NA

AXIS is seeking a Senior Analyst, Third Party Services to join the Claims Shared Services organization. Reporting to the Head of Claims Third Party Delegated Services, this role is responsible for supporting the effective management and oversight of North America Claims Third Party Administrators (TPAs) and non-legal claim vendors globally.

The role is accountable for the effective oversight of service providers and vendors across the third-party lifecycle, including sourcing, due diligence, contracting, onboarding, performance management, renewal and offboarding.  The role will lead defined governance activities, provide informed analysis and challenge, and deliver meaningful management information to support business decision-making.

This is a hands-on senior role in which the successful candidate will build effective relationships with Claims Third Party Management, Claims Leadership, Underwriting Operations, Program Managers, Compliance, QA, Legal, Vendor Management and service providers. They will be responsible for driving timely decisions, achieving effective issue remediation and consistently delivering strong third party governance outcomes including supporting continuous improvement efforts for the Claims third party management framework.

The Successful Candidate Will Be Responsible For

TPA and Non-Legal Third Party Governance Administration & Coordination

  • Act as the primary Third Party Services contact for an allocated portfolio of TPAs and non-legal Claims service providers.
  • Lead scheduled governance and performance reviews, ensuring clear assessment of service delivery, risk, controls and customer outcomes.
  • Undertake onboarding, renewal and offboarding activities, coordinating stakeholder input and ensuring that governance requirements are completed to the required standard.
  • Evaluate compliance with contractual obligations, service levels, governance standards and agreed performance measures.
  • Identify material risks, control weaknesses and performance concerns, applying appropriate challenge and escalating issues where required.
  • Agree, monitor and escalate remediation plans, ensuring actions are delivered within agreed timescales.
  • Maintain accurate portfolio records, governance schedules and relationship profiles to support effective management and decision-making.

Due Diligence & Audit Support

  • Coordinate planning and execution of initial and ongoing due diligence reviews.
  • Assemble and organize documentation required for due diligence reviews.
  • Maintain audit evidence repositories and supporting documentation.
  • Track audit findings, remediation activities and implementation status.
  • Prepare materials for internal audit, compliance and regulatory reviews.
  • Maintain records of governance approvals, assessments and supporting evidence.
  • Assist with periodic governance reporting and documentation reviews.

Performance Analysis and Management Insight

  • Produce recurring TPA and vendor performance reports.
  • Maintain scorecard data, KPI reporting and service tracking metrics.
  • Assist in preparation of management reporting packages.
  • Analyse service performance trends and exception reporting.
  • Track service level performance and remediation commitments.
  • Maintain governance dashboards and reporting repositories.

Governance Framework and Process Management

  • Develop and maintain governance procedures, operating guides and process documentation for managing third party services providers.
  • Organize document repositories and version control processes.
  • Coordinate updates to governance templates, checklists and standards documentation.
  • Maintain governance evidence and records retention requirements.
  • Support preparation of presentations and leadership materials.
  • Ensure documentation remains current and audit ready.

Stakeholder Leadership and Strategic Delivery

  • Coordinate activities across Claims, Programs, Underwriting Operations, QA, Compliance, Legal and Vendor Management.
  • Maintain action logs, issue trackers and governance review records.
  • Facilitate communication between stakeholders involved in governance activities.
  • Support implementation of governance initiatives and process enhancements.
  • Assist with special projects relating to delegated claims and third-party service governance.

Skills, Experience & Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in third party management, sourcing and procurement roles.
  • 2-5 years of experience in insurance operations, claims operations and delegated authority roles preferred.
  • Strong organizational and administrative skills.
  • Demonstrated attention to detail and documentation discipline.
  • Experience preparing reports, scorecards and management information.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Teams and SharePoint.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
  • Experience supporting audits, compliance reviews, vendor governance or operational oversight activities preferred.
  • Knowledge of claims operations, delegated claims administration or program business preferred.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.

 We anticipate offering a base salary of 125-140K dependent upon a variety of factors including experience and location.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.description_html:

AXIS is seeking a US Renewable Energy Claims Associate to join our Global Markets Claims team. This developmental role supports the handling of renewable energy claims under the supervision of experienced claims professionals. The successful candidate will gain practical experience in claim investigation, coverage review, reserving, stakeholder communication, and claim resolution across first-party and third-party losses.

The role will help deliver the AXIS Global Markets Claims value proposition by working with clients, brokers, external adjusters, engineers, counsel, underwriters, actuaries, and operations colleagues. The trainee will support clear communication, accurate claim administration, and a premier claims service while developing the technical judgment required for progressively broader responsibility.

The successful candidate will:

• Support the handling of US Renewable Energy claims allocated to the trainee under the supervision of senior claims professionals.
• Assist with triage of first notification of loss and the timely engagement of appropriate adjusters, engineers, counsel, and other service providers.
• Review policy wordings and claim information to identify potential coverage considerations and escalate issues for senior review.
• Assist with claim investigations, exposure assessments, reserve recommendations, and resolution planning within delegated authority and supervision requirements.
• Maintain accurate, timely, and complete claim files in accordance with AXIS policies, procedures, and service standards.
• Monitor claim activity, document next steps, follow up on outstanding information, and escalate material developments promptly.
• Work closely with clients, brokers, independent adjusters, engineers, external legal advisors, and other experts to help maintain a premier claims service.
• Engage with underwriters, actuaries, operations, and other internal stakeholders in relation to claims, reporting, and management information.
• Support the review and validation of indemnity and expense payments to help ensure accurate and timely processing.
• Develop a working knowledge of renewable energy technologies, relevant legal frameworks, policy coverage, and claims handling practices.
• Meet agreed expectations for claim quality, productivity, diary management, and claims handling cycle time.
• Continue professional development through formal training, coaching, licensing, and practical claims experience.
• Demonstrate the AXIS behaviors that support and align with AXIS values: People, Decisiveness, Excellence, and Stronger Together.
 
KEY SKILLS & ABILITIES:

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience preferred.
• One to three years of experience with a US insurer, broker, claims organization, renewable energy business, engineering firm, or related industry is preferred but not essential.
• Claims adjuster license preferred; willingness and ability to obtain and maintain licenses required by applicable states.
• Interest in commercial property, renewable energy, engineering, construction, or complex claims.
• Strong analytical, numerical, and solution-focused skills, with the ability to work accurately to deadlines.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present information clearly and concisely for the intended audience.
• Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
• Effective organization, planning, time management, and attention to detail.
• Ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively in a hybrid and self-directed environment.
• Proficiency with Excel, Word, and PowerPoint preferred; familiarity with Outlook, OneNote, and other Microsoft Office products is desirable.
• Integrity, professionalism, curiosity, willingness to learn, and a collaborative team approach.


For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of 60-90K. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is [Exempt/Non-Exempt] for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

Underwriter – Builder’s Risk

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

AXIS’ U.S. Construction team is seeking an underwriter with a focus on Builder’s Risk (Project and Master). This role will support the growth and profitability of our Builder’s Risk portfolio by underwriting new and renewal business, building broker and customer relationships, and developing technical expertise and supporting business development within the Construction team. This position can be based out of any of our Midwest or West Coast offices.

What will you do in this role?

  • Continue developing Builder's Risk expertise while building strong relationships with brokers and customers and contributing to underwriting, retention, and growth objectives across the portfolio.
  • Analyze and qualify opportunities based upon the organization’s appetite and be able to effectively communicate such.
  • Underwrite within the underwriting governance framework.
  • Evaluate, underwrite, and negotiate new and renewal business within delegated authority and underwriting guidelines while exercising sound underwriting judgment.
  • Develop and/or maintain relationships with our broker partners in support of desired business retention as well as work with our customers and brokers to identify their insurance needs and provide recommendations and possible solutions to achieve it where possible.
  • Support business development efforts through broker interactions and the identification of growth opportunities within assigned accounts and territories.
  • Manage assigned underwriting responsibilities and contribute to portfolio performance objectives in support of organizational goals.
  • Participate in industry functions and professional events to continue building market knowledge and representing AXIS professionally.
  • Participate in and help facilitate broker and customer meetings to strengthen relationships, identify opportunities, and support retention and growth objectives
  • Work collaboratively with colleagues across the organization to ensure our customer’s needs are met.

About You:

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table, so while there are some qualifications and experiences, we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge might lend itself to fulfilling this role and help us achieve our goals.

What you need to have:

  • 3 - 5 years of Builder’s Risk, Property, or Commercial Insurance underwriting experience.
  • Curiosity and desire to learn
  • Experience analyzing and underwriting a range of commercial property or Builder’s Risk exposures.
  • Solid understanding of Builder's Risk coverage, exposure analysis, pricing principles, and marketplace dynamics.
  • Able to analyze standard and moderately complex risks and communicate underwriting concepts or positions to audiences of varying experience.
  • Able to independently manage routine underwriting responsibilities while collaborating effectively in a team setting.
  • Capable of handling time constraints for quoting new and renewal business.

What we prefer you to have:

  • Understanding of both admitted (retail) and non-admitted / Excess & Surplus (wholesale) underwriting framework.
  • Experience collaborating with brokers and supporting relationship development within an assigned market or territory.
  • Creative problem-solving skills.
  • Reasonably proficient with Microsoft Office applications.

Role Factors:

In this role, you will typically be required to:

  • This will be a hybrid role with an expectation of being in an AXIS office 3 days per week (as applicable)
  • Travel roughly 25%
  • Participate on weekly team calls / meetings when operating in hybrid environments

What we offer:

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $130,000 - $165,000K. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

North America Casualty Treaty Reinsurance Underwriter


Job Family Grouping

AXIS Re - Underwriting

Job Family

AXIS Re - Underwriting | Underwriters

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

Reporting to the Head of North America General Casualty and Workers Compensation, AXIS Re, the successful candidate will underwrite and manage a portfolio of North American General Casualty and Workers Compensation Treaty Reinsurance business. The role will contribute to Business Unit profit goals, portfolio strategy, client and broker engagement, and disciplined cycle management across General Liability, Workers Compensation, Commercial Auto Liability, Umbrella/Excess Liability, and other casualty classes within the team's appetite.

What will you do in this role?

·   Originate, analyze, price, structure, negotiate, and underwrite North America general casualty and workers compensation treaty business in accordance with underwriting guidelines, portfolio appetite, allocated authority, and established best practices.

·   Manage assigned renewals and new-business opportunities across proportional and non-proportional treaty structures, including quota share, surplus share, working excess, and catastrophe or clash protections, as applicable.

·   Assess cedent strategy, management, underwriting controls, distribution, claims practices, reserving, rate adequacy, exposure trends, and historical performance to develop a clear underwriting view.

·   Partner with actuarial, claims, contract wording, finance, and legal colleagues to evaluate treaty economics, key assumptions, terms and conditions, and potential volatility.

·   Build and maintain strong relationships with reinsurance intermediaries and cedent clients to support profitable business origination, retention, and long-term strategic partnerships.

·   Contribute to casualty strategy and portfolio management, including appetite, guidelines, aggregate and limit management, concentration monitoring, and deployment of capacity.

·   Monitor market conditions and casualty loss drivers, including social inflation, litigation trends, legal and regulatory developments, medical inflation, loss-cost trends, and changes in underlying policy terms.

·   Prepare clear underwriting referrals, portfolio updates, and recommendations for senior leadership and governance forums.

·   Participate in cedent underwriting audits, claims reviews, stewardship meetings, and ongoing monitoring of account performance.

·   Maintain accurate and timely underwriting documentation, pricing records, exposure data, and internal system entries.

·   Travel to service clients, meet brokers, conduct audits, and attend industry conferences and market events.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities, and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.

About You

You are a hands-on casualty treaty underwriting professional with strong technical judgment and a record of building and managing a complex book of reinsurance business. You understand the treaty underwriting lifecycle, from submission review and portfolio analysis through pricing, structuring, negotiation, authorization, documentation, and post-bind monitoring. You bring professional presence, commercial judgment, and the ability to communicate, influence, and build relationships that add value to the AXIS Re portfolio and support longer-term strategic initiatives.

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge may help you succeed in this role and contribute to our goals.

What you need to have

·   Demonstrated casualty underwriting, reinsurance underwriting, broking, actuarial, or related experience with a strong understanding of North American casualty business.

·   Knowledge of General Casualty and Workers Compensation, with familiarity across Commercial Auto Liability, Umbrella/Excess Liability, General Liability and related casualty classes.

·   Working knowledge of actuarial and pricing concepts, including experience partnering with actuarial teams to evaluate and price reinsurance treaties.

·   Ability to assess exposure and experience data, loss development, rate and exposure change, limits, retentions, attachment points, and treaty economics.

·   Strong grasp of underlying policy forms, reinsurance contract wording, exclusions, claims issues, and the roles of claims, actuarial, legal, accounting, and finance in the underwriting process.

·   Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to audiences at all levels, including executive leadership.

·   Strong analytical, negotiation, marketing, and influencing skills, with sound judgment when faced with ambiguity or changing priorities.

·   Client-focused approach and flexibility in developing solutions that meet client needs while maintaining underwriting discipline.

·   Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple submissions, renewals, and peak-period workflows.

·   Highly collaborative and versatile, with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a cross-functional team.

·   Ability to initiate and independently lead defined projects and portfolio initiatives.

·   Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent industry experience.

What we prefer you to have

·   CPCU, ARe, ACAS, FCAS, ARM, or other relevant industry designation.

·   A minimum of five years of casualty insurance, reinsurance underwriting, actuarial, claims, or broking experience.

·   Experience underwriting or analyzing both proportional and non-proportional casualty treaty structures.

·   Established relationships with reinsurance brokers and North American casualty insurers.

·   Effective strategic relationship management and portfolio management skills.

·   Advanced Excel capability, including lookup functions, PivotTables, and analysis across multiple data sets.

·   Experience building dashboards or data models using Power BI.

·   Experience with AI Assistants a plus. 

·   Based in the New York City area or another approved AXIS office location.

Role Factors

·   Travel to visit clients and brokers, conduct underwriting audits, and attend industry conferences. 

·   Be in the office, or visiting brokers or clients, three days per week.

·   Attend broker and client events as required, including evenings and some weekend travel. 

What we offer

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $185,000 - $250,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors, including your specific experience and work location.

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate performance and your individual performance. You will also be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package that includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and more.

This role is exempt for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

Job Description: Technology and AI Strategy Lead


How does this role contribute to our collective success?

AXIS is undertaking a multi-year transformation to strengthen how we operate,

serve customers, and create competitive advantage. Technology and AI are important enablers of this transformation, creating opportunities to improve operational effectiveness, support business growth, and enhance customer outcomes.


The Technology & AI Strategy Lead is responsible for shaping, maintaining, and driving execution of the enterprise technology and AI agenda in partnership with business, technology, data, risk, and functional leaders. The role owns the integrated strategic agenda, enterprise-level recommendations, strategic coherence, value framework, and executive decision support. It does not own delivery of individual products or programs; delivery remains with the relevant business and technology owners, and business leaders remain accountable for outcomes, adoption, and benefit realization.


The role provides independent analysis, subject matter expertise, and strategic recommendations that help leadership evaluate technology and AI opportunities, risks, and trade-offs. Success requires strong business acumen, strategic thinking, stakeholder engagement, and the ability to translate complex technology concepts into practical business implications and measurable outcomes.
________________________________________

Key Responsibilities


Technology & AI Strategy


  • Support the development and refinement of the technology and AI strategy aligned with enterprise and business objectives.
  • Partner with business and functional leaders to identify opportunities where technology and AI can improve business performance, operational effectiveness, and customer outcomes.
  • Analyze emerging technology and AI trends, market developments, and vendor capabilities to inform strategic recommendations.
  • Assess opportunities to improve engineering effectiveness, delivery consistency, automation, and modernization efforts.
  • Consider responsible AI, data governance, cybersecurity, privacy, operational resilience, and regulatory requirements when developing recommendations and strategic assessments.

Portfolio Prioritization & Strategic Coherence

  • Support the development and maintenance of technology and AI roadmaps aligned to business objectives and transformation priorities.
  • Evaluate proposed initiatives and business cases against strategic goals, resource capacity, risk considerations, and organizational readiness.
  • Identify dependencies, opportunities for alignment, and potential conflicts across initiatives and programs.
  • Develop analysis and recommendations to support planning, prioritization, and investment discussions.
  • Contribute strategic insights that help leaders evaluate business needs, risks, costs, and expected value.

Execution Discipline & Value Realization

  • Develop and challenge value frameworks to evaluate expected business value and measure outcomes from technology and AI initiatives.
  • Analyze initiative progress, adoption trends, risks, and dependencies and provide insights to stakeholders, included any needed course corrections.
  • Identify lessons learned and opportunities to scale successful practices and capabilities.
  • Refresh the enterprise roadmap and investment recommendations based on delivery evidence, realized outcomes, emerging risks, and organizational learning.
  • Prepare strategic analyses, presentations, and recommendations for executive team.

Stakeholder Engagement & Change Enablement

  • Develop strategies to drive adoption of technology and AI-enabled capabilities across the enterprise.
  • Build collaborative relationships across business, technology, data, finance, risk, and transformation teams.
  • Facilitate workshops, planning sessions, and stakeholder discussions related to technology and AI priorities.
  • Develop clear, business-focused communications and presentations that help leaders understand strategic opportunities and implications.
  • Support initiatives that improve organizational understanding and adoption of technology and AI capabilities.
  • Identify barriers to adoption and recommend actions that support successful organizational change.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Support cross-functional strategic initiatives through influence, coordination, and collaboration.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor on technology and AI strategy-related matters.
  • Contribute subject matter expertise and analysis to governance and planning discussions.
  • Help stakeholders evaluate opportunities, risks, implementation considerations, and long-term implications of strategic initiatives.
    _______________________________________

About You

  • Significant experience in technology strategy, digital transformation, AI enablement, business transformation, management consulting, or a related field.
  • Strong understanding of technology, data, and AI concepts and their application to business problems.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze complex issues and develop practical, value-focused recommendations.
  • Experience evaluating business cases and connecting technology investments to business outcomes.
  • Strong analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving capabilities.
    Proven success influencing stakeholders and building alignment across matrixed organizations.
  • Excellent communication, facilitation, storytelling, and presentation skills, with experience engaging senior leaders.
  • Working knowledge of responsible AI, data governance, cybersecurity, privacy, operational resilience, and regulatory considerations.
  • Ability to balance strategic thinking with practical execution.
    Insurance, reinsurance, financial services, or other regulated-industry experience preferred.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required; advanced degree preferred.
    ________________________________________

Role Factors

  • Requires close partnership with business, technology, transformation, risk, and functional teams.
  • Success depends on expertise, influence, relationship building, strategic judgment, and the ability to navigate complex business challenges.
  • Regular participation in planning sessions, strategy reviews, governance forums, and leadership communications.
  • Operates within established enterprise governance frameworks and provides recommendations and guidance to support decision making.
  • Works independently on complex assignments requiring assessment of multiple business, technology, operational, and risk considerations.
  • Planning horizon is primarily annual and aligned with strategic planning and investment cycles.

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $250,000 to $275,000 (NY). Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 


In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  


Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Director, Talent Management & Workforce Readiness

Job Family Grouping: Human Resources

Job Family: Talent Development

Grade: F

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

This role designs and drives AXIS's talent management and workforce readiness agenda in partnership with HR and business leaders, ensuring the organization has the leadership, skills, capabilities, and talent required to deliver business priorities today and in the future. You will establish and continuously improve the frameworks, processes, and insights that support performance, talent, succession, and workforce decisions across the organization. This is a talent management role with a workforce readiness component; learning and development experience alone will not meet the requirements. Success will be measured through stronger leadership pipelines, improved workforce readiness, effective talent decisions, and the organization's ability to build the capabilities needed for future growth.


What will you do in this role?

·       You will design, drive, and continuously improve AXIS's core talent management processes, including goal setting, performance management, talent reviews, assessments, succession planning, and development planning. You will establish clear frameworks and governance that support high-quality talent decisions and stronger leadership pipelines.

·       You will drive workforce readiness efforts by helping the business understand the leadership, skills, capabilities, and talent needed to deliver future priorities. You will assess workforce gaps, use internal and external talent intelligence, and identify actions to build, buy, borrow, reskill, redeploy, or automate capabilities.

·       You will identify development needs and priorities through performance, talent, succession, assessment, and workforce planning insights. You will partner with the Head of Learning to ensure development programs and investments address the organization's most important leadership, skill, and capability gaps; this role does not own learning program design or delivery.

·       You will partner with business leaders, HR Business Partners, the COO organization, and transformation teams to assess the workforce impact of changes in business strategy, technology, AI, and how work gets done. You will translate those changes into clear recommendations for skills, roles, workforce planning, mobility, succession, and talent investments.

·       You will use talent data, workforce intelligence, assessments, and external market insights to identify risks and opportunities and provide practical recommendations to senior leaders. You will monitor the health and effectiveness of talent and workforce practices and use insights to improve them over time.

·       You will lead and develop the Talent Operations & HR Business Analyst, manage key external partners, and work across HR and the business to deliver priorities, strengthen manager capability, and drive adoption of talent management and workforce readiness practices.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.


About You:

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are some qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge could help you fulfil this role and contribute to our goals.


What you need to have:

·       10+ years of progressive HR experience, including at least 5 years of direct responsibility for designing, leading, or significantly evolving core talent management processes such as performance management, talent reviews, assessments, succession planning, and development planning at an enterprise or business-unit level.

·       2+ years of experience translating business strategy into future workforce, skills, or capability requirements through strategic workforce planning, skills strategy, organization transformation, workforce analytics, or a closely related discipline.

·       Demonstrated experience designing and implementing talent frameworks, governance, and processes across multiple businesses, functions, or geographies.

·       Demonstrated experience influencing senior leaders and using talent data, workforce intelligence, and business insights to support decisions.

·       Experience assessing complex talent and workforce issues, identifying risks and opportunities, and translating findings into clear recommendations and actions.

·       Experience leading enterprise-wide change, managing competing priorities, and driving adoption through HR Business Partners and people managers.

·       Experience leading and developing a team member, managing external partners, and collaborating effectively across HR and the business.

·       Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive talent, assessment, succession, and workforce information with discretion and sound judgment.


What we prefer you to have:

·       Direct experience with strategic workforce planning, skills-based workforce strategies, talent intelligence, or workforce transformation. Candidates are not expected to have equal depth in talent management and workforce planning, but must demonstrate credible experience across both.

·       Experience assessing how AI, automation, and evolving ways of working affect roles, skills, capacity, and talent needs.

·       Experience using Workday or similar technology to support talent and workforce processes.

·       Experience selecting, implementing, or governing assessment solutions that support talent and leadership decisions.

·       Experience in insurance, financial services, or another highly regulated global industry.

Role Factors:

In this role, you will typically be required to:

Be in the office 3 days per week

Travel domestically and internationally as business needs require


What we offer:

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $212,000 to 234,000 (NY/CT).

Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.  · You will lead and develop the Talent Operations & HR Business Analyst, manage key external partners, and work across HR and the business to deliver priorities, strengthen manager capability, and drive adoption of talent management and workforce readiness practices.

 · 2+ years of experience translating business strategy into future workforce, skills, or capability requirements through strategic workforce planning, skills strategy, organization transformation, workforce analytics, or a closely related discipline.
 · Demonstrated experience designing and implementing talent frameworks, governance, and processes across multiple businesses, functions, or geographies.
 · Demonstrated experience influencing senior leaders and using talent data, workforce intelligence, and business insights to support decisions.
 · Experience assessing complex talent and workforce issues, identifying risks and opportunities, and translating findings into clear recommendations and actions.

jobs.description_html:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

How does this role contribute to our collective success?
Data, analytics and AI are critical enablers of AXIS' strategic ambitions. The Head of Insights & Analytics – North America will lead the delivery of insights, analytics and AI solutions that support North American underwriting teams in making better, faster and more informed decisions.
This role is accountable for translating business priorities into impactful data products, analytics solutions and AI-enabled capabilities that improve underwriting performance, portfolio management, risk selection, operational efficiency and customer outcomes.
As the senior Insights & Analytics leader aligned to the North America business, you will act as a strategic partner to underwriting leadership, ensuring that data and AI investments are focused on measurable business value. You will also play a critical leadership role in delivering AI-enabled underwriting transformation initiatives, including oversight of the AI components of AXCEED and other key initiatives within the North American strategic portfolio.
You will serve as the primary interface between North American business stakeholders and the broader Data & Analytics organisation, ensuring that priorities are aligned, solutions are fit-for-purpose, and value is realised.

What will you do in this role?
Lead North America Insights & Analytics Delivery

  • Own the delivery and value realisation of the North America Insights & Analytics portfolio.
  • Act as the primary Data & Analytics partner to North American underwriting leadership teams.
  • Develop a deep understanding of underwriting strategy, operational challenges and growth objectives.
  • Translate business opportunities into actionable analytics, AI and data product initiatives.

Deliver Measurable Business Value

  • Ensure all initiatives are linked to clear business outcomes and success measures.
  • Drive adoption of analytics and AI solutions across underwriting teams.
  •  Champion evidence-based decision making through effective use of data and insights.

Lead AI and Advanced Analytics Solutions

  • Provide business leadership and oversight for AI-enabled underwriting initiatives.
  • Partner with Data Scientists, AI Engineers, Architects and Technology teams to industrialise and scale AI capabilities.
  • Ensure AI solutions are aligned to AXIS governance standards, risk appetite and responsible AI principles.
  • Promote practical and value-focused use of AI across the North America underwriting function.

Build Strong Business Partnerships

  • Establish trusted relationships with North America underwriting leaders and key stakeholders.
  • Act as a trusted advisor on insights, analytics, AI and data-driven decision making.
  • Facilitate alignment between business priorities and enterprise Data & Analytics strategy.

Lead and Develop High Performing Teams

  • Provide leadership to North America-aligned Insights & Analytics team members.
  • Create an environment that promotes collaboration, innovation, continuous improvement and accountability.
  • Develop team capability across insights, analytics and AI disciplines.
  • Foster knowledge sharing and reuse across the wider Insights & Analytics community.

Improve Ways of Working

  • Drive adoption of agile and product-oriented delivery practices.
  • Ensure solutions are scalable, sustainable and maintainable.
  • Promote reuse of data products, models and analytics capabilities.
  • Foster a culture of experimentation, learning and continuous improvement.

Success Measures
Success in this role will be measured through:

  • Business Impact
  • Demonstrable improvement in underwriting effectiveness, portfolio performance and operational efficiency resulting from delivered solutions.
  • Quantifiable business value generated through insights, analytics and AI initiatives.
  • Stakeholder Satisfaction
  • Strong business partner satisfaction and trust.
  • Insights and analytics capabilities becoming embedded within day-to-day underwriting decision making.
  • Portfolio Delivery
  • Successful execution of North America strategic portfolio commitments.
  • Delivery of agreed outcomes, benefits and value targets.
  • Team Performance
  • High levels of engagement, capability development and retention.
  • Strong collaboration across the wider Data & Analytics function.
  • Innovation and Modernisation
  • Increased adoption of AI-enabled capabilities.
  • Improved speed, quality and scalability of insights and analytics delivery.

About you:
We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table, so while there are some qualifications and experiences, we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge might lend itself to fulfilling this role and help us achieve our goals.
What you need to have:

Experience

  • Significant experience leading analytics, business intelligence, data science or AI teams. A minimum of 10 years’ experience in analytics, business intelligence, data science or AI, including at least 3 years leading teams within complex organisations.
  • Experience partnering closely with insurance underwriting or specialty insurance business functions. A minimum of 3 years’ experience in the insurance or reinsurance industry, partnering closely with underwriting or specialty insurance business functions.
  • Demonstrated success delivering business value through analytics and AI initiatives.
  • Experience leading at least two cross-functional transformation or strategic delivery programmes.
  • Proven record of influencing senior stakeholders and executive leadership teams.
  • Experience operating within agile delivery environments.
  • Experience directly managing a team of at least 6 people, including team leads or senior individual contributors.

Knowledge & Technical Expertise

  • Strong understanding of insights, analytics, data science, AI and data product delivery.
  • Knowledge of modern AI and machine learning capabilities, including generative AI applications.
  • Understanding of underwriting processes, portfolio management and insurance analytics.
  • Strong appreciation of responsible AI, governance and risk management principles.
  • Ability to identify the most appropriate solution for a business problem, whether traditional reporting, advanced analytics, predictive modelling or AI.

Leadership Capabilities

  • Strategic thinker with strong commercial acumen.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills.
  • Strong people leadership and coaching capability.
  • Ability to bring clarity and direction in complex environments.
  • Comfortable balancing strategic priorities with delivery execution.

What we prefer you to have:

  • At least 3 years’ experience in North American specialty or commercial insurance underwriting analytics.
  • Experience deploying AI or machine learning solutions into production in an underwriting or portfolio management context.
  • Education: An advanced degree in a relevant field (e.g., Data Science, Statistics, Business Analytics, Computer Science, or similar) is highly desirable, or equivalent professional experience.

Role Factors:
Be in the office 3 days per week

What we offer:
For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $180,000 to $200,000 (NY), Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.
In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.description_html:
